title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
天下有道則庶人不議
刁㟳
同考試官訓導楊　批〔寫出有道氣象宛然在目〕
同考試官教諭宋　批〔題本冠冕作者多襲陳言今〕
〔人厭觀求其化腐爲新快人心目者僅見此篇允宜前寘〕
考試官教諭張　批〔析理明白〕
考試官教諭李　批〔平順得旨〕
===
世際隆平之日民無非間之言盖民心之是非
顧上之政治何如耳天下有道則上無失政矣
民何間然之有哉昔聖人通論天下之勢及此
盖謂人君臨馭天下統理民物紀綱整肅四方
仰一統於無虞海宇昇平萬國戴一人之有慶
君出治而臣輔治自朝廷而方岳有穆穆明明
之休君出命而臣奉命自王國而萬邦有皇皇
師師之風禮樂大政掌握於一人之手而政無
多門也征伐大權綱維於朝廷之上而權無下
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
天下有道，則庶人不議。
刁㟳
同考試官訓導楊，批〔寫出有道氣象，宛然在目。〕
同考試官教諭宋，批〔題本冠冕，作者多襲陳言，今〕〔人厭觀。求其化腐爲新、快人心目者，僅見此篇，允宜前寘。〕
考試官教諭張，批〔析理明白。〕
考試官教諭李，批〔平順得旨。〕
世際隆平之日，民無非間之言。盖民心之是非，顧上之政治何如耳。天下有道，則上無失政矣，民何間然之有哉？昔聖人通論天下之勢，及此，盖謂人君臨馭天下，統理民物，紀綱整肅，四方仰一統於無虞；海宇昇平，萬國戴一人之有慶。君出治而臣輔治，自朝廷而方岳，有穆穆明明之休；君出命而臣奉命，自王國而萬邦，有皇皇師師之風。禮樂大政，掌握於一人之手，而政無多門也；征伐大權，綱維於朝廷之上，而權無下
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When the Way prevails under Heaven, the common people do not debate affairs of government.”
Diao Li 刁㟳

Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He depicts the scene of the Way prevailing so vividly that it seems to stand before our eyes.”
Associate Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently grand, but writers mostly repeat stale expressions that readers nowadays tire of seeing. In seeking a composition that transforms the stale into the fresh and delights the heart and eye, I have found only this essay. It certainly deserves a place near the front.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The analysis of principle is clear.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Smooth and fluent, it captures the intended meaning.”

When the age enjoys profound peace, the people utter no words of censure or criticism. For the judgments of right and wrong in the people’s hearts depend simply on the quality of government above. When the Way prevails under Heaven, those above commit no errors in governing. What, then, could the people find to criticize?

Long ago, when the Sage discussed the general condition of the realm, he touched upon this point. His meaning was that the ruler presides over all under Heaven and governs the people and all things. The guiding principles and regulations are orderly and strict; the four quarters look up to a unified rule free from danger. Peace flourishes throughout the realm, and the myriad states uphold the blessings enjoyed by the One Man. The ruler initiates governance, and his ministers assist him in governing: from the court to the regional authorities, there is the excellence of reverence and enlightened rule. The ruler issues commands, and his ministers carry them out: from the royal domain to the myriad states, there is a spirit of august dignity and mutual emulation. The great affairs of rites and music lie in the hands of the One Man, so that government does not issue from multiple sources. The great authority to undertake punitive expeditions is held firmly at court, so that authority does not pass down…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
移也天下有道如此但見生斯世也為斯民也
莫不慶王綱之丕振翕然同文同軌之天喜王
化之大同藹然遵道遵路之俗號令一布帖耳
聽命之恐後閭閻里巷無異心也何嘗有所私
議以非其上哉所以然者非箝其口也蓋上無
失政自不容於議耳政教一施心悅誠服之不
暇市井草莽無異志也何嘗有所私議以毀其
上哉所以爾者非捫其舌也蓋上無失政自無
事於議耳吁下無私議而由乎上無失政如此
===
為人君者可不強於自治以一斯民之心哉大
抵此章夫子雖通論天下之勢實所以為當時
發也蓋是時三家強公室弱君臣失道綱常淪
沒禮樂名分蕩然無復存矣故夫子歷論有道
而及無道之得失以見為君者不可無自治之
計為臣者不可萌僭竊之心其扶世立教挽今
返古之意藹然溢於言表矣
庸德之行庸言之謹有所不足不敢不勉
有餘不敢盡
punctuated:
移也。天下有道如此，但見生斯世也，為斯民也，莫不慶王綱之丕振，翕然同文同軌之天；喜王化之大同，藹然遵道遵路之俗。號令一布，帖耳聽命之恐後，閭閻里巷無異心也，何嘗有所私議以非其上哉？所以然者，非箝其口也，蓋上無失政，自不容於議耳。政教一施，心悅誠服之不暇，市井草莽無異志也，何嘗有所私議以毀其上哉？所以爾者，非捫其舌也，蓋上無失政，自無事於議耳。吁！下無私議，而由乎上無失政如此，為人君者，可不強於自治，以一斯民之心哉？大抵此章，夫子雖通論天下之勢，實所以為當時發也。蓋是時三家強，公室弱，君臣失道，綱常淪沒，禮樂名分蕩然無復存矣。故夫子歷論有道而及無道之得失，以見為君者不可無自治之計，為臣者不可萌僭竊之心。其扶世立教、挽今返古之意，藹然溢於言表矣。

庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉；有餘，不敢盡。
translation_en:
…does not shift downward. Such is the condition of the realm when the Way prevails. All who live in this age and belong to its people celebrate the great strengthening of royal order, united in a world of common writing and common carriage tracks. They rejoice in the universal reach of royal moral transformation, amid flourishing customs of following the Way and its paths. Once commands are proclaimed, they listen submissively, fearing only that they may be late in obeying. Throughout the residential quarters and lanes, none harbors a dissenting heart. When have they ever engaged in private criticism to find fault with their superiors? This is not because their mouths are gagged. Rather, those above commit no errors in government, naturally leaving no room for criticism. Once government and instruction are put into effect, people give themselves wholeheartedly to joyful and sincere submission. In marketplaces and the countryside, none harbors a dissenting purpose. When have they ever engaged in private criticism to disparage their superiors? This is not because their tongues are restrained. Rather, those above commit no errors in government, naturally leaving no occasion for criticism. Ah! Since the absence of private criticism below thus results from the absence of misgovernment above, how can a ruler fail to exert himself in ordering his own conduct and rule, thereby uniting the hearts of the people?

In this chapter, although the Master discusses the condition of the realm generally, his words were in fact prompted by his own times. At that time, the three great families were powerful and the ducal house was weak. Ruler and ministers had departed from the Way; the cardinal bonds and enduring norms had fallen into oblivion; rites, music, and the distinctions of title and status had been swept away, leaving nothing intact. Thus the Master discusses in turn the successes and failures of ages when the Way prevails and when it does not, showing that rulers must have a plan for ordering their own conduct and rule, and that ministers must not entertain intentions of usurpation. His purpose—to sustain the world and establish moral teaching, to turn the present back toward antiquity—is abundantly manifest beyond the words themselves.

In practicing ordinary virtues and exercising care in ordinary speech, where one falls short, one dares not fail to exert oneself; where one has a surplus, one dares not exhaust it.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
王崇獻
同考試官訓導李　批〔拈書出題此甚平易而佳〕
作獨少是篇詞潔理明宜在所取
同考試官教諭王　批〔認理精措詞當可取〕
考試官教諭張　批〔措詞雅健他作所不及〕
考試官教諭李　批〔詞不務而意自足佳作也〕
君子自脩於言行之常而益盡其功焉夫道不
遠人自脩之功所當盡也君子致勉乎此而言
行不已其功爲其不遠人以爲道也豈不於斯
===
而可見乎昔中庸是章論道不遠人至此而言
君子自責自脩之事葢謂道本不遠於人人自
有以遠乎道君子於此宜何如哉亦惟不遠人
以爲道耳彼其孝弟忠信之道乃日用常行之
理吾之所當然也行之不力則道於我乎遼邈
矣葢必以是道之責於人者于以自脩於庸德
之間躬行之允迪之而孝弟忠信必求踐乎其
實不苟焉以䟽行也言之不謹則道於我乎扞
格矣葢必以是道之責於彼者于以自脩於庸
punctuated:
王崇獻

同考試官訓導李批〔拈書出題，此甚平易，而佳〕作獨少。是篇詞潔理明，宜在所取。
同考試官教諭王批〔認理精，措詞當，可取〕
考試官教諭張批〔措詞雅健，他作所不及〕
考試官教諭李批〔詞不務而意自足，佳作也〕

君子自脩於言行之常，而益盡其功焉。夫道不遠人，自脩之功所當盡也。君子致勉乎此，而言行不已其功，爲其不遠人以爲道也，豈不於斯而可見乎？昔《中庸》是章論道不遠人，至此而言君子自責自脩之事。葢謂道本不遠於人，人自有以遠乎道。君子於此宜何如哉？亦惟不遠人以爲道耳。彼其孝弟忠信之道，乃日用常行之理，吾之所當然也。行之不力，則道於我乎遼邈矣。葢必以是道之責於人者，于以自脩於庸德之間，躬行之，允迪之，而孝弟忠信必求踐乎其實，不苟焉以䟽行也。言之不謹，則道於我乎扞格矣。葢必以是道之責於彼者，于以自脩於庸
translation_en:
Wang Chongxian 王崇獻

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The question is drawn from the book; it is quite straightforward, yet good〕 answers are particularly scarce. This essay is concise in expression and clear in reasoning; it should be among those selected.
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Precise in its grasp of principle and appropriate in its wording; worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Its elegant and vigorous wording surpasses that of the other essays.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is unlabored [?], yet the meaning is fully conveyed: a fine essay.〕

The gentleman cultivates himself in ordinary speech and conduct, and thereby brings his efforts ever closer to fulfillment. The Way is not far from people, and the work of self-cultivation must be carried through fully. The gentleman exerts himself in this, never ceasing his efforts in speech and conduct, because he practices the Way without departing from what is close to people. Is this not evident here? This chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the Way is not far from people; at this point it speaks of the gentleman’s holding himself accountable and cultivating himself. Its meaning is that the Way is inherently not far from people, but people themselves do things that distance them from the Way. What, then, should the gentleman do? Simply practice the Way without departing from what is close to people. The Way of filial piety, fraternal deference, loyalty, and trustworthiness consists of the principles of everyday conduct: what we ourselves ought to do. If I do not practice it vigorously, the Way becomes remote from me. I must therefore take what I require of others in accordance with this Way and apply it to cultivating myself in ordinary virtues, personally practicing it and faithfully following it. In filial piety, fraternal deference, loyalty, and trustworthiness, I must seek to realize their substance, rather than act carelessly and neglect their practice. If I am not careful in speech, a barrier arises between the Way and myself. I must therefore take what I require of others in accordance with this Way and apply it to cultivating myself in ordinary …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
言之際無易焉無苟焉而孝弟忠信務求擇乎
其可不泛焉以徒言也夫庸德之行雖云力矣
然力行難常失於不足使不足而不勉焉不幾
於行之不力乎又必於孝弟未能也而勉焉以
能之忠信未盡也而強焉以盡之行之弗篤弗
措也行之不益力哉庸言之發雖云謹矣然故
言易常至於有餘使有餘而不訒焉不幾於謹
之未至乎又必欲言夫孝弟也恥躬不逮則訒
之而不敢盡言夫忠信也恐未能行則訒之而
===
不敢發言之弗謹弗措也謹之不益至哉吁德
之行已力而益力言之謹已至而益至君子不
遠人以為道如此此道之所以不遠於人也歟
大抵道也者原於天命具於人心見於行事本
近而且易不待勉強而能也但人於道不求諸
近而求諸遠不求之易而求之難則反失其道
矣故夫子於此首言道不遠人而又歷論治人
愛人責己之道無非所以明道不遠人人不可
遠人以為道也子思子引之以明道之費隱其
punctuated: 言之際，無易焉，無苟焉，而孝弟忠信務求擇乎其可，不泛焉以徒言也。夫庸德之行雖云力矣，然力行難，常失於不足。使不足而不勉焉，不幾於行之不力乎？又必於孝弟未能也，而勉焉以能之；忠信未盡也，而強焉以盡之。行之弗篤弗措也，行之不益力哉？庸言之發雖云謹矣，然故言易，常至於有餘。使有餘而不訒焉，不幾於謹之未至乎？又必欲言夫孝弟也，恥躬不逮，則訒之而不敢盡；言夫忠信也，恐未能行，則訒之而不敢發。言之弗謹弗措也，謹之不益至哉？吁！德之行已力而益力，言之謹已至而益至，君子不遠人以為道如此，此道之所以不遠於人也歟！大抵道也者，原於天命，具於人心，見於行事，本近而且易，不待勉強而能也。但人於道，不求諸近而求諸遠，不求之易而求之難，則反失其道矣。故夫子於此首言道不遠人，而又歷論治人、愛人、責己之道，無非所以明道不遠人，人不可遠人以為道也。子思子引之以明道之費隱，其
translation_en:
…in everyday speech, allowing neither carelessness nor negligence, and, in speaking of filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness, striving to choose what is appropriate rather than indulging in empty generalities. Though one may exert oneself in practicing everyday virtues, vigorous practice is difficult and often falls short. If one falls short yet makes no further effort, does this not amount to insufficient exertion in practice? Thus, where one cannot yet fulfill filial devotion and fraternal respect, one must strive to become capable of doing so; where one has not fully realized loyalty and trustworthiness, one must exert oneself to realize them fully. One must not stop until one’s practice is earnest and steadfast. Will one’s exertion in practice not thereby increase? Though one may be careful in uttering everyday words, speaking is easy [?], and one often says too much. If one says too much yet does not restrain one’s speech, does this not amount to falling short in caution? Thus, when wishing to speak of filial devotion and fraternal respect, one must feel ashamed that one’s conduct does not measure up, and therefore hold back, not daring to say all one might. When speaking of loyalty and trustworthiness, one must fear being unable to put them into practice, and therefore hold back, not daring to utter the words. One must not stop until one’s speech is cautious. Will that caution not thereby become more complete?

Ah! Already diligent in practicing virtue, one becomes still more diligent; already thoroughly cautious in speech, one becomes still more cautious. Such is the gentleman’s refusal to depart from human beings in pursuing the Way. Is this not why the Way is never far from human beings? In general, the Way originates in Heaven’s mandate, is fully present in the human heart, and manifests itself in conduct. It is inherently near and easy, and can be practiced without forced exertion. Yet if people seek the Way in what is distant rather than near, and in what is difficult rather than easy, they instead lose the Way. Thus the Master here begins by saying that the Way is not far from human beings, and then discusses in turn the ways of governing others, loving others, and holding oneself accountable. All this serves to make clear that the Way is not far from human beings, and that people must not depart from human beings in pursuing it. Master Zisi quotes these words to illuminate the Way’s pervasive operation and hidden subtlety; his…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
示人體道之功何其深切而著明哉
多助之至天下順之
杜珏
同考試官教諭邵　批　此題作者多不知天下順之即多助之至往往岐而二之惟此篇一破便見題意且終篇文彩燁然堪
式後學
考試官教諭張　批　語皆平實可錄
考試官訓諭李　批　說出孟子立言之意
===
大賢論人和之極而天下無不歸焉蓋天下之
心未易得也今多助之至而天下歸心如此非
得道之君其何以致之哉吾想孟子因論天時
地利之不如人和而推言及此謂夫民心向背
而國之治亂係焉政治得失而民之從違關焉
善圖治者亦惟得道以得人心焉耳誠能發號
施令而巨細必得其道由是庶民小于而遠邇
自罔不服殆必丕應徯志幡然起夫助我之念
心悅誠服翕然興夫助我之心助不徒助而
有以極其多焉多不徒多多而有以極其至焉
punctuated:
示人體道之功，何其深切而著明哉！

多助之至，天下順之。
杜珏

同考試官教諭邵批：此題作者多不知「天下順之」即「多助之至」，往往岐而二之。惟此篇一破便見題意，且終篇文彩燁然，堪式後學。
考試官教諭張批：語皆平實，可錄。
考試官訓諭李批：說出孟子立言之意。

大賢論人和之極，而天下無不歸焉。蓋天下之心未易得也，今多助之至，而天下歸心如此，非得道之君，其何以致之哉？吾想孟子因論天時、地利之不如人和，而推言及此，謂夫民心向背，而國之治亂係焉；政治得失，而民之從違關焉。善圖治者，亦惟得道以得人心焉耳。誠能發號施令，而巨細必得其道，由是庶民小于，而遠邇自罔不服，殆必丕應徯志，幡然起夫助我之念；心悅誠服，翕然興夫助我之心。助不徒助，而有以極其多焉；多不徒多多，而有以極其至焉。
translation_en:
…how profound, incisive, and clear is its instruction in the work of embodying the Way!

“At the utmost extent of abundant support, all under Heaven submit to him.”
Du Jue

Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: Most who write on this topic fail to understand that “all under Heaven submit to him” is precisely “the utmost extent of abundant support.” They often separate these into two distinct things. This essay alone reveals the meaning of the topic in its opening statement, and its literary brilliance shines throughout. It can serve as a model for later students.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: The language is consistently straightforward and sound; the essay merits inclusion.

Examiner Li, Instructor [?], comments: It brings out Mencius’s intention in making this statement.

The great worthy discusses the ultimate degree of harmony among people, at which none under Heaven fail to give their allegiance. The hearts of all under Heaven are not easily won. Yet here, when abundant support reaches its utmost extent, all under Heaven give their hearts in this way. How could anyone but a ruler who has attained the Way bring this about? I imagine that Mencius, in discussing how favorable timing bestowed by Heaven and advantageous terrain are inferior to harmony among people, extended his argument to this point. He meant that a state’s order or disorder depends on whether the people’s hearts turn toward or away from it, and that the people’s obedience or resistance hinges on the successes and failures of government. Those skilled in seeking good government need only attain the Way in order to win the people’s hearts.

If a ruler can truly issue commands and promulgate orders so that every matter, great or small, accords with the Way, then the common people and lesser persons [?], near and far, will naturally all submit. Surely they will respond in great numbers and await the fulfillment of their aspirations, promptly conceiving the thought of supporting me; pleased in heart and sincerely convinced, they will unite in the desire to support me. Such support is not merely support: it reaches the fullest abundance. Nor is this abundance merely abundance [the transcription repeats “abundant”]: it reaches its utmost extent.…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
然多助之至何如彼其蹙率土而東焉以西天
下如彼其大也望雲霓而來順者濟濟乎惟恐
吾之或後環天下而南焉以北疆域如彼其廣
也避水火而來歸者祁祁乎惟恐人之或先不
必封疆是界歸之者合天下而一心無離德也
多助之至何如哉不必山谿是險順之者磬率
土而一志無叛心也多助之至何若哉是則得
道多助而天下皆歸如此人和無以加矣戰必
無不勝矣尚何天時地利之足恃哉大抵戰國
===
之時聖賢道否功利日滋用兵者往往以天時
地利為務而不知得道以為之本徒事乎小而
不務乎大齊其末而不揣其本末足以言善治
者也故孟子於此發為天時地利不如人和之
論至此又以得道為人和之本使當時國君果
能得道以得人心則地利之險人為之守天時
之善人為之乘有所不戰戰必勝矣惜乎終不
能聽徒使孟子託之空言也可慨已夫
易
punctuated:
然多助之至何如？彼其蹙率土而東焉以西，天下如彼其大也，望雲霓而來順者濟濟乎，惟恐吾之或後；環天下而南焉以北，疆域如彼其廣也，避水火而來歸者祁祁乎，惟恐人之或先。不必封疆是界，歸之者合天下而一心，無離德也，多助之至何如哉！不必山谿是險，順之者磬率土而一志，無叛心也，多助之至何若哉！是則得道多助，而天下皆歸如此，人和無以加矣，戰必無不勝矣，尚何天時地利之足恃哉！大抵戰國之時，聖賢道否，功利日滋，用兵者往往以天時地利為務，而不知得道以為之本，徒事乎小而不務乎大，齊其末而不揣其本，末足以言善治者也。故孟子於此發為天時地利不如人和之論，至此又以得道為人和之本。使當時國君果能得道以得人心，則地利之險，人為之守；天時之善，人為之乘。有所不戰，戰必勝矣。惜乎終不能聽，徒使孟子託之空言也，可慨已夫！

易
translation_en:
But what is it like when abundant support reaches its utmost extent? Throughout all the land [?], from east to west, vast as the world is, those who come to submit—as people look eagerly for clouds and a rainbow promising rain—arrive in multitudes, each fearing only that he himself may fall behind. Throughout the world, from south to north, broad as its territories are, those who come to give their allegiance, escaping flood and fire, arrive in throngs, each fearing only that others may precede him. There is no need to rely on territorial boundaries to keep them within: those who give their allegiance unite the whole world in a single purpose, with none estranged in loyalty. Such is the utmost abundance of support! There is no need to rely on mountains and ravines as defenses: those who submit embrace all the land [?] in a single resolve, with no thought of rebellion. Such is the utmost abundance of support! Thus, one who attains the Way gains abundant support, and the whole world gives its allegiance in this manner. Harmony among the people could be no greater; in battle, victory would invariably follow. What grounds remain for relying on favorable timing and advantageous terrain?

Generally speaking, during the Warring States period, the Way of the sages and worthies was obstructed, while the pursuit of achievement and profit grew daily. Those who employed armies often devoted themselves to favorable timing and advantageous terrain, without understanding that attaining the Way should be their foundation. They attended only to minor matters and neglected the great ones, putting the branches in order without examining the root. This was insufficient [?] to warrant calling them good rulers. Thus Mencius advanced here his argument that favorable timing and advantageous terrain do not equal harmony among the people; at this point he further made attainment of the Way the foundation of that harmony. Had the rulers of his time truly been able to attain the Way and thereby win the people's hearts, the people would have defended their advantageous terrain and exploited favorable timing for them. They might refrain from battle, but whenever they fought, they would certainly win. Alas, in the end they could not heed him, leaving Mencius to commit his teaching to words without practical effect. How lamentable!

Book of Changes

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
上下交而其志同也
杜玨
同考試官教諭邵　批　近時學易者多以小見臆說迎合上意而於聖人贊易意義漫不究心獨此篇筆力高古句法
不詭於理豈用心於經學而不為俗所變者耶
考試官教諭張　批　易義潔淨
考試官教諭李　批　充蔚可觀
君臣相際而心同此所以為泰也蓋心同則道
同而治功可成此君臣相際一至於此則人事
===
之泰為何如哉昔伏羲以泰名卦文王以小往
大来吉亨繫辭吾夫子傳彖申明之意謂乾本
在上而居下猶君上之下交於臣也坤本在下
而居上猶臣下之上交於君也上交於下則是
為君者不以崇高富貴自恃惟以尊德樂道為
心以貴下賤三接之禮隆也用上敬下三錫之
命重也殆猶天道下濟而光明焉下交於上則
是為臣者不以隱居獨善自高惟以行義達道
為事自內比外攄利見之誠也用下敬上致匪
punctuated:
上下交而其志同也。
杜玨
同考試官教諭邵批：近時學易者，多以小見臆說迎合上意，而於聖人贊易意義，漫不究心。獨此篇筆力高古，句法不詭於理，豈用心於經學而不為俗所變者耶？
考試官教諭張批：易義潔淨。
考試官教諭李批：充蔚可觀。
君臣相際而心同，此所以為泰也。蓋心同則道同，而治功可成。此君臣相際，一至於此，則人事之泰為何如哉！昔伏羲以泰名卦，文王以「小往大来，吉亨」繫辭。吾夫子傳彖，申明之，意謂乾本在上而居下，猶君上之下交於臣也；坤本在下而居上，猶臣下之上交於君也。上交於下，則是為君者不以崇高富貴自恃，惟以尊德樂道為心。以貴下賤，三接之禮隆也；用上敬下，三錫之命重也。殆猶天道下濟而光明焉。下交於上，則是為臣者不以隱居獨善自高，惟以行義達道為事。自內比外，攄利見之誠也；用下敬上，致匪
translation_en:
“Those above and those below enter into communion, and their aspirations are the same.”
Du Jue 杜玨
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: “Recently, many who study the Book of Changes have catered to the wishes of their superiors with narrow views and speculative explanations, giving no serious thought to the meaning of the Sage’s elucidation of the Changes. This essay alone displays an elevated, classically informed literary force, and its phrasing does not depart from principle. Could its author be someone who applies himself to classical learning without being changed by prevailing fashions?”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The interpretation of the Changes is clear and pure.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Rich and flourishing, it merits admiration.”
When ruler and ministers enter into relations with one another and are of one mind, this is what constitutes Peace (Tai). For when their minds are one, their Way is one, and achievements in government can be realized. Once relations between ruler and ministers reach this point, how great must be the peace of human affairs!
Long ago, Fuxi named the hexagram Peace, and King Wen appended the words, “The small departs and the great comes: auspiciousness and success.” Our Master Confucius further explained this in his Commentary on the Judgment. His meaning was that Qian, Heaven, originally belongs above yet occupies the lower position, just as the ruler reaches downward to commune with his ministers. Kun, Earth, originally belongs below yet occupies the upper position, just as ministers reach upward to commune with their ruler.
When those above commune with those below, the ruler does not rely upon his exalted station, wealth, and honor, but sets his heart solely upon honoring virtue and delighting in the Way. In his noble position he condescends to those of humble station: magnificent is the courtesy of granting three audiences. From his superior position he shows respect to those below: weighty are the commands conferring three rewards. This is indeed like the Way of Heaven, which descends to bestow its benefits and shines brightly.
When those below commune with those above, ministers do not pride themselves on living in seclusion and cultivating their own goodness alone, but devote themselves solely to practicing righteousness and putting the Way into effect. From within they ally themselves with those without, expressing their sincerity in seeking the beneficial encounter with the great man. From their subordinate position they show respect to those above, displaying a devotion that is not …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
躬之節也殆猶地道卑而上行焉夫上下之交
如此吾知叅贊天地阜安民物以立不世之功
者固君之志也而臣之所願欲者亦不外是則
都俞於廟堂之上有孚攣如其利斷金也豈睽
之遇主于巷乎黼黻皇猷琺琿治化以建非常
之業者固臣之志也而君之所好尚者亦不出
此則賡歌於殿陛之間厥孚交如其臭如蘭也
豈坎之納約自牖乎是則際明良之嘉會成治
世之宏圖猗歟盛哉大抵君臣相遇非偶然者
===
要皆氣數之盛以致之也故孔子傳泰卦之彖
而以君臣際會為言則義文名卦繫辭之旨藹
然於言意之表而以見易之關於天下治道者
非淺淺也豈直為象數之書乎此又學易者所
當致意焉
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也
夏廷芝
同考試官教諭邵　批〔題本平易作者多牽强支入講草率可厭此篇體認明白辭氣老健而一結尤有精采宜〕
punctuated:
躬之節也，殆猶地道卑而上行焉。夫上下之交如此，吾知叅贊天地、阜安民物以立不世之功者，固君之志也，而臣之所願欲者亦不外是。則都俞於廟堂之上，有孚攣如，其利斷金也，豈睽之遇主于巷乎？黼黻皇猷、琺琿治化以建非常之業者，固臣之志也，而君之所好尚者亦不出此。則賡歌於殿陛之間，厥孚交如，其臭如蘭也，豈坎之納約自牖乎？是則際明良之嘉會，成治世之宏圖，猗歟盛哉！大抵君臣相遇，非偶然者，要皆氣數之盛以致之也。故孔子傳泰卦之彖，而以君臣際會為言，則義文名卦繫辭之旨，藹然於言意之表，而以見《易》之關於天下治道者非淺淺也，豈直為象數之書乎？此又學《易》者所當致意焉。
夫《易》，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。
夏廷芝
同考試官教諭邵，批〔題本平易，作者多牽强支入，講草率可厭。此篇體認明白，辭氣老健，而一結尤有精采，宜〕
translation_en:
…the integrity of selfless service, much as the way of earth is lowly yet moves upward. When intercourse between those above and those below is like this, I know that assisting Heaven and Earth, bringing prosperity and peace to the people and all things, and thereby establishing achievements unmatched in their age are indeed the ruler’s aspirations; what his ministers desire goes no further than this. Then, in their approving exchanges in the court, they are bound together by sincerity, and their sharpness can cut through metal. How could this be merely what the hexagram Opposition describes as “meeting one’s lord in a narrow lane”? To embellish the imperial plans and adorn [?] the civilizing work of government, thereby establishing extraordinary accomplishments, is indeed the ministers’ aspiration; what the ruler esteems likewise goes no further than this. Then, as they answer one another in song amid the palace halls and steps, their sincerity flows between them, and their fragrance is like orchids. How could this be merely what the hexagram The Abysmal describes as “presenting simple offerings through the window”? Thus an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers enjoy an auspicious encounter and accomplish the grand design of a well-governed age. Ah, how glorious!
Generally speaking, the meeting of ruler and ministers is no chance occurrence: it is brought about by the flourishing of cosmic forces and their allotted cycles. Thus, when Confucius commented on the Judgment of the hexagram Peace and spoke of the encounter between ruler and ministers, the intentions of Fu Xi and King Wen [?] in naming the hexagram and appending its statements became abundantly apparent beyond the words and their immediate meaning. This shows that the Changes has no superficial connection with the way of governing the world. Could it be merely a book of images and numbers? This, too, is something to which students of the Changes should give thought.
“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient workings of things.”
Xia Tingzhi.
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic itself is straightforward, but writers often force their interpretations and introduce extraneous material [?]; their exposition is careless and tiresome. This piece shows clear understanding, and its language and tone are mature and vigorous. Its conclusion is especially brilliant. It deserves…〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
得之寧不歆羨
考試官教諭張　批〔說理之文自合如此〕
考試官教諭李　批〔講極研字不類泛作〕
論易之為書乃聖人所以闡夫理之妙焉蓋理
莫妙於深與幾也然非聖人之作易其孰能極
之研之也哉昔大傳論易有聖人之道四焉至
此謂夫易有辭也有占也而辭占為天下之至
精易有象也有變也而象變為天下之至變易
之為書如此果何為者哉彼如幽明之故死生
===
之說與夫鬼神屈信之機皆理之至深而難測
者也易之辭占莫不推而極之焉蓋必不假乎
料想臆度之私有以究竟其本原發用之輿殆
猶鑑之空而毫髮畢照也若然則理之深者在
易而通志之體立矣易非聖人之所以極深者
乎如吉凶之未至悔吝之將萌與夫失得憂虞
之象皆理之至幾而難見者也易之象變莫不
研而審之焉蓋必無事乎讖緯術數之學有以
詳察其端倪眹兆之微殆猶衡之平而錙銖不
punctuated:
得之，寧不歆羨？
考試官教諭張，批〔說理之文，自合如此。〕
考試官教諭李，批〔講極研字，不類泛作。〕
論易之為書，乃聖人所以闡夫理之妙焉。蓋理莫妙於深與幾也，然非聖人之作易，其孰能極之研之也哉？昔大傳論易，有聖人之道四焉。至此謂夫易有辭也，有占也，而辭占為天下之至精；易有象也，有變也，而象變為天下之至變。易之為書如此，果何為者哉？彼如幽明之故、死生之說，與夫鬼神屈信之機，皆理之至深而難測者也。易之辭占，莫不推而極之焉。蓋必不假乎料想臆度之私，有以究竟其本原發用之輿，殆猶鑑之空而毫髮畢照也。若然，則理之深者在易，而通志之體立矣。易非聖人之所以極深者乎？如吉凶之未至、悔吝之將萌，與夫失得憂虞之象，皆理之至幾而難見者也。易之象變，莫不研而審之焉。蓋必無事乎讖緯術數之學，有以詳察其端倪眹兆之微，殆猶衡之平而錙銖不
translation_en:
…to obtain it—how could one not admire and envy it?
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Writing that elucidates principle should indeed be like this.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔It explicates the words “fathom” and “investigate,” unlike a merely conventional composition.〕
I submit that the Book of Changes is the means by which the sages elucidate the subtleties of principle. Nothing in principle is subtler than its depths and its incipient movements. Yet had the sages not composed the Changes, who could have fathomed those depths and investigated those beginnings? The Great Commentary, discussing the Changes, earlier identified four ways of the sages within it. Here it says that the Changes has statements and prognostications, and these constitute the utmost refinement under Heaven; it has images and transformations, and these constitute the utmost change under Heaven. Such being the Changes as a book, what purpose does it serve?
Consider the causes underlying the hidden and the manifest, the explanations of death and life, and the workings of the withdrawal and expansion of ghosts and spirits: these are the deepest and most unfathomable aspects of principle. The statements and prognostications of the Changes pursue and fathom them all. They assuredly do not rely on private conjecture and speculation, but provide the means to investigate fully their ultimate sources and the unfolding of their operation [?]. It is rather like an unclouded mirror in which even the finest hair is reflected. If so, the depths of principle reside in the Changes, and the foundation for comprehending intentions is established. Is the Changes not the means by which the sages fathom the depths?
Consider good and ill fortune before they arrive, remorse and humiliation as they begin to emerge, and the signs of loss and gain, anxiety and apprehension: these are the most incipient and least perceptible aspects of principle. The images and transformations of the Changes investigate and scrutinize them all. They assuredly have no need of the learning of prophetic texts, apocryphal writings, or divinatory techniques, but provide the means to examine closely the subtlety of their beginnings and portentous signs. It is rather like a level balance on which even the smallest weights do not…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
爽也若然則理之幾者在易而成務之體具矣
易非聖人之所以研幾者乎是則辭占象變信
乎爲聖人之道而人之所當尚者歟抑嘗論之
人惟心之精斯能極深以通志人惟心之變斯
能研幾以成務然則易之精變即聖人之心虛
靈也而其所極之深所研之幾即聖人心中所
具之理也是則易乃無言之聖人聖人乃有言
之易而此章首尾皆曰易有聖人之道良有以
夫
===
書
惟暨乃僚罔不同心以匡乃辟
王崇獻
同考試官訓導李　批　商書篇搨中作者類能
言之但浮詞可厭獨此篇甚明意足且寫出高宗重望傅說之
意殆盡異日出爲
世用其必有以仰體
君上之心者矣
同考試官教諭王　批　本題作者率多冗雜舛理惟
punctuated:
爽也。若然，則理之幾者在易，而成務之體具矣。易非聖人之所以研幾者乎？是則辭占象變，信乎爲聖人之道，而人之所當尚者歟！抑嘗論之：人惟心之精，斯能極深以通志；人惟心之變，斯能研幾以成務。然則易之精變，即聖人之心虛靈也；而其所極之深、所研之幾，即聖人心中所具之理也。是則易乃無言之聖人，聖人乃有言之易，而此章首尾皆曰「易有聖人之道」，良有以夫！

書
「惟暨乃僚，罔不同心以匡乃辟。」
王崇獻

同考試官訓導李批：商書篇搨中，作者類能言之，但浮詞可厭。獨此篇甚明意足，且寫出高宗重望傅說之意殆盡。異日出爲世用，其必有以仰體君上之心者矣。

同考試官教諭王批：本題作者率多冗雜舛理，惟
translation_en:
…without the slightest discrepancy. If so, the incipient workings of principle reside in the Changes, and the essential basis for accomplishing affairs is fully present. Is the Changes not therefore the means by which the sage investigates these incipient workings? Thus its statements, prognostications, images, and transformations are indeed the way of the sage, which people ought to esteem!

Yet I have reflected on this: only through the refinement of the mind can one plumb the depths and comprehend purposes; only through the mind’s capacity for change can one investigate incipient workings and accomplish affairs. Thus the refinement and transformation of the Changes are precisely the emptiness and spiritual responsiveness of the sage’s mind. The depths it plumbs and the incipient workings it investigates are precisely the principles inherent in that mind. The Changes is therefore a sage without speech, and the sage is the Changes endowed with speech. There is good reason indeed that both the beginning and the end of this chapter state: “The Changes contains the way of the sage.”

Documents
“You and your colleagues must all be of one mind in setting your sovereign right.”
Wang Chongxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Among the essays on the Documents of Shang [?], the writers generally manage to discuss the subject, but their empty rhetoric is tiresome. This essay alone is exceptionally clear and fully expresses its meaning. Moreover, it conveys almost exhaustively the weight of Gaozong’s expectations of Fu Yue. When its author later enters public service, he will surely be able to appreciate and give effect to his sovereign’s intentions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Those writing on this topic are mostly verbose and confused, and go astray in their reasoning. Only…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
是篇綠詞老健說理詳明蓋嘗究心於壁經而得其妙者歟錄之
考試官教諭張　批〔深得命相之旨〕
考試官教諭李　批〔理明詞順〕
協人已之心而盡輔弼之道此賢王之望大臣
也蓋一已聰明有限而衆人聞見無窮大臣之
責必合衆人之心以輔君焉昔高宗命說之意
若曰以已事君固相職之當然以人事君尤相
職之當盡彼納誨輔德我之望於爾者固切矣
然爾之下有卿士焉皆共天位而食天祿者誰
===
無輔君之心乎啓心沃心我之資於汝者固至
矣然爾之下有衆職焉皆治天民而理天事者
孰無正君之責乎汝必倡而導之使職之大者
此心職之小者此心而臣救其君之失合大小
而同符不判其心於爾我也統而率之使職之
尊者此志職之卑者此志而弼正其君之非合
尊卑而一致不隔其心於形骸也彬彬乎各操
夫堯舜其君之心務使君之德純一不二足以
匹休先世而表正乎萬邦焉濟濟乎各秉夫左
punctuated:
是篇綠詞老健，說理詳明，蓋嘗究心於壁經而得其妙者歟？錄之。
考試官教諭張批〔深得命相之旨〕。
考試官教諭李批〔理明詞順〕。
協人已之心而盡輔弼之道，此賢王之望大臣也。蓋一已聰明有限，而衆人聞見無窮，大臣之責必合衆人之心以輔君焉。昔高宗命說之意若曰：「以已事君，固相職之當然；以人事君，尤相職之當盡。彼納誨輔德，我之望於爾者固切矣。然爾之下有卿士焉，皆共天位而食天祿者，誰無輔君之心乎？啓心沃心，我之資於汝者固至矣。然爾之下有衆職焉，皆治天民而理天事者，孰無正君之責乎？汝必倡而導之，使職之大者此心，職之小者此心，而臣救其君之失，合大小而同符，不判其心於爾我也；統而率之，使職之尊者此志，職之卑者此志，而弼正其君之非，合尊卑而一致，不隔其心於形骸也。彬彬乎，各操夫堯舜其君之心，務使君之德純一不二，足以匹休先世而表正乎萬邦焉；濟濟乎，各秉夫左
translation_en:
…this essay’s wording [?] is mature and vigorous, and its exposition of principle detailed and clear. Surely its author has devoted himself to the classic recovered from within a wall and grasped its subtleties? It is selected for inclusion.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔It profoundly grasps the intent behind appointing a chief minister.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The reasoning is clear and the language flows smoothly.〕
To harmonize others’ minds with one’s own and fully discharge the duty of assisting the ruler: this is what a worthy king expects of his great ministers. One person’s intelligence is limited, whereas what the multitude have heard and seen is inexhaustible. A great minister’s responsibility therefore requires him to unite the minds of all in assisting the ruler. The intent of Gaozong’s charge to Yue was as though he said:
“To serve the ruler through your own efforts is certainly a chief minister’s proper duty; to serve the ruler through others is especially a duty that a chief minister must fulfill. My expectation that you offer instruction and assist my virtue is indeed earnest. Yet beneath you are high ministers and officers, all sharing Heaven’s offices and receiving Heaven’s emoluments. Who among them lacks the desire to assist the ruler? I rely on you most fully to open and nourish my mind. Yet beneath you are the holders of the many offices, all governing Heaven’s people and managing Heaven’s affairs. Who among them lacks the responsibility to rectify the ruler?
“You must take the initiative and guide them, so that those whose offices are great and those whose offices are small share this same purpose. Thus, as ministers remedy their ruler’s failings, great and small will act in accord, without dividing their minds into yours and mine. You must unite and lead them, so that those whose offices are exalted and those whose offices are humble share this same resolve. Thus, as they assist and correct their ruler’s errors, exalted and humble will act as one, without allowing their separate bodily existence to divide their minds. With cultivated refinement, let each cherish the desire to make his ruler a Yao or a Shun, striving to make the ruler’s virtue pure and undivided, sufficient to match the glory of earlier generations and set an upright example for the myriad states. In dignified concord, let each hold fast to the resolve to assist …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
右嚴辟之志務使君之心至誠無僞足以追配
前人而作則乎天下焉夫如是則能合衆人之
善以成輔君之功何患相業有不盡哉抑論之
泰山不辭土壤故能成其大河海不擇細流故
能成其深人君不資衆善何以成其德乎高宗
有見於此故拳拳於說言之下文說復之曰后
從諫則聖臣不命其承有以見高宗之心惟恐
進諫之不多傅說之意惟恐從諫之不切君明
臣良更相戒飭此高宗所以爲商令王而無愧
於湯傅說所以爲商賢佐而無愧於尹也歟
爾克敬典在德時乃罔不變允升于大猷
張諾
同考試官訓導李　批〔此作以身教立說深得成王〕
===
〔命君陳端本化敎之意且文有典則氣也雄渾其東魯之佳〕
〔士也高薦何忝〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔體認真切發揮詳盡風簷〕
〔寸晷之下能有此作非素於講貫而有得者不能本房優〕
〔選舍子其誰〕
punctuated:
右嚴辟之志，務使君之心至誠無僞，足以追配前人而作則乎天下焉。夫如是，則能合衆人之善，以成輔君之功，何患相業有不盡哉？抑論之，泰山不辭土壤，故能成其大；河海不擇細流，故能成其深。人君不資衆善，何以成其德乎？高宗有見於此，故拳拳於說。言之下文，說復之曰：「后從諫則聖，臣不命其承。」有以見高宗之心惟恐進諫之不多，傅說之意惟恐從諫之不切。君明臣良，更相戒飭，此高宗所以爲商令王而無愧於湯，傅說所以爲商賢佐而無愧於尹也歟！

爾克敬典在德，時乃罔不變，允升于大猷。
張諾

同考試官訓導李，批〔此作以身教立說，深得成王〕〔命君陳端本化敎之意。且文有典則，氣也雄渾，其東魯之佳〕〔士也。高薦何忝！〕

同考試官教諭王，批〔體認真切，發揮詳盡。風簷〕〔寸晷之下，能有此作，非素於講貫而有得者不能。本房優〕〔選，舍子其誰？〕
translation_en:
…the resolve to assist and revere their sovereign, striving to make his heart utterly sincere and free of falsehood, sufficient to equal his predecessors and serve as a model for all under Heaven. In this way, one can unite the goodness of all to accomplish the work of assisting the ruler. Why then worry that any part of a chief minister’s work might remain unfulfilled? To discuss it further: Mount Tai does not reject soil, and thus achieves its greatness; rivers and seas do not discriminate against small streams, and thus achieve their depth. If a ruler does not draw upon the goodness of all, how can he perfect his virtue? Gaozong understood this and therefore earnestly exhorted Yue. In the passage that follows these words, Yue replied: “When the sovereign follows remonstrance, he becomes a sage; his servants carry out his wishes without awaiting commands.” This shows that Gaozong feared only that too little remonstrance would be offered, while Fu Yue feared only that the ruler would not follow it wholeheartedly. An enlightened ruler and a worthy minister admonished one another in turn. Was this not why Gaozong became an excellent king of Shang, worthy of Tang, and Fu Yue became a worthy assistant of Shang, worthy of Yi Yin?

“If you can reverently uphold the constant norms and ground yourself in virtue, then none will fail to change, and they will truly advance along the great Way.”
Zhang Nuo

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This composition bases its argument on teaching by personal example and deeply grasps King Cheng’s intention in commanding Jun Chen to put the foundation in order and transform the people through instruction. Moreover, its writing has classical standards, and its force is vigorous and full. He is an outstanding scholar of eastern Lu. How could recommending him highly be undeserved?”

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “His understanding is genuine and precise, and his exposition thorough. To produce such a composition beneath the wind-swept eaves, in the brief time allotted, would be impossible for anyone who had not gained understanding through sustained study and discussion. For the premier selection from this examining section, whom could we choose but you?”

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張　批〔得經義程度〕
考試官教諭李　批〔深合題意〕
惟大臣能謹其身教則有以化乎民而善乎俗
矣蓋民之於上固不從其令而從其好大臣能
謹其所好而以身為教焉則民之化俗之善有
出於必然者矣昔成王命君陳往治東郊而言
及乎此謂夫訓告之切孰若身教之難忘誦說
之勤不如薰炙之易入往治殷民惟自爾身始
焉是故父子君臣之道常道也是道也爾有之
===
殷民未染惡之先亦有之殆必兢兢焉立爾民
極父子盡其親君臣盡其義于以得是道而著
之於躬行無表裏之相違可也兄弟夫婦朋友
之理常理也是理也爾具之殷民未有遷之前
亦具之殆必業業焉立爾民則長幼盡其序夫
婦盡其別朋友盡其信于以得是理而見之於
實踐無內外之相背可也如是則能盡其厚而
謹其所好矣吾知實之感人捷於桴鼓彼殷之
頑民以蕩凌德向固弗若于汝政矣今則得於
punctuated:
考試官教諭張，批〔得經義程度〕。
考試官教諭李，批〔深合題意〕。
惟大臣能謹其身教，則有以化乎民而善乎俗矣。蓋民之於上，固不從其令而從其好。大臣能謹其所好而以身為教焉，則民之化、俗之善，有出於必然者矣。昔成王命君陳往治東郊，而言及乎此，謂夫訓告之切，孰若身教之難忘？誦說之勤，不如薰炙之易入。往治殷民，惟自爾身始焉。是故父子君臣之道，常道也。是道也，爾有之，殷民未染惡之先亦有之。殆必兢兢焉立爾民極，父子盡其親，君臣盡其義，于以得是道而著之於躬行，無表裏之相違，可也。兄弟夫婦朋友之理，常理也。是理也，爾具之，殷民未有遷之前亦具之。殆必業業焉立爾民則，長幼盡其序，夫婦盡其別，朋友盡其信，于以得是理而見之於實踐，無內外之相背，可也。如是，則能盡其厚而謹其所好矣。吾知實之感人，捷於桴鼓。彼殷之頑民，以蕩凌德，向固弗若于汝政矣，今則得於
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Meets the standard for interpreting the Classics.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Closely accords with the meaning of the topic.〕
Only when a great minister is conscientious about teaching by personal example can he transform the people and improve their customs. For in their dealings with those above them, the people follow not their commands but their preferences. If a great minister is careful about what he favors and teaches through his own conduct, the transformation of the people and improvement of their customs will necessarily follow.
Long ago, when King Cheng ordered Jun Chen to govern the eastern suburbs, he spoke of this. His meaning was: however earnest verbal admonitions may be, how can they compare with the enduring impression of personal example? Diligent recitation and explanation cannot match the ease with which close exposure to virtue penetrates the heart. In going to govern the people of Yin, begin with your own person.
Thus, the Way governing fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, is the constant Way. You possess this Way, and the people of Yin also possessed it before they were tainted by evil. You must therefore, with vigilant care, establish yourself as the highest example for your people: let fathers and sons fully realize their mutual affection, and rulers and ministers their righteousness. In this way, grasp this Way and manifest it in your own conduct, allowing no discrepancy between outward appearance and inward reality.
The principles governing brothers, husbands and wives, and friends are constant principles. You are endowed with them, and the people of Yin were likewise endowed with them before they underwent a change. You must therefore, with utmost care, establish yourself as the standard for your people: let elder and younger fully observe their proper order, husbands and wives their distinctions, and friends their trustworthiness. In this way, grasp these principles and manifest them in practice, allowing no contradiction between the inner and the outer. By doing so, you can fully realize your moral sincerity and be careful about what you favor.
I know that the power of genuine conduct to move others is swifter than a drum’s response to the drumstick. Those recalcitrant people of Yin, who let unrestrained conduct override virtue, formerly would not comply with your governance; now, however, they gain from …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
觀感莫不舍其舊而從乎新怙侈滅義昔固弗
化于汝訓矣今則有所企慕莫不去其惡而遷
於善親義之理藹然於比屋之間而與古之於
變時雍同一大道之時也序別信之道秩然於
閭閻之下而與古之四方風動同一昇平之世
也如是則民亦歸於厚而從其所好矣是則世
道之善而善於殷民向化之日殷民之化而化
於君陳身教之餘端本澄源責其有所歸乎抑
考有周之世文武作之於前成王述之於後其
===
所以為殷民安排而布置者蓋無不周矣而猶
洶洶不靖者何哉蓋殷之頑民染紂之惡深被
周之化淺加之三監為周至親而又叛武庚為
殷之後而被誅而有以動搖其心耳斯時也若
無周公君陳之徒相繼撫之則周之天下未可
知也然亦殷民之幸耳若在強楚之時則席卷
而坑之矣又何暇於多誥哉嗚呼此周家所以
為仁厚之至而享國八百年也歟
詩
punctuated:
觀感，莫不舍其舊而從乎新；怙侈滅義，昔固弗化于汝訓矣，今則有所企慕，莫不去其惡而遷於善。親義之理藹然於比屋之間，而與古之「於變時雍」同一大道之時也；序別信之道秩然於閭閻之下，而與古之「四方風動」同一昇平之世也。如是，則民亦歸於厚而從其所好矣。是則世道之善，而善於殷民向化之日；殷民之化，而化於君陳身教之餘。端本澄源，責其有所歸乎？

抑考有周之世，文武作之於前，成王述之於後，其所以為殷民安排而布置者，蓋無不周矣。而猶洶洶不靖者，何哉？蓋殷之頑民染紂之惡深，被周之化淺，加之三監為周至親而又叛，武庚為殷之後而被誅，而有以動搖其心耳。斯時也，若無周公、君陳之徒相繼撫之，則周之天下未可知也。然亦殷民之幸耳。若在強楚之時，則席卷而坑之矣，又何暇於多誥哉？嗚呼！此周家所以為仁厚之至，而享國八百年也歟！

詩
translation_en:
…through observing your example and being moved by it, all will abandon their old ways and follow the new. Clinging to extravagance and extinguishing righteousness, they formerly remained unchanged by your instruction; now, however, they have something to admire and aspire to, and all will cast off their evil and turn toward goodness. The principles of affection and righteousness will flourish among neighboring households, making this an age of the Great Way like that of antiquity, when “they were transformed and thus brought into harmony.” The Way of proper precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness will prevail in orderly fashion throughout the villages, making this an age of peace like that of antiquity, when “the four quarters were stirred as by the wind.” Thus the people too will return to generosity of character and follow what their ruler esteems. The moral condition of the age will become good when the people of Yin turn toward transformation; and the people of Yin will be transformed through the enduring influence of Jun Chen’s personal example. In setting the root right and clearing the source, does not responsibility have its proper resting place?

Moreover, if we examine the Zhou age, Kings Wen and Wu began the work, and King Cheng continued it afterward. Their arrangements and provisions for the people of Yin were surely complete in every respect. Why, then, did the people remain agitated and unsettled? It was because the recalcitrant people of Yin were deeply imbued with the evil of King Zhou of Shang, while Zhou’s transforming influence had touched them only lightly. Furthermore, the Three Supervisors were close kinsmen of the Zhou house, yet rebelled, while Wu Geng, a descendant of Yin, was put to death. These events were enough to unsettle their hearts. At that time, had men such as the Duke of Zhou and Jun Chen not successively pacified them, the fate of Zhou’s rule over the realm would have been uncertain. Yet this was also good fortune for the people of Yin. Had they lived in the time of mighty Chu, they would have been swept away and buried alive. What leisure would there have been for so many proclamations? Alas! Was this not why the Zhou house attained the utmost benevolence and generosity, and enjoyed possession of its realm for eight hundred years?

Book of Odes

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
威儀抑抑德音秩秩無怨無惡率由羣匹
受福無疆四方之綱之綱之紀燕及朋友
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
趙睿
同考試官訓導楊　批〔題本正大作者多騁浮詞體貼欠明惟此篇鋪張明白詞語舂容深得詩人稱願之意讀之令人躍然是宜録出〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔詞氣温雅説出公尸稱願王者子孫之意殆無餘蘊佳作也〕
考試官教諭張　批〔理致明白而詞足以發之可〕
===
考試官教諭李　批〔理明詞健嘉可嘉〕
詩人稱願王者之子孫也既欲其立治本而獲
福以統治尤欲其垂治休而得臣以願治蓋脩
德任賢人君獲福統治之大本也然非垂治休
而得臣以願之又豈能久福以保治哉公尸答
君而稱願其子孫如此忠愛之意至矣昔公尸
之所以答鳬鷖此則稱願其子孫謂夫人君之
punctuated:
威儀抑抑，德音秩秩，無怨無惡，率由羣匹。受福無疆，四方之綱。之綱之紀，燕及朋友。百辟卿士，媚于天子。不解于位，民之攸墍。

趙睿

同考試官訓導楊　批〔題本正大，作者多騁浮詞，體貼欠明。惟此篇鋪張明白，詞語舂容，深得詩人稱願之意，讀之令人躍然，是宜録出。〕

同考試官教諭朱　批〔詞氣温雅，説出公尸稱願王者子孫之意，殆無餘蘊，佳作也。〕

考試官教諭張　批〔理致明白，而詞足以發之，可。〕

考試官教諭李　批〔理明詞健，嘉可嘉。〕

詩人稱願王者之子孫也，既欲其立治本而獲福以統治，尤欲其垂治休而得臣以願治。蓋脩德任賢，人君獲福統治之大本也。然非垂治休而得臣以願之，又豈能久福以保治哉？公尸答君而稱願其子孫如此，忠愛之意至矣。昔公尸之所以答《鳬鷖》，此則稱願其子孫，謂夫人君之
translation_en:
“Your bearing is restrained and dignified; your virtuous reputation is orderly and constant. Without resentment or hatred, you follow the company of worthy men. You receive blessings without limit and serve as the guiding cord of the four quarters. Their guiding cord and ordering thread, you extend peace and happiness to your friends. The many lords, ministers, and officers love the Son of Heaven. Unflagging in their posts, they are those in whom the people find repose.”

Zhao Rui.

Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently upright and grand, but most writers indulge in empty rhetoric and fail to apprehend its meaning clearly. This essay alone develops it lucidly, with language that is measured and ample, deeply capturing the poet’s intention in offering praise and good wishes. Reading it makes one leap with delight. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The language and tone are gentle and elegant. It expresses the ancestral impersonator’s intention in praising and blessing the king’s descendants, leaving virtually nothing unexplored. An excellent composition.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear, and the language adequately conveys it. Acceptable.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Clear reasoning and vigorous language: praiseworthy, indeed praiseworthy.”

The poet offers praise and good wishes for the king’s descendants. He wishes them to establish the foundations of good government and obtain blessings through which to govern; still more, he wishes them to hand down the blessings of good government and obtain ministers through whom to aspire to good government [?]. For cultivating virtue and employing worthy men are the fundamental means by which a ruler obtains blessings and governs. Yet unless he hands down the blessings of good government and obtains ministers to wish for this [?], how can he perpetuate those blessings and preserve good government? In replying to the ruler, the ancestral impersonator offers such praise and wishes for his descendants: his loyalty and affection are utterly complete. title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
願莫大乎福祿之盛福祿之盛莫大乎子孫之
賢吾願吾王之子孫德之見於威儀者抑抑乎
其甚密德之形於聲譽者秩秩乎其有常威儀
美矣又能無私怨焉以任乎衆賢而賢者在位
聲譽隆矣又能無私惡焉以由乎羣匹而能者
在職是以能受無疆之福禁膺寶曆乘六龍以
御天四方之廣一在其統括也享無窮之福寵
握瑤圖居九重以凝命萬邦之大一在其綱維
也夫惟能綱乎四方也則庶績咸熙而君師之
===
道盡臣下不賴之以安乎能紀乎四方也則庶
事惟康而治理之功成朋友不賴之以燕乎是
以大小而百辟媚焉受吾天子者同一心內而卿
士媚而戴吾元后者同一志惟欲時脩德時任
賢綱焉常張永受無疆之福于以措斯民於康
乂而同沾垂拱之休可也奚但安及臣下而已
哉時任賢時脩德紀焉常理永享無窮之休于
以撫羣生於嘉靖而同被無為之化可也豈但
燕及朋友而已哉吁統治於脩德任賢之餘保
punctuated: 願莫大乎福祿之盛，福祿之盛莫大乎子孫之賢。吾願吾王之子孫，德之見於威儀者，抑抑乎其甚密；德之形於聲譽者，秩秩乎其有常。威儀美矣，又能無私怨焉，以任乎衆賢，而賢者在位；聲譽隆矣，又能無私惡焉，以由乎羣匹，而能者在職。是以能受無疆之福，禁膺寶曆，乘六龍以御天，四方之廣，一在其統括也；享無窮之福，寵握瑤圖，居九重以凝命，萬邦之大，一在其綱維也。夫惟能綱乎四方也，則庶績咸熙，而君師之道盡，臣下不賴之以安乎？能紀乎四方也，則庶事惟康，而治理之功成，朋友不賴之以燕乎？是以大小而百辟媚焉，受吾天子者同一心；內而卿士媚，而戴吾元后者同一志。惟欲時脩德，時任賢，綱焉常張，永受無疆之福，于以措斯民於康乂，而同沾垂拱之休可也，奚但安及臣下而已哉？時任賢，時脩德，紀焉常理，永享無窮之休，于以撫羣生於嘉靖，而同被無為之化可也，豈但燕及朋友而已哉？吁！統治於脩德任賢之餘，保
translation_en: …no wish is greater than abundant blessings and emoluments, and no abundance of blessings and emoluments is greater than having worthy descendants. I wish that the descendants of our king may manifest their virtue in a bearing most carefully restrained, and express their virtue in a reputation marked by order and constancy. Their bearing is admirable; moreover, they can set aside private resentments to employ the many worthy men, so that the worthy hold positions of authority. Their reputation is exalted; moreover, they can set aside private dislikes to make use of their many associates, so that the capable hold office. Thus they can receive boundless blessings, assume the precious imperial succession [?], and ride the six dragons to govern Heaven: the whole vast expanse of the four quarters falls within their encompassing rule. They enjoy blessings without end, are favored with possession of the precious chart of sovereignty, and dwell within the ninefold palace to secure Heaven’s mandate: the whole immensity of the myriad states lies within their governing framework. Only because they can hold together the four quarters do all achievements flourish and the way of ruler and teacher find complete fulfillment. Do their subjects not depend upon this for peace? Because they can bring order to the four quarters, all affairs proceed harmoniously and the work of government succeeds. Do their friends not depend upon this for repose? Thus the many lords, great and small, love them, and those who receive our Son of Heaven [?] share one heart; within the court, the ministers love them, and those who uphold our sovereign share one purpose. They desire only that he cultivate virtue and employ worthy men, keeping the guiding cords of government ever taut and receiving boundless blessings forever. By this means he may settle the people in peace and good order, so that all share the beneficence of rule with folded hands. How could the resulting peace extend only to his subjects? Let him employ worthy men and cultivate virtue, keeping the ordering threads of government ever straight and enjoying endless favor forever. By this means he may nurture all living people in prosperity and tranquility, so that all receive the transforming influence of effortless rule. How could the resulting repose extend only to his friends? Ah! Through cultivating virtue and employing worthy men, he exercises comprehensive rule; he preserves…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
治於安臣致愛之後公尸答君而稱願其子孫
之賢如此何其忠愛之至哉大抵富貴尊榮一
身之福子孫之賢無疆之福故禹得啓賢而夏
祚以永文得武聖而周業以昌既醉之詩則曰
孝子不匱永錫爾類有駜之頌則曰君子有穀
詒孫子是子孫之賢誠為王者之盛福也今公
尸答君而願其子孫之賢如此其亦有見於此
歟
天命降監下民有嚴
同考試官訓導楊　批〔此題傳註最明白作者體認　欠精往往以高宗敬天畏民講殊戾本旨見理明而措詞當者〕
〔無踰此篇〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔題意天命在民正見民之所　以可畏此作體貼明白措詞整潔故錄以式後學〕
考試官教諭張　批〔題意正如此他作無出其右者〕
考試官教諭李　批〔典雅可取〕
詩人即天命之有在乎民而見其民為可畏焉
banxin: 鄉試錄文　十七　刁　嵎
punctuated:
治於安臣致愛之後。公尸答君，而稱願其子孫之賢如此，何其忠愛之至哉！大抵富貴尊榮，一身之福；子孫之賢，無疆之福。故禹得啓賢，而夏祚以永；文得武聖，而周業以昌。《既醉》之詩則曰：「孝子不匱，永錫爾類。」《有駜》之頌則曰：「君子有穀，詒孫子。」是子孫之賢，誠為王者之盛福也。今公尸答君，而願其子孫之賢如此，其亦有見於此歟？

天命降監，下民有嚴。

同考試官訓導楊　批〔此題傳註最明白，作者體認　欠精，往往以高宗敬天畏民講，殊戾本旨。見理明而措詞當者〕〔無踰此篇。〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔題意天命在民，正見民之所　以可畏。此作體貼明白，措詞整潔，故錄以式後學。〕
考試官教諭張　批〔題意正如此，他作無出其右者。〕
考試官教諭李　批〔典雅可取。〕

詩人即天命之有在乎民，而見其民為可畏焉。
translation_en:
…governance after bringing peace to his ministers and securing their affection. The ritual impersonator of the ancestor answers the ruler and expresses such wishes for the worthiness of his descendants: how consummate his loyalty and affection! Wealth, high rank, honor, and glory are generally blessings for one person’s lifetime; worthy descendants are a blessing without limit. Thus Yu had the worthy Qi, and the Xia dynasty endured; King Wen had the sage King Wu, and the Zhou enterprise flourished. The poem “Already Drunk” (Ji zui) says: “May filial sons never fail; may blessings forever be bestowed upon your kind.” The hymn “The Stout Steeds” (You bi) says: “The lord has goodness to bequeath to his descendants.” Worthy descendants are indeed a sovereign’s great blessing. Now the ritual impersonator answers the ruler and thus wishes him worthy descendants. Does he not also perceive this principle?

“Heaven’s Mandate descends in scrutiny; the people below are to be held in awe.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: “The commentaries explain this topic most clearly, but writers’ understanding is insufficiently precise. They frequently interpret it as Gaozong’s reverence for Heaven and awe of the people, greatly contradicting its original purport. For clear perception of principle and fitting expression, no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The topic means that Heaven’s Mandate resides in the people, revealing precisely why the people are to be held in awe. This essay apprehends that meaning clearly and expresses it neatly and coherently. It has therefore been recorded as a model for future students.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The meaning of the topic is exactly this. No other essay surpasses it.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Classical and elegant; worthy of selection.”

The poet proceeds from the fact that Heaven’s Mandate resides in the people to show that the people are to be held in awe.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
蓋民之視聽天命之所在也然則下民之勢不
亦為可畏哉宜詩人以是而頌美高宗也是詩
祀高宗之樂此則將言致中興之道而先言及
此謂夫彼蒼者天人皆以為高高在上穹然其
形而已殊不知天雖高也臨下有赫而命實降
監焉人皆以為赫赫在上蒼然其色而已殊不
知天雖遠也日監在茲而命實下視焉遷予奪
於冲漠之中視不自視而自民之視以為視是
其視在於民也宰去留於蒼冥之表聽不自聽
===
而自民之聽以為聽是其聽在於民也夫天雖
高而視聽有在乎民民雖卑而視聽有通乎天
吾知民心向背而天命之予奪繫之是民雖至
愚而有至神者存閭巷之喧騰一雷霆之震動
也嚴孰甚焉民心從違而天命之去留以之是
民雖至卑而有至高者寓億兆之觀瞻一日月
之照臨也嚴孰加焉是則下民有嚴如此則君
之不可不畏乎民也明矣高宗有見乎此而以
安民為務此其所以得下民之心而受上天之
punctuated: 蓋民之視聽，天命之所在也。然則下民之勢，不亦為可畏哉？宜詩人以是而頌美高宗也。是詩，祀高宗之樂。此則將言致中興之道，而先言及此。謂夫彼蒼者天，人皆以為高高在上，穹然其形而已，殊不知天雖高也，臨下有赫，而命實降監焉。人皆以為赫赫在上，蒼然其色而已，殊不知天雖遠也，日監在茲，而命實下視焉。遷予奪於冲漠之中，視不自視，而自民之視以為視，是其視在於民也。宰去留於蒼冥之表，聽不自聽，而自民之聽以為聽，是其聽在於民也。夫天雖高，而視聽有在乎民；民雖卑，而視聽有通乎天。吾知民心向背，而天命之予奪繫之。是民雖至愚，而有至神者存；閭巷之喧騰，一雷霆之震動也，嚴孰甚焉？民心從違，而天命之去留以之。是民雖至卑，而有至高者寓；億兆之觀瞻，一日月之照臨也，嚴孰加焉？是則下民有嚴如此，則君之不可不畏乎民也明矣。高宗有見乎此，而以安民為務，此其所以得下民之心，而受上天之
translation_en:
For what the people see and hear is where Heaven’s Mandate resides. Is not the position of the common people, then, something to hold in awe? It is fitting that the poet should praise Gaozong on this account. This ode was music for sacrifices to Gaozong. Here, before speaking of the way he brought about a restoration, it first addresses this matter. As for that azure Heaven, people all suppose that it is merely a lofty, vaulted form above them. They fail to understand that, although Heaven is high, it looks down in radiant majesty, and its Mandate indeed descends to oversee those below. People all suppose that it is merely a brilliant presence above, azure in color. They fail to understand that, although Heaven is distant, it watches here daily, and its Mandate indeed looks down upon them. Amid empty stillness, it shifts between bestowing and withdrawing the Mandate. It sees not through sight of its own, but takes the people’s sight as its sight: thus its seeing resides in the people. Beyond the azure heavens, it governs whether the Mandate departs or remains. It hears not through hearing of its own, but takes the people’s hearing as its hearing: thus its hearing resides in the people.

Although Heaven is high, its seeing and hearing reside in the people; although the people are lowly, their seeing and hearing communicate with Heaven. I know that the bestowal or withdrawal of Heaven’s Mandate depends upon whether the people’s hearts turn toward the ruler or away from him. Thus, although the people are utterly unknowing, something supremely numinous exists within them. The clamor of the lanes and alleys is itself a peal of thunder: what could be more awe-inspiring? Whether Heaven’s Mandate departs or remains follows whether the people’s hearts submit or resist. Thus, although the people are utterly lowly, something supremely lofty dwells within them. The gaze of the countless multitudes is itself the illumination of the sun and moon: what could surpass it in awesomeness? Such is the awe-inspiring power of the common people; it is therefore clear that a ruler cannot but hold them in awe. Gaozong understood this and made securing the people’s well-being his task. This was how he won the hearts of the common people and received from Heaven above its …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
命也中興之福有由然哉大抵盤庚既沒治道
寖衰人心既離天命幾墜有商王業蕩乎其衰
矣一旦高宗者出惻然以撥亂反治爲己任賞
無所僭刑無所濫畏民敬天之心不敢少怠合
人心於已離復天命於既墜此其所以平荆楚
畏諸侯而卒成中興之業也商之子孫可不知
所自哉
春秋
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
會王世子于首止　諸侯盟于首止〔僖公五〕
年公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘　諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
王藝
===
同考試官訓導陸　批〔此題作者雜用他傳多戾經〕
〔旨惟此篇專主兩盟下胡傳而作非的見之學不能也是宜録出〕
考試官教諭張　批〔深合吾重詞複之旨〕
考試官教諭李　批〔文有發越〕
春秋於霸主之會盟有複詞以美其正大倫者
punctuated:
命也。中興之福有由然哉！大抵盤庚既沒，治道寖衰，人心既離，天命幾墜，有商王業蕩乎其衰矣。一旦高宗者出，惻然以撥亂反治爲己任，賞無所僭，刑無所濫，畏民敬天之心不敢少怠，合人心於已離，復天命於既墜。此其所以平荆楚，畏諸侯，而卒成中興之業也。商之子孫可不知所自哉！

春秋

公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯，會王世子于首止。諸侯盟于首止。〔僖公五〕年，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。諸侯盟于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕

王藝

同考試官訓導陸，批〔此題作者雜用他傳，多戾經〕〔旨。惟此篇專主兩盟下胡傳而作，非的見之學不能也。是宜録出。〕
考試官教諭張，批〔深合吾重詞複之旨。〕
考試官教諭李，批〔文有發越。〕

春秋於霸主之會盟，有複詞以美其正大倫者，
translation_en:
…the mandate of Heaven. The blessings of dynastic restoration indeed had their source! After Pan Geng died, the way of good government gradually declined. The people’s hearts became estranged, Heaven’s mandate nearly fell away, and the royal enterprise of Shang tottered toward decline. Then Gaozong arose. Deeply concerned, he took as his own responsibility the task of ending disorder and restoring good government. His rewards exceeded no proper bounds, and his punishments were never excessive. He dared not relax for even a moment his reverence for the people and respect for Heaven. He reunited the people’s hearts after they had become estranged and recovered Heaven’s mandate after it had all but fallen away. Thus he pacified Jing and Chu, overawed the regional lords, and ultimately accomplished the restoration of the dynasty. Could the descendants of Shang fail to recognize the source of this achievement?

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. The regional lords made a covenant at Shouzhi. 〔Duke Xi, fifth〕 year. The duke met the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. The regional lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu. 〔Duke Xi, ninth year.〕

Wang Yi

Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Those writing on this topic draw indiscriminately on other commentaries and frequently depart from the Classic’s〕〔meaning. This essay alone bases itself specifically on Hu’s commentary under the two covenant entries. Without learning grounded in precise discernment, this could not have been achieved. It therefore deserves to be included.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔It accords profoundly with my understanding of the purpose of repeated wording [?].〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing has expressive force.〕

In its accounts of the hegemon’s meetings and covenants, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes repeats its wording to praise his rectification of the great human relationships…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
有復詞以美其明大禁者此見齊桓有大功於
天下也春秋復詞書之良有以夫慨周道不復
於西鎬幸齊桓主覇於東州于時惠王寵帶子
鄭危疑天下之大倫殆喪矣桓公有憂之於是
控大扶小因世子下臨既會首止以商同尊之
議及世子返駕復盟首止以申翼戴之義定大
本於杌隉而國勢不搖奠神器於靈長而邦家
□慶□幾太子踐祚是為襄王一舉而父子君
臣之道皆得焉桓之功何如其大哉吾知冠裳
無左衽之憂人類免禽犢之患未必不賴於此
也仲尼稱其一匡豈無謂乎故春秋於會盟同
地再言首止所以著其美之大而不厭於繁也
于時襄王始政諸侯放恣天子之大禁久廢矣
桓公欲明之於是率異恊同因宰孔賜胙既會
葵丘以展下拜之恭逮宰孔言旋復盟葵丘以
嚴約束之令初命一詞三綱之典攸係四命迭
舉九經之要具存已而牲血不歃信在諸侯一
舉而文武成康之法復振焉桓之功又何如哉
punctuated:
有復詞以美其明大禁者，此見齊桓有大功於天下也。《春秋》復詞書之，良有以夫！慨周道不復於西鎬，幸齊桓主覇於東州。于時惠王寵帶，子鄭危疑，天下之大倫殆喪矣。桓公有憂之，於是控大扶小，因世子下臨，既會首止以商同尊之議，及世子返駕，復盟首止以申翼戴之義。定大本於杌隉而國勢不搖，奠神器於靈長而邦家□慶。□幾太子踐祚，是為襄王。一舉而父子君臣之道皆得焉，桓之功何如其大哉！吾知冠裳無左衽之憂，人類免禽犢之患，未必不賴於此也。仲尼稱其一匡，豈無謂乎？故《春秋》於會盟同地再言首止，所以著其美之大而不厭於繁也。
于時襄王始政，諸侯放恣，天子之大禁久廢矣。桓公欲明之，於是率異恊同，因宰孔賜胙，既會葵丘以展下拜之恭，逮宰孔言旋，復盟葵丘以嚴約束之令。初命一詞，三綱之典攸係；四命迭舉，九經之要具存。已而牲血不歃，信在諸侯。一舉而文武成康之法復振焉，桓之功又何如哉！
translation_en:
…there are also repeated phrases that praise his clarification of the great prohibitions. This shows that Duke Huan of Qi rendered great service to all under Heaven. The Spring and Autumn Annals surely had good reason to record these events in repeated wording! It was lamentable that the Way of Zhou was not restored at western Hao, but fortunate that Duke Huan of Qi exercised hegemony in the eastern regions. At that time, King Hui favored Dai, while his son Zheng was in a precarious and uncertain position; the great human relationships of the realm were nearly lost. Duke Huan was concerned about this. Accordingly, he restrained the great states and supported the small. Taking advantage of the heir apparent’s presence among the lords, he first convened the meeting at Shouzhi to discuss their common acknowledgment of the prince’s exalted position. After the heir apparent departed, he again assembled them at Shouzhi to conclude a covenant affirming their duty to support him. He secured the great foundation amid instability, so that the strength of the state did not waver, and established the sacred vessel of sovereignty for enduring prosperity, so that the royal house enjoyed blessings [?]. Soon afterward [?], the heir apparent ascended the throne as King Xiang. In a single undertaking, the proper ways of fathers and sons, rulers and ministers were all upheld. How great was Duke Huan’s achievement! I know that the preservation of civilized dress from the threat of robes fastened on the left, and humanity’s escape from the plight of birds and calves [?], may well have depended on this. Could Zhongni’s praise of his having “set the realm right” have been without meaning? Thus, although the meeting and covenant occurred at the same place, the Spring and Autumn Annals names Shouzhi twice, making manifest the greatness of his merit without shunning repetition.
At that time, King Xiang had just begun his reign, and the regional lords acted without restraint; the Son of Heaven’s great prohibitions had long fallen into disuse. Duke Huan wished to make them clear. Accordingly, he brought the divergent parties into accord. On the occasion when Chief Minister Kong bestowed sacrificial meat upon him, he first held the meeting at Kuiqiu to demonstrate his reverence by descending to bow. Once Chief Minister Kong had departed, he again assembled the lords at Kuiqiu to conclude a covenant and enforce its binding commands. The wording of the first injunction concerned the principles of the Three Bonds; the four further injunctions, proclaimed in succession, embodied all the essentials of the Nine Guidelines. Thereupon, no one smeared his lips with the sacrificial blood: trust prevailed among the regional lords. In a single undertaking, the institutions of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were revived. What, then, can be said of Duke Huan’s achievement!…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
大哉吾知收人心於星散之餘扶王綱於解紐
之後未必不伏於此也孟子與其爲盛豈無見
乎故春秋於會盟同地再言葵丘又以著其美
之大而不嫌於贅也吁始也一舉而大倫正終
也一舉而大禁明桓亦當時之傑然者歟雖然
桓之霸亦可謂盛矣何葵丘一盛而遽衰歟盖
桓之霸仲之相也桓無至誠之德仲無格心之
學志之所期者霸也非王也期於王者至於王
期於霸者止於霸桓仲之願既滿於葵丘之盛
桓仲之業不得不衰於葵丘之盟也使桓仲以
王道自期其功烈豈止於葵丘邪豈衰於葵丘
邪
===
西狩獲麟〔哀公十四年〕
袁檟
同考試官訓導陸　批〔題本正大作者類多不諳傳意〕
〔獨袁生此作前用王道人倫說後用孟子性命之言融化出終天〕
〔道之意篇末又斷制獲麟之疑他日深明經學必能處大事決大〕
〔疑矣本房之白月未難與〕
punctuated:
大哉！吾知收人心於星散之餘，扶王綱於解紐之後，未必不伏於此也。孟子與其爲盛，豈無見乎？故春秋於會盟同地，再言葵丘，又以著其美之大，而不嫌於贅也。吁！始也一舉而大倫正，終也一舉而大禁明，桓亦當時之傑然者歟！雖然，桓之霸亦可謂盛矣，何葵丘一盛而遽衰歟？盖桓之霸，仲之相也。桓無至誠之德，仲無格心之學，志之所期者霸也，非王也。期於王者至於王，期於霸者止於霸。桓仲之願既滿於葵丘之盛，桓仲之業不得不衰於葵丘之盟也。使桓仲以王道自期，其功烈豈止於葵丘邪？豈衰於葵丘邪？

西狩獲麟〔哀公十四年〕
袁檟
同考試官訓導陸批〔題本正大，作者類多不諳傳意。〕〔獨袁生此作，前用王道人倫說，後用孟子性命之言，融化出終天〕〔道之意。篇末又斷制獲麟之疑，他日深明經學，必能處大事、決大〕〔疑矣。本房之白月，未難與。〕
translation_en:
… How great! I understand that gathering people’s hearts after they had scattered like stars, and sustaining the bonds of royal authority after they had come undone, may well have had their foundations here. When Mengzi praised this as a flourishing achievement, was his judgment without insight? Thus, although the meeting and covenant took place at the same location, the Spring and Autumn Annals names Kuiqiu twice, again to manifest the greatness of this achievement’s excellence, without considering the repetition superfluous. Ah! At the beginning, a single action set the great human relationships aright; at the end, a single action made the great prohibitions clear. Was Duke Huan not an outstanding man of his age?

Nevertheless, although Duke Huan’s hegemony may indeed be called flourishing, why did it decline so abruptly after reaching its height at Kuiqiu? Duke Huan’s hegemony depended on Guan Zhong’s service as minister. Huan lacked the virtue of perfect sincerity, and Zhong lacked the learning necessary to rectify the ruler’s heart. Their ambition was hegemony, not true kingship. Those who aspire to true kingship attain it; those who aspire to hegemony stop at hegemony. Once Huan and Zhong’s wishes had been fulfilled by the flourishing achievement at Kuiqiu, their undertaking could not but decline from the covenant at Kuiqiu onward. Had Huan and Zhong set their aspirations upon the Kingly Way, would their achievements have stopped at Kuiqiu? Would they have declined at Kuiqiu?

During a Hunt in the West, a Qilin Was Captured [Fourteenth year of Duke Ai]
Yuan Jia

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, an Assistant Instructor: [The topic is fundamentally upright and grand, but most writers do not understand the commentary’s meaning.] [Only this composition by student Yuan first employs an exposition of the Kingly Way and human relationships, then draws upon Mengzi’s statements on human nature and Heaven’s mandate, integrating them to bring out the meaning of concluding in accordance with the Way of Heaven. At the end of the essay, he also adjudicates the doubts surrounding the capture of the qilin. In the future, when he has attained a profound understanding of classical learning, he will surely be able to handle great affairs and resolve great doubts. As for being the “white moon” of this examination section, it would not be difficult to accord him that distinction [?].]

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張　批〔講出絶筆於天道之意迥異〕
衆作
考試官教諭李　批〔深得胡傳之旨〕
聖經有感乎天道聖筆因終乎天道此西狩獲
麟有以見聖人秉筆之成功絶筆之妙用也且
麟之爲瑞也昭昭矣非盛世不出非明王不至
春秋何世也魯𠅘何君也麟何爲獲於魯之西
狩乎蓋天地間之常理惟感與應爾人事感於
下則天道應於上世值周末彛倫之壞甚矣夫
===
子爲世道之計作春秋之書明王道以垂範百
王正人倫以綱維百世治功與禹周相配神化
與天地同流志氣交孚而天人之相感深矣故
制作之文方成於衆魯帝王之瑞遂出於西郊
是豈偶然者哉正與河洛之呈祥鳳鳥之來儀
同一感應之理也然則何爲絶筆於獲麟乎蓋
聖人之於天道曰命與性爾命固由於天而性
則在於已世值周末天道之否極矣夫子致盡
性之功任參贊之責以人合天而不任於天以
punctuated:
考試官教諭張，批〔講出絶筆於天道之意，迥異〕衆作。
考試官教諭李，批〔深得胡傳之旨〕
聖經有感乎天道，聖筆因終乎天道。此西狩獲麟，有以見聖人秉筆之成功、絶筆之妙用也。且麟之爲瑞也，昭昭矣。非盛世不出，非明王不至。春秋何世也？魯𠅘何君也？麟何爲獲於魯之西狩乎？蓋天地間之常理，惟感與應爾。人事感於下，則天道應於上。世值周末，彛倫之壞甚矣。夫子爲世道之計，作春秋之書，明王道以垂範百王，正人倫以綱維百世。治功與禹周相配，神化與天地同流，志氣交孚，而天人之相感深矣。故制作之文方成於衆魯，帝王之瑞遂出於西郊。是豈偶然者哉？正與河洛之呈祥、鳳鳥之來儀，同一感應之理也。然則何爲絶筆於獲麟乎？蓋聖人之於天道，曰命與性爾。命固由於天，而性則在於已。世值周末，天道之否極矣。夫子致盡性之功，任參贊之責，以人合天，而不任於天，以
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔“It brings out the meaning of ending the writing in accordance with the Way of Heaven, standing far apart from〕 the other compositions.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“It profoundly grasps the purport of Hu’s Commentary.”〕
The sage’s classic moved the Way of Heaven, and the sage’s brush accordingly came to rest in accordance with the Way of Heaven. Thus, in the capture of the qilin during the western hunt, we can see the accomplished work of the sage’s taking up his brush and the subtle efficacy of his laying it down. Moreover, that the qilin is an auspicious sign is perfectly clear. It does not emerge except in a flourishing age; it does not arrive except under an enlightened king. What sort of age was that of the Spring and Autumn Annals? What sort of ruler was the ruler of Lu [?]? Why was a qilin captured during Lu’s western hunt? The constant principle operating between Heaven and Earth is simply that of stimulus and response. When human affairs exert a stimulus below, the Way of Heaven responds above. In the closing years of the Zhou, the enduring moral relationships had fallen into grave disorder. Planning for the moral order of the world, the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals. He elucidated the kingly Way to furnish a model for a hundred kings and rectified human relationships to provide a guiding framework for a hundred generations. His achievement in ordering the world matched that of Yu and the Duke of Zhou; his wondrous transforming influence flowed together with Heaven and Earth. Their purposes and vital energies accorded in mutual trust, and the reciprocal influence of Heaven and humanity was profound. Thus, just as his normative writing was completed in Lu [?], the auspicious sign of imperial and royal rule appeared in the western outskirts. Could this have been accidental? It exemplified precisely the same principle of stimulus and response as the auspicious signs presented by the Yellow River and the Luo River, and the phoenix coming to display its stately bearing.
Why, then, did he cease writing at the capture of the qilin? The sage’s relation to the Way of Heaven concerns simply destiny and human nature. Destiny indeed derives from Heaven, while one’s nature resides within oneself. In the closing years of the Zhou, the obstruction of the Way of Heaven had reached its extreme. The Master carried to completion the work of fully realizing his nature and assumed the responsibility of participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth. Through human effort he brought humanity into accord with Heaven, without leaving matters to Heaven; through …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
義立命而不委於命至誠格天地之心瑞應兆
文明之治天人胞合而聖人之能事畢矣故經
以人事而作因以天道而終是豈苟然者哉正
與周南之麟趾召南之騶虞同一終篇之義也
秉筆也而天道應絕筆也以天道終聖人先天
而天弗違後天而奉天時其功用之極有如此
夫雖然獲麟之說不一曰文成致麟曰感麟而
作要皆未可知也孟子曰孔子懼作春秋此其
大者麟固為聖人出也然春秋之作不係於麟
===
之有無麟不出春秋未必不作也春秋不作麟
未必不出也特以麟而終其所感深矣此固獲
麟意也
禮記
凡居民財必因天地寒煖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間異俗剛柔輕重遲速異齊
五味異和器械異制衣服異宜脩其教不
易其俗齊其政不易其宜
回登
punctuated:
義立命，而不委於命。至誠格天地之心，瑞應兆文明之治，天人胞合，而聖人之能事畢矣。故經以人事而作，因以天道而終，是豈苟然者哉？正與《周南》之《麟趾》、《召南》之《騶虞》同一終篇之義也。秉筆也，而天道應；絕筆也，以天道終。聖人先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時，其功用之極有如此夫！雖然，獲麟之說不一，曰文成致麟，曰感麟而作，要皆未可知也。孟子曰：「孔子懼，作《春秋》。」此其大者。麟固為聖人出也，然《春秋》之作不係於麟之有無。麟不出，《春秋》未必不作也；《春秋》不作，麟未必不出也。特以麟而終，其所感深矣。此固獲麟意也。
禮記
凡居民財，必因天地寒煖燥濕、廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。
回登
translation_en:
…establishing his destiny through righteousness rather than abandoning himself to destiny. His utmost sincerity moved the heart of Heaven and Earth, and an auspicious response heralded a reign of cultural illumination. Heaven and humanity were united [?], and the sage’s work was complete. Thus the Classic was composed on the basis of human affairs and brought to a close in accordance with the Way of Heaven. Could this have been arbitrary? Its conclusion has precisely the same significance as “The Qilin’s Hoofs,” which concludes the “Airs of Zhou and the South,” and “The Zouyu,” which concludes the “Airs of Shao and the South.” When he took up his brush, the Way of Heaven responded; when he laid it down, he concluded with the Way of Heaven. When the sage acted before Heaven, Heaven did not contravene him; when he acted after Heaven, he followed Heaven’s seasons. Such was the utmost reach of his achievement!
Nevertheless, accounts of the capture of the qilin differ. Some say that completion of the text brought forth the qilin; others, that he composed the work because he was moved by the qilin’s appearance. Ultimately, neither claim can be known for certain. Mengzi said, “Confucius became apprehensive and composed the Spring and Autumn Annals.” This is the essential point. The qilin certainly appeared for the sage, but the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals did not depend on whether it appeared. Had the qilin not appeared, the Annals would not necessarily have remained unwritten; had the Annals not been written, the qilin would not necessarily have failed to appear. Yet he specifically concluded with the qilin, so profoundly was he moved by it. This, indeed, is the meaning of the capture of the qilin.
Record of Rites
Whenever settling the people and ordering their resources, one must take account of the differing conditions of Heaven and Earth—cold and warmth, dryness and dampness, broad valleys and great rivers. The people born among these have different customs. Their dispositions differ in firmness and gentleness, levity and gravity, slowness and speed; their blends of the five flavors differ; their implements differ in design; and different clothing suits them. Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; bring their government into order without changing what suits them.
Hui Deng.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張　批〔場屋中作禮經文字多用廳見穿鑿詞語險僻令人厭觀此篇一破灑然詞格峻整而理致精到必深於禮者用録以式〕
考試官教諭張　批〔長題貴該括是作得之〕
考試官教諭李　批〔明凈可嘉〕
聖王之儲民用也不強其所難同惟一其所可
同夫習俗本於人情雖不可同而政教原於天
性則可同也聖王於此得不度其可否而財成
輔相之哉王制記此謂夫民生日用必須乎材
===
聖王儲材必有其道何耶是故天地之氣東南
多煖西北多寒因之為絺為裘以備寒煖之用
焉地勢高者必燥卑者必濕因之為舟為車以
備燥濕之用焉谷谿而廣川流而大自天地初
分其形制已不同矣民生於谷民生於川自兩
儀奠位其習俗亦云異矣以言情性之緩急則
有剛柔輕重遲速之異齊以言飲食之調劑則
有鹹苦酸辛甘滑之異和同一備用也而器械
之制不能無或殊同一文身也而衣服之宜不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張　批〔場屋中作禮經文字，多用廳見穿鑿，詞語險僻，令人厭觀。此篇一破，灑然，詞格峻整，而理致精到，必深於禮者，用録以式。〕
考試官教諭張　批〔長題貴該括，是作得之。〕
考試官教諭李　批〔明凈可嘉。〕
聖王之儲民用也，不強其所難同，惟一其所可同。夫習俗本於人情，雖不可同，而政教原於天性，則可同也。聖王於此，得不度其可否，而財成輔相之哉？《王制》記此，謂夫民生日用必須乎材，聖王儲材必有其道，何耶？是故天地之氣，東南多煖，西北多寒，因之為絺、為裘，以備寒煖之用焉。地勢高者必燥，卑者必濕，因之為舟、為車，以備燥濕之用焉。谷谿而廣，川流而大，自天地初分，其形制已不同矣。民生於谷，民生於川，自兩儀奠位，其習俗亦云異矣。以言情性之緩急，則有剛柔輕重遲速之異齊；以言飲食之調劑，則有鹹苦酸辛甘滑之異和。同一備用也，而器械之制不能無或殊；同一文身也，而衣服之宜不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Examination essays on the Classic of Rites frequently employ hearsay [?] and strained interpretations; their language is obscure and eccentric, making them tiresome to read. This essay breaks free of that tendency and is refreshingly clear. Its diction and structure are rigorous and orderly, and its reasoning is precise and penetrating. Its author must have a profound understanding of ritual. It is selected for inclusion as a model.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔For a long topic, comprehensive coverage is essential. This composition achieves it.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Its clarity and purity merit praise.〕
When the sage kings laid up supplies for the people’s use, they did not force uniformity upon what was difficult to make uniform, but unified only what could be made uniform. Customs are rooted in human feelings and cannot be made uniform; government and instruction, however, originate in Heaven-endowed human nature and can be made uniform. In dealing with these matters, could the sage kings fail to assess what was practicable and what was not, and accordingly shape and assist them? The chapter “Royal Regulations” records this, saying that the people’s daily lives necessarily depend upon material resources, and that the sage kings must have had a proper way of storing these resources. What was it?
Thus, in the climatic influences of Heaven and Earth, the southeast is predominantly warm and the northwest predominantly cold. Accordingly, they made fine ramie clothing and fur garments to provide for use in warmth and cold. High-lying terrain is necessarily dry, and low-lying terrain necessarily wet. Accordingly, they made boats and carriages to provide for use in dry and wet conditions. Broad valleys and ravines, and great flowing rivers: ever since Heaven and Earth first separated, their physical configurations have differed. People live in valleys and beside rivers; ever since the Two Powers, Heaven and Earth, took their places, the people’s customs, too, have differed. In the deliberateness or urgency of their dispositions, there are differing measures of firmness and gentleness, lightness and gravity, slowness and speed. In the seasoning of food and drink, there are different blends of saltiness, bitterness, sourness, pungency, sweetness, and smoothness. Implements all serve to meet practical needs, yet their designs cannot be without differences; clothing all serves to adorn the body, yet what is suitable cannot…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
能無或異聖王於此亦豈必強之使同哉惟脩
其三綱五典之教使彝倫攸敘典禮克敦陶民
性於治化之中而已爾若夫民情之異俗尚嘗
有所更張乎齊其禮樂刑政之用俾紀綱振舉
法度脩明肅民心於矩度之内而已爾若夫民
俗之異宜何嘗有所變易乎是知同其政教則
有以復人性之本然因其俗宜則有以順人情
之自然聖王財成輔相之道何以加於此哉嗟
夫天生材以資世民須材以養生民材之當居
===
也尚矣柰何五方皆有性千里不同風欲一律
以齊之未必不咈其情之所安故聖王之馭世
必因其俗宜之異而一以政教之同則民材以
備民用以足不強其必齊而自無不齊不強其
必得而自無不得此其所以善於調劑天下而
致大一統之治也歟
脩身及家平均天下
遏貢
同考試官教諭張 批〔揭書命題非甚難者但作者〕
punctuated:
能無或異。聖王於此，亦豈必強之使同哉？惟脩其三綱五典之教，使彝倫攸敘，典禮克敦，陶民性於治化之中而已爾。若夫民情之異俗，尚嘗有所更張乎？齊其禮樂刑政之用，俾紀綱振舉，法度脩明，肅民心於矩度之内而已爾。若夫民俗之異宜，何嘗有所變易乎？是知同其政教，則有以復人性之本然；因其俗宜，則有以順人情之自然。聖王財成輔相之道，何以加於此哉？嗟夫！天生材以資世，民須材以養生，民材之當居也尚矣。柰何五方皆有性，千里不同風，欲一律以齊之，未必不咈其情之所安。故聖王之馭世，必因其俗宜之異，而一以政教之同，則民材以備，民用以足。不強其必齊，而自無不齊；不強其必得，而自無不得。此其所以善於調劑天下，而致大一統之治也歟！
脩身及家，平均天下。
遏貢
同考試官教諭張批〔揭書命題，非甚難者，但作者〕
translation_en:
…cannot be without differences. In these matters, would the sage kings insist on forcing everyone to conform? They merely cultivated instruction in the Three Bonds and Five Constant Relationships, so that the enduring human relationships were properly ordered and established rites duly honored, molding the people's dispositions through good government and moral transformation. As for the differing customs arising from people's sentiments, did they ever alter them? They made uniform the application of rites, music, punishments, and administration, ensuring that governing principles were upheld and laws and standards maintained and clarified, thereby bringing people's hearts into disciplined conformity with proper bounds. As for the differing practices suited to local customs, when did they ever change them? Thus we know that uniform government and instruction provide the means to restore human nature to its original condition, while accommodation to local customs provides the means to follow the natural inclinations of human feeling. How could the sage kings' way of shaping and assisting the workings of nature surpass this?
Alas! Heaven produces resources to sustain the world, and the people depend upon resources to nourish their lives. The proper accommodation of people and resources [?] has long been a concern. Yet the five regions each have their own dispositions, and places a thousand li apart have different customs. To seek to bring them into conformity under a single rule might well go against what their feelings find congenial. Thus, in governing the world, the sage kings necessarily accommodated differences in local customs and circumstances, while unifying them through common government and instruction. The people's resources were thereby fully provided, and their needs adequately met. Without compelling uniformity, they naturally left nothing unharmonized; without compelling everyone to obtain what they needed, they naturally left none unprovided for. Was this not how they skillfully harmonized all under Heaven and achieved the rule of grand unity?
“Cultivate oneself, extend this to the family, and bring equity and peace to all under Heaven.”
E Gong 遏貢 [?].
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Selecting a passage from a book to set a topic is not especially difficult, but those who compose answers …〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
多選註意率於脩身及家上分截甚是無謂獨此作能隨傳註立說
深得本旨且明白痛快文辭整整故取以為本房之冠
考試官教諭張　批〔說出知古樂而明修身之道可取〕
考試官教諭李　批〔能融會傳意以文錄之〕
君子知古樂以端其本則化洽於遠近矣盖身
者家國天下之本也能端其本則舉此而措之
又何化之不洽哉昔子夏因魏文侯不知古樂
之可好故告之至此意謂天下國家本於身而
身之脩本於樂君子誠知古樂之和正以廣而
===
不流會守拊鼓而有序和序之理洞鑒其惡若
知古樂之始奏以文而本乎仁復亂以武而制
以義仁義之道昭灼其纖悉以之脩身吾見欲
心以平耳目聰明而查滓其消融也蹀以釋血
氣和平邪穢其蕩滌也身不於是而脩乎脩身
之道既明由是篤近舉遠而化無不洽矣是故
身者家之本也以之齊家則樂行而倫清父子
和親長幼和順肅雍之化形於閨門淫僻不作
也和睦之道敦于九族乖戾不生也家不於是
punctuated:
多選註意，率於脩身及家上分截，甚是無謂。獨此作能隨傳註立說，深得本旨，且明白痛快，文辭整整，故取以為本房之冠。
考試官教諭張　批〔說出知古樂而明修身之道可取〕
考試官教諭李　批〔能融會傳意以文錄之〕
君子知古樂以端其本，則化洽於遠近矣。盖身者家國天下之本也，能端其本，則舉此而措之，又何化之不洽哉？昔子夏因魏文侯不知古樂之可好，故告之至此。意謂天下國家本於身，而身之脩本於樂。君子誠知古樂之和正，以廣而不流，會守拊鼓而有序，和序之理洞鑒其惡；若知古樂之始，奏以文而本乎仁，復亂以武而制以義，仁義之道昭灼其纖悉。以之脩身，吾見欲心以平，耳目聰明，而查滓其消融也；蹀以釋，血氣和平，邪穢其蕩滌也。身不於是而脩乎？脩身之道既明，由是篤近舉遠，而化無不洽矣。是故身者家之本也，以之齊家，則樂行而倫清，父子和親，長幼和順。肅雍之化形於閨門，淫僻不作也；和睦之道敦于九族，乖戾不生也。家不於是
translation_en:
…Most select ideas from the annotations [?], generally making a division at “cultivating oneself and extending this to the family”—a thoroughly pointless distinction. This composition alone develops its argument in accordance with the commentary and annotations, thoroughly grasping the original purport. Moreover, it is clear and incisive, and its language is well ordered. I therefore selected it as the finest essay in this examining section.
Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: 〔Its explanation that understanding ancient music brings clarity about the way of self-cultivation merits selection.〕
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: 〔It integrates the meaning of the commentary; I select it for its literary merit.〕
When the gentleman understands ancient music and thereby rectifies his foundation, his transforming influence reaches both near and far. The self is the foundation of the family, the state, and all under Heaven. If one can rectify this foundation, then, applying it more broadly, where could one's transforming influence fail to reach? Formerly, because Marquis Wen of Wei did not understand why ancient music deserved to be loved, Zixia explained matters to him thus far. His meaning was that all under Heaven, the state, and the family are rooted in the self, while cultivation of the self is rooted in music. If the gentleman truly understands the harmony and correctness of ancient music—its breadth without excess, and the order observed in its ensemble and its playing of the struck instruments and drums [?]—he will thoroughly perceive the principles of harmony and order in their depths [?]. If he understands how ancient music begins with civil movements rooted in benevolence, and concludes with martial movements regulated by righteousness, the way of benevolence and righteousness will become brilliantly clear in its minutest details.
