Applying this to self-cultivation, I see the desirous heart calmed, the ears and eyes made keen, and impurities dissolved; agitation is released [?], the blood and vital energies become harmonious and balanced, and depravity and defilement are swept away. Is the self not thereby cultivated? Once the way of self-cultivation is understood, one strengthens what is near and extends it to what is distant, and one's transforming influence reaches everywhere.
Thus the self is the foundation of the family. Applying this to ordering the family, music is practiced and human relationships become clear: fathers and sons are harmonious and affectionate, elders and juniors harmonious and compliant. A reverent and harmonious transforming influence manifests itself within the household, and licentiousness and perversity do not arise. The way of harmony and concord is strengthened among the nine degrees of kinship, and discord does not emerge. Is the family not thereby …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而齊乎家者一國天下之本也以之平均天下
則樂行而民向方風焉以移俗焉以易世躋泰
和無偏無黨上下一德也民囿熙皥無反無側
遠近同化也天下不於是而平均乎吁君子知
古樂而明脩身之道則家齊國治而天下平如
此吾君之聽樂烏可不知所擇耶抑論古樂之
為用大矣時至春秋樂教不興民偽日滋當時
之人靡然趨於新樂之是好求其知古樂之正
而好之者幾何人哉無惟乎魏文侯聽之而惟
===
恐臥也向非子夏歷舉而詳告之則人又孰從
而知古樂之正足以脩身及家平均天下也哉
善乎吾夫子論為邦有曰樂則韶舞放鄭聲子
夏之言其有得於此歟
第貳場
論
君子之學以潤身為本
杜珏
同考試官教諭邵 批〔作論當以立意為主造語乃〕
punctuated:
而齊乎？家者，一國天下之本也。以之平均天下，則樂行而民向方，風焉以移，俗焉以易，世躋泰和，無偏無黨，上下一德也；民囿熙皥，無反無側，遠近同化也。天下不於是而平均乎？吁！君子知古樂而明脩身之道，則家齊國治而天下平如此，吾君之聽樂，烏可不知所擇耶？抑論古樂之為用大矣！時至春秋，樂教不興，民偽日滋。當時之人靡然趨於新樂之是好，求其知古樂之正而好之者，幾何人哉？無惟乎魏文侯聽之而惟恐臥也。向非子夏歷舉而詳告之，則人又孰從而知古樂之正足以脩身及家、平均天下也哉？善乎吾夫子論為邦有曰：「樂則韶舞，放鄭聲。」子夏之言，其有得於此歟？

第貳場

論

君子之學以潤身為本

杜珏

同考試官教諭邵批〔作論當以立意為主，造語乃〕
translation_en:
…and thus be brought into order? The family is the foundation of the state and of all under Heaven. By using music to bring peace and equitable order to all under Heaven, music will prevail and the people will turn toward righteousness. Customs and practices will change, and the age will attain supreme harmony. Without partiality or faction, those above and below will share one virtue. The people will dwell in radiant concord; without perversity or deviation, those far and near will share the same transforming influence. Will all under Heaven not thereby attain peace and equitable order? Ah! When the gentleman understands ancient music and comprehends the way of cultivating himself, his family is ordered, his state is governed, and all under Heaven is brought to peace in this manner. How, then, can our ruler listen to music without knowing what to choose?

Indeed, the efficacy of ancient music is great! By the Spring and Autumn period, instruction through music no longer flourished, and deceit among the people increased daily. People of that time followed the prevailing trend, delighting only in new music. How many could be found who understood the correctness of ancient music and delighted in it? It is hardly surprising [?] that when Marquis Wen of Wei listened to it, his only fear was that he would fall asleep. Had Zixia not enumerated its features and explained them to him in detail, from whom could people have learned that the correctness of ancient music suffices to cultivate oneself, extend that cultivation to the family, and bring peace and equitable order to all under Heaven? How excellent were the words of our Master when discussing the government of a state: “For music, use the Shao dance; banish the sounds of Zheng.” Had Zixia’s words perhaps grasped something of this teaching?

Second Session

Discourse

The Gentleman’s Learning Takes the Refinement of His Person as Its Foundation

Du Jue

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔In composing a discourse, establishing its central idea should come first; crafting its language is…〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
其次者塲中作者不究題目原委率多牽引舊詞殊爲可厭此篇能
究其所自而著之筆下理有根據辭有波瀾中間提掇一本字尤有
關鍵非學識老成者不能宜録之以矯塲屋之氣習也
考試官教諭張　批〔不煩繩削而自精到當是作手〕
考試官教諭李　批〔有源委有發越讀之終篇猶有餘味老手也〕
學之道有本有末得其本則末自隨之何
則人之一身人物之本學者必於其本焉
圖之則舉近以及遠守約而施博措之於
===
治人應物亦無乎不順且利矣否則大本
一失更學何事秪見夫人之衆物之夥治
之而不能治應之而不能應徒自紛擾耳
君子知其然其學汲汲其心皇皇一理未
明求以知之一理未備求以體之所以然
者何也無非爲潤身計耳故身潤而本立
本立而末隨天下之事可徐就吾之條理
矣噫此君子之先本後末所以爲善學歟
邵子曰君子之學以潤身爲本請因是而
punctuated:
其次者。塲中作者不究題目原委，率多牽引舊詞，殊爲可厭。此篇能究其所自而著之筆下，理有根據，辭有波瀾。中間提掇一本字，尤有關鍵，非學識老成者不能。宜録之，以矯塲屋之氣習也。
考試官教諭張，批〔不煩繩削而自精到，當是作手〕
考試官教諭李，批〔有源委，有發越，讀之終篇猶有餘味，老手也〕
學之道，有本有末，得其本則末自隨之。何則？人之一身，人物之本。學者必於其本焉圖之，則舉近以及遠，守約而施博，措之於治人應物，亦無乎不順且利矣。否則大本一失，更學何事？秪見夫人之衆、物之夥，治之而不能治，應之而不能應，徒自紛擾耳。君子知其然，其學汲汲，其心皇皇，一理未明，求以知之；一理未備，求以體之。所以然者何也？無非爲潤身計耳。故身潤而本立，本立而末隨，天下之事可徐就吾之條理矣。噫！此君子之先本後末，所以爲善學歟！邵子曰：「君子之學以潤身爲本。」請因是而
translation_en:
…is secondary. Those who compose in the examination hall fail to investigate the subject’s origins and implications; most merely drag in familiar phrases, which is exceedingly tiresome. This essay can trace the subject to its source and set it down in writing: its reasoning has a firm foundation, and its language has movement and variety. The way it singles out the word “root” in the middle is especially pivotal; only someone mature in learning and understanding could accomplish this. It should be included in the record to correct the habitual tendencies of examination writing.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Without requiring correction or trimming, it is naturally refined and exact. This must be an accomplished writer.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔It traces origins and ramifications and develops its ideas with vigor. Even after reading the entire piece, a lingering savor remains. This is a seasoned hand.〕
The Way of learning has a root and branches. Once its root is grasped, the branches follow of themselves. Why is this? One’s own person is the root of one’s dealings with people and things. Learners must direct their efforts toward this root. Then they can proceed from what is near to what is distant, hold to what is essential while applying it broadly, and, when putting it into practice in governing people and responding to things, find nothing that does not go smoothly and advantageously. Otherwise, once this great root is lost, what else is there to learn? One sees only the multitude of people and the profusion of things: one tries to govern them but cannot, tries to respond to them but cannot, and merely becomes entangled in confusion.
Knowing this, the gentleman pursues learning diligently and remains ever watchful in his heart. If a single principle is not yet clear, he seeks to understand it; if a single principle is not yet fully realized, he seeks to embody it. Why does he do so? All his efforts are directed toward refining his own person. Thus, when his person is refined, the root is established; when the root is established, the branches follow. The affairs of the world can gradually be brought into accord with the order within himself. Ah! Is this priority the gentleman gives to the root over the branches not what makes him adept at learning? Master Shao said, “The gentleman’s learning takes the refinement of his own person as its root.” Allow me, on this basis, to…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
論焉夫天下之事莫不有本一事有一事
之本一物有一物之本物本於蒙數本於
一發生本於一陽之復斂穫本於一陰之
遇水本於源之遠山本於基之厚學之本
獨不在於潤身乎是故面墻之立豐屋之
蔀不學過也舍己之田耘人之田不知本
也然則人必貴於學學必貴於務本君子
可少忽也哉嘗試以吾身自列於天地者
而並觀之未嘗不嘆吾身之大而不知學
===
者小之也夫天地者萬物之父母也人與
我雖共為父母之子而本末緩急亦未嘗
混焉者也何者明己之德而後民可新成
己之德而後物可成身不行道不能行於
妻子己身罔治豈能治乎國人此理也亦
勢也君子知吾身為天下人物之本是以
不屑屑於他事惟以潤身為急固非欲獨
善也知本之在此而所務亦在此也不遑
遑於他務獨以潤身為心抑非欲忘世也
punctuated: 論焉。夫天下之事，莫不有本。一事有一事之本，一物有一物之本。物本於蒙，數本於一，發生本於一陽之復，斂穫本於一陰之遇。水本於源之遠，山本於基之厚，學之本獨不在於潤身乎？是故面墻之立、豐屋之蔀，不學過也；舍己之田，耘人之田，不知本也。然則人必貴於學，學必貴於務本，君子可少忽也哉？嘗試以吾身自列於天地者而並觀之，未嘗不嘆吾身之大，而不知學者小之也。夫天地者，萬物之父母也。人與我雖共為父母之子，而本末緩急亦未嘗混焉者也。何者？明己之德而後民可新，成己之德而後物可成。身不行，道不能行於妻子；己身罔治，豈能治乎國人？此理也，亦勢也。君子知吾身為天下人物之本，是以不屑屑於他事，惟以潤身為急，固非欲獨善也，知本之在此，而所務亦在此也；不遑遑於他務，獨以潤身為心，抑非欲忘世也。
translation_en:
…discuss it. Nothing among the affairs of the world is without a root. Each affair has its own root, and each thing has its own root. Things are rooted in incipience; numbers are rooted in one. Generation and growth are rooted in the return of a single yang line; gathering and harvesting are rooted in the encounter with a single yin line. Water is rooted in the remoteness of its source, and mountains in the solidity of their foundations. Can the root of learning alone fail to lie in enriching oneself through virtue? Thus, standing as though facing a wall, or dwelling beneath the screening of a grand house, is the fault of failing to learn; abandoning one’s own field to weed another’s is failing to understand the root. People must therefore prize learning, and learning must prize attending to the root. Can the gentleman neglect this even slightly?

Whenever I consider my own person standing alongside Heaven and Earth, viewing them together, I cannot but marvel at the greatness of my own person, which those who do not understand learning diminish. Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things. Although others and I are alike children of these parents, the distinctions between root and branch, and between what may wait and what is urgent, are never confused. Why? Only after making one’s own virtue bright can one renew the people; only after perfecting one’s own virtue can one bring other things to fulfillment. If one does not personally practice the Way, it cannot prevail even among one’s wife and children. If one’s own person is not well ordered, how can one bring order to the people of the state? This follows both from principle and from the circumstances of things.

The gentleman knows that his own person is the root of his dealings with all people and things under Heaven. Thus he does not busy himself with other affairs, but regards enriching himself through virtue as urgent. This certainly does not mean that he wishes merely to perfect himself alone: he knows that the root lies here, and here too lies what he must pursue. He does not anxiously chase other tasks, but sets his mind solely on enriching himself through virtue. Nor does this mean that he wishes to forget the world…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
知所急者在此而所學亦在此也春絃夏
誦學非不勤也無非爲潤身而設左詩右
書學非不富也罔非爲潤身而謀於大學
而學焉必知脩身爲本而格致誠正之功
無少忽於中庸而學焉必知誠身爲本而
博審愼篤之力無少息學於易以求潤身
於時學於書以求潤身於中學於詩禮春
秋以求潤身於正於敬義不敢以貪爲學
懼其侈吾身而泛也不敢以固爲學懼其
===
迂吾身而僻也不敢以傲爲學懼其卓鶩
吾身而孤也不敢以夸爲學懼其猖獗吾
身而惰也盤有銘几有誡將以潤吾身也
左準繩右規矩將以潤此身也襲絅於錦
闇然日章芟茅於徑介然成路將以潤此
身也曾子曰心廣體胖孟子曰睟面盎背
君子有之矣由是推吾潤身者以潤家推
吾潤身者以潤國推吾潤身者以潤天下
使人由其誠教人盡其材其施之也不悖
punctuated: 知所急者在此，而所學亦在此也。春絃夏誦，學非不勤也，無非爲潤身而設；左詩右書，學非不富也，罔非爲潤身而謀。於《大學》而學焉，必知脩身爲本，而格致誠正之功無少忽；於《中庸》而學焉，必知誠身爲本，而博審愼篤之力無少息。學於《易》，以求潤身於時；學於《書》，以求潤身於中；學於《詩》《禮》《春秋》，以求潤身於正、於敬義。不敢以貪爲學，懼其侈吾身而泛也；不敢以固爲學，懼其迂吾身而僻也；不敢以傲爲學，懼其卓鶩吾身而孤也；不敢以夸爲學，懼其猖獗吾身而惰也。盤有銘，几有誡，將以潤吾身也；左準繩，右規矩，將以潤此身也；襲絅於錦，闇然日章，芟茅於徑，介然成路，將以潤此身也。曾子曰：「心廣體胖。」孟子曰：「睟面盎背。」君子有之矣。由是推吾潤身者以潤家，推吾潤身者以潤國，推吾潤身者以潤天下，使人由其誠，教人盡其材，其施之也不悖，
translation_en: …He knows that what is urgent lies here, and his learning is likewise directed here. Playing the strings in spring and reciting in summer, he is certainly diligent in learning; all this is undertaken to enrich his person through virtue. With the Odes on his left and the Documents on his right, his learning is certainly abundant; all this is planned to enrich his person. In studying the Great Learning, he must recognize cultivation of the person as the root, never neglecting the work of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind. In studying the Doctrine of the Mean, he must recognize making his person sincere as the root, never relaxing his efforts at broad learning, searching inquiry, careful reflection, and earnest practice. He studies the Changes to enrich his person through acting appropriately to the time; he studies the Documents to enrich his person through holding to the mean; he studies the Odes, the Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals to enrich his person through rectitude, reverence, and righteousness. He dares not make acquisitiveness his manner of learning, fearing that it would make him extravagant and unfocused. He dares not make rigidity his manner of learning, fearing that it would make him impractical and narrow. He dares not make arrogance his manner of learning, fearing that it would make him aspire to stand above others [?] and become isolated. He dares not make boastfulness his manner of learning, fearing that it would make him unruly and indolent. Inscriptions on his basin and admonitions on his table are intended to enrich his person. The leveling instrument and inked line on his left, the compass and square on his right, are intended to enrich this person. Wearing a plain outer garment over brocade, remaining unobtrusive yet growing more manifest each day; clearing the grass from a footpath so that a narrow way becomes passable—all this is intended to enrich this person. Zengzi said, “The mind is expansive and the body at ease.” Mengzi said, “It shines clearly in the face and fills out the back.” The gentleman possesses these qualities. From this he extends what enriches his own person to enrich his family, extends it to enrich the state, and extends it to enrich all under Heaven. He enables people to follow their sincerity and teaches them to develop their abilities fully. In applying this, he does not act contrary to what is right…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
其求之也不拂源泉混混有本者固如是
乎嗚呼學之道有末有本末達之天下國
家本係於一人之身使身不潤抑亦末矣
本之則無如之何多聞適以爲泛博學適
以爲僻求之愈峻適以爲孫造之愈深適
以爲惟一學之加一道之累也一事之窮
一本之失也安於自肆難於自檢趨道之
名而自逸於形器之外取學之末而自淪
於妄誕之歸無惟乎致遠則泥矣雖然君
===
子所務之本其義甚大在易謂之元在春
秋謂之一在子思謂之大本在仲舒謂之
大始邵堯夫以内聖外王之學爲抑末反
本之論其知此義矣不然演河圖何以以
中五爲本制圓圖何以以天根爲言愚於
此又有以知堯夫知本之本焉因併及之
同前
遵貢
同考試官教諭張　批〔此作議論精切筆勢雄健〕
punctuated:
其求之也不拂。源泉混混，有本者固如是乎！嗚呼！學之道有末有本，末達之天下國家，本係於一人之身。使身不潤，抑亦末矣。本之，則無如之何。多聞適以爲泛，博學適以爲僻；求之愈峻，適以爲孫；造之愈深，適以爲惟。一學之加，一道之累也；一事之窮，一本之失也。安於自肆，難於自檢，趨道之名，而自逸於形器之外；取學之末，而自淪於妄誕之歸。無惟乎致遠則泥矣！雖然，君子所務之本，其義甚大。在《易》謂之元，在《春秋》謂之一，在子思謂之大本，在仲舒謂之大始。邵堯夫以内聖外王之學爲抑末反本之論，其知此義矣。不然，演河圖，何以以中五爲本？制圓圖，何以以天根爲言？愚於此又有以知堯夫知本之本焉，因併及之。
同前。
遵貢。
同考試官教諭張，批〔此作議論精切，筆勢雄健。〕
translation_en:
…and what one seeks does not run counter to it. A spring flows ceaselessly: surely this is how it is with those who have a root! Alas! The way of learning has branches and a root. Its branches extend to all under Heaven, the state, and the family; its root rests in the individual person. If learning fails to enrich one's person, it too amounts merely to branches. As for establishing its root, nothing can then be done. Hearing much serves only to make one diffuse; broad learning serves only to make one deviate. The loftier one's seeking, the more it leads to withdrawal [?]; the deeper one's attainment, the more it leads to mere pondering [?]. Each addition to one's learning becomes another encumbrance upon the Way; each matter investigated to the utmost becomes another loss of the root. At ease in self-indulgence but finding self-restraint difficult, one pursues the name of the Way while letting oneself wander beyond concrete forms and objects. Grasping the branches of learning, one sinks into delusion and absurdity. Is it any wonder [?] that, when attempting to reach far, one becomes bogged down?
Nevertheless, the root to which the gentleman devotes himself has profound significance. In the Book of Changes it is called the Primal; in the Spring and Autumn Annals it is called the One; Zisi calls it the Great Root; Zhongshu calls it the Great Beginning. Shao Yaofu, through his learning of inward sagehood and outward kingship, advanced the argument for curbing the branches and returning to the root. Surely he understood this meaning! Otherwise, when expounding the River Chart, why did he take the central five as its root? When making the Circular Diagram, why did he speak of the Root of Heaven? From this I, in my humble judgment, have further grounds to recognize that Yaofu understood the root of the root; hence I mention it here as well.
Same as above.
Zun Gong [?].
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition's argument is incisive and apt, and its writing vigorous and powerful.〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
博而約達而實其論場之巨擘歟
考試官教諭張　批〔論得邵子意且筆勢圓活滔滔　不滯讀之令人起敬〕
考試官教諭李　批〔意經學醫俗　而諸條特之作〕
善為學者不于其末而于其本焉學不可
以不知本也學知所本則為己而不為人
務內而不務外其所學也大矣若不究其
本而惟末是圖則為人矣為人而學將何
以有成哉善學君子所以致嚴於此而學
===
以潤身為本焉學本潤身則知所以為己
而積中發外之盛自有不可遏者彼治人
應物君子何暇為哉然亦非故置人物於
度外也蓋以治己為重而治人在所輕治
己為急而應物在所緩况吾之學能潤身
則治人應物特舉而措之耳噫學以潤身
為本此君子所以為善學者歟請因邵子
之言而論之人之生也五行之秀鍾之二
氣之精孕之其體則天地之塞其性則天
punctuated:
博而約，達而實，其論場之巨擘歟！
考試官教諭張　批〔論得邵子意，且筆勢圓活，滔滔不滯，讀之令人起敬。〕
考試官教諭李　批〔意經學醫俗，而諸條特之作。〕
善為學者，不于其末而于其本焉。學不可以不知本也。學知所本，則為己而不為人，務內而不務外，其所學也大矣。若不究其本，而惟末是圖，則為人矣。為人而學，將何以有成哉？善學君子所以致嚴於此，而學以潤身為本焉。學本潤身，則知所以為己，而積中發外之盛，自有不可遏者。彼治人應物，君子何暇為哉？然亦非故置人物於度外也。蓋以治己為重，而治人在所輕；治己為急，而應物在所緩。况吾之學能潤身，則治人應物，特舉而措之耳。噫！學以潤身為本，此君子所以為善學者歟！請因邵子之言而論之。人之生也，五行之秀鍾之，二氣之精孕之。其體則天地之塞，其性則天
translation_en:
…Broad yet concise, penetrating yet substantial: surely he is a master in the field of discourse!

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The argument captures Master Shao’s meaning. Moreover, the writing is fluent and lively, flowing freely without obstruction; reading it inspires respect.〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Its purport concerns classical learning and remedies vulgarity [?]; an exceptional composition in its various points [?].〕

Those who learn well attend to learning’s root rather than its branches. In learning, one must know the root. When learners know what to take as their foundation, they learn for their own cultivation rather than for others’ approval, attending to the inward rather than the outward: great indeed is their learning. If they fail to investigate the root and pursue only the branches, they learn for others’ approval. How can learning for others’ approval lead to accomplishment? This is why the gentleman who learns well is so exacting on this point and takes the enrichment of his own person as the foundation of learning. When learning rests on enriching one’s person, one knows how to cultivate oneself, and the abundant virtue accumulated within and manifested outwardly naturally becomes impossible to restrain. As for governing others and responding to external affairs, what leisure does the gentleman have for these? Yet neither does he deliberately put people and affairs beyond his concern. Rather, he regards governing himself as weighty and governing others as relatively light; governing himself is urgent, while responding to affairs can wait. Moreover, if our learning can enrich our own persons, governing others and responding to affairs require only that we put it into practice. Ah! Taking the enrichment of one’s person as the foundation of learning—is this not what makes the gentleman a good learner? Let me discuss this on the basis of Master Shao’s words. At a human being’s birth, the finest qualities of the Five Phases converge in him, and the essences of the two vital forces give him life. His bodily substance is that which fills Heaven and Earth; his nature is Heaven’s…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
地之帥四端備焉萬善具焉吾身本自潤
也何待於學以潤其身乎殊不知氣稟拘
於有生之初物欲蔽於有生之後天賦我
以性而我情之天形我以人而我物之是
以我之得於天者始有不全天之畀於我
者容有不盡伊欲全之盡之其道柰何亦
曰學之焉耳世之人非惟不知夫學學而
亦不知其本不詞章其學則功名其學不
功名其學則空虛其學詞章之學綴緝文
彩之語記誦奥僻之書果足以潤身乎功
名之學從事於術數刑名留心於權謀縱
橫果足以潤身乎空虛之學溺於虛而不
求其實惑於無而不求其有又豈足以潤
身乎君子之學非此之學也反之於吾身
求之於性分惟以潤身為本耳我思古人
從事四勿顏子之學以潤身為本也故所
立卓爾具體而微顏之學有以潤其身矣
日加三省曾子之學以潤身為本也故得
punctuated: 地之帥，四端備焉，萬善具焉，吾身本自潤也，何待於學以潤其身乎？殊不知氣稟拘於有生之初，物欲蔽於有生之後。天賦我以性，而我情之；天形我以人，而我物之。是以我之得於天者始有不全，天之畀於我者容有不盡。伊欲全之盡之，其道柰何？亦曰學之焉耳。世之人非惟不知夫學，學而亦不知其本。不詞章其學，則功名其學；不功名其學，則空虛其學。詞章之學，綴緝文彩之語，記誦奥僻之書，果足以潤身乎？功名之學，從事於術數刑名，留心於權謀縱橫，果足以潤身乎？空虛之學，溺於虛而不求其實，惑於無而不求其有，又豈足以潤身乎？君子之學，非此之學也。反之於吾身，求之於性分，惟以潤身為本耳。我思古人，從事四勿，顏子之學以潤身為本也，故所立卓爾，具體而微，顏之學有以潤其身矣。日加三省，曾子之學以潤身為本也，故得
translation_en:
…the commander of Heaven and Earth. The four moral beginnings are all present within us, and every goodness is complete. Our persons are originally enriched in themselves: why should we need learning to enrich them? Yet this overlooks how our endowment of vital energy constrains us from the beginning of life, and how material desires obscure us thereafter. Heaven endows me with a moral nature, yet I turn it into mere feelings; Heaven gives me human form, yet I make myself a mere thing. Thus what I have received from Heaven comes to be impaired, and what Heaven has bestowed upon me may remain incompletely realized. If we wish to preserve it whole and realize it fully, what way is there? The answer is simply to learn.

People in the world not only fail to understand learning; even when they learn, they fail to understand its foundation. If their learning is not devoted to literary composition, it is devoted to achievement and fame; if not to achievement and fame, then to emptiness. Learning devoted to literary composition strings together ornate phrases and memorizes obscure books: can it truly enrich the person? Learning devoted to achievement and fame concerns itself with techniques of control and the matching of performance to official designation, and attends to stratagems and diplomatic maneuvering: can it truly enrich the person? Learning devoted to emptiness becomes immersed in the insubstantial without seeking what is substantial, and is deluded by nonbeing without seeking what exists: how could it enrich the person? The gentleman’s learning is none of these. He turns back to his own person and seeks within his allotted moral nature, taking the enrichment of his person alone as his foundation.

I think of the ancients. Master Yan devoted himself to the four prohibitions: his learning took the enrichment of his person as its foundation. Thus what he established stood lofty, and he embodied the whole, though on a smaller scale. Yan’s learning indeed served to enrich his person. Master Zeng examined himself daily on three counts: his learning took the enrichment of his person as its foundation. Thus he was able to…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
闡一貫心廣體胖曾之學有以潤其身矣
知言養氣孟子之學以潤身為本也故充
塞天地睟面盎背孟之學有以潤其身矣
聖賢之學皆以潤身為本故能為天地立
心為生民立命為萬世開太平其事業耿
耿不磨何莫不自潤身中來耶君子以聖
賢為標的以潤身為根本仁義可以潤身
也吾則於仁義而學焉禮智可以潤身也
吾則於禮智而學焉必格物必致知學之
===
不已其功必誠意必正心學之不怠其力
以誠敬為入門以踐履為實地不忠不信
不習日學曾子之三省勿視勿聽勿言勿
動日學顏子之四勿窮理盡性學孟氏之
知言直養無害學孟氏之養氣道理無往
而不在君子無往而不學非為人也非
為應物也惟欲以潤身為本焉但見欲淨
而理還人泯而天定非念不足以喪其所
養外物不足以奪其所守心與理融理與
punctuated: 闡一貫，心廣體胖，曾之學有以潤其身矣。知言養氣，孟子之學以潤身為本也，故充塞天地，睟面盎背，孟之學有以潤其身矣。聖賢之學皆以潤身為本，故能為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平。其事業耿耿不磨，何莫不自潤身中來耶？君子以聖賢為標的，以潤身為根本。仁義可以潤身也，吾則於仁義而學焉；禮智可以潤身也，吾則於禮智而學焉。必格物，必致知，學之不已其功；必誠意，必正心，學之不怠其力。以誠敬為入門，以踐履為實地。不忠、不信、不習，日學曾子之三省；勿視、勿聽、勿言、勿動，日學顏子之四勿。窮理盡性，學孟氏之知言；直養無害，學孟氏之養氣。道理無往而不在，君子無往而不學。非為人也，非為應物也，惟欲以潤身為本焉。但見欲淨而理還，人泯而天定，非念不足以喪其所養，外物不足以奪其所守。心與理融，理與
translation_en:
…to elucidate the single thread running through the Way, his mind became expansive and his body at ease: Zengzi’s learning thus enriched his person. Understanding words and nourishing vital energy, Mengzi took enriching his person as the foundation of learning. Thus his vital energy filled Heaven and Earth, and his virtue shone in his face and suffused his back: Mengzi’s learning thus enriched his person.

The learning of sages and worthies all takes enriching the person as its foundation. Thus they could establish a mind for Heaven and Earth, establish a destiny for the people, and inaugurate Great Peace for ten thousand generations. Their achievements shine undimmed: which of them did not arise from enriching the person? The gentleman takes the sages and worthies as his standard and enriching his person as his foundation. Benevolence and righteousness can enrich the person, so I devote myself to learning benevolence and righteousness; ritual propriety and wisdom can enrich the person, so I devote myself to learning ritual propriety and wisdom. One must investigate things and extend knowledge, never ceasing one’s efforts in learning; one must make one’s intentions sincere and rectify one’s mind, never slackening one’s exertions in learning. Sincerity and reverence provide the entryway, and putting learning into practice provides firm ground.

In considering whether one has failed in loyalty, failed in trustworthiness, or failed to practice what one has learned, one daily follows Zengzi’s three self-examinations. In refraining from looking, listening, speaking, or acting contrary to ritual propriety, one daily follows Yanzi’s four prohibitions. By fathoming principle and fully realizing one’s nature, one learns Mengzi’s understanding of words; by nourishing vital energy with uprightness and doing it no injury, one learns Mengzi’s cultivation of vital energy. There is nowhere that the principles of the Way are absent, and nowhere that the gentleman does not learn. He does this neither for others nor to respond to external things; his sole wish is to take enriching his person as the foundation. Then one sees desires cleared away and principle restored, human desires effaced and Heaven’s order established. Errant thoughts cannot destroy what he has nurtured, and external things cannot wrest away what he holds fast. The mind merges with principle, and principle with…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
心會仁義根於心其發見自不可禦禮智
本於內其生色自不可遏包含徧覆無所
不愛其氣象一春風和氣之可挹仁之潤
身何如耶稱量裁度無所不宜其氣象一
秋霜烈日之可畏義之潤身何如耶左準
繩右規矩肅肅乎其威儀禮之英華發越
不其潤身乎判是非別邪正昭昭乎其藻
鑑智之光彩旁燭不其潤身乎仰不愧俯
不怍從容自得於鳶飛魚躍之天動靜何
===
舒泰也無人非無鬼責優游自適於光風
霽月之鄉襟懷何灑落也飲水甘於列鼎
不願乎人之膏粱縕袍華於珮玉不願乎
人之文繡君子之學至於潤身如此始不
負其所期不負其所學矣其即顏子具體
而微之日曾子心廣體胖之時孟子睟面
盎背之境也由是推無不準動無不化內
焉而家則家無不齊所以潤其家者此也
外焉而國則國無不治所以潤其國者此
punctuated: 心會。仁義根於心，其發見自不可禦；禮智本於內，其生色自不可遏。包含徧覆，無所不愛，其氣象一春風和氣之可挹，仁之潤身何如耶？稱量裁度，無所不宜，其氣象一秋霜烈日之可畏，義之潤身何如耶？左準繩，右規矩，肅肅乎其威儀，禮之英華發越，不其潤身乎？判是非，別邪正，昭昭乎其藻鑑，智之光彩旁燭，不其潤身乎？仰不愧，俯不怍，從容自得於鳶飛魚躍之天，動靜何舒泰也！無人非，無鬼責，優游自適於光風霽月之鄉，襟懷何灑落也！飲水甘於列鼎，不願乎人之膏粱；縕袍華於珮玉，不願乎人之文繡。君子之學至於潤身如此，始不負其所期，不負其所學矣。其即顏子具體而微之日，曾子心廣體胖之時，孟子睟面盎背之境也。由是推無不準，動無不化。內焉而家，則家無不齊，所以潤其家者此也；外焉而國，則國無不治，所以潤其國者此
translation_en:
…and principle accords with the heart. Benevolence and righteousness take root in the heart, and their manifestation cannot be checked; ritual propriety and wisdom are grounded within, and their expression in the countenance cannot be restrained. Embracing and sheltering all, leaving nothing unloved, one has a presence like a spring breeze whose gentle warmth may be savored. How richly does benevolence grace the person! Weighing and judging, making every determination fitting, one has a presence as awe-inspiring as autumn frost or the blazing sun. How richly does righteousness grace the person! With level and marking line to the left, compass and square to the right, how solemn is one's dignified bearing! The flowering of ritual propriety shines forth: does it not grace the person? Distinguishing right from wrong and separating the deviant from the correct, how clear is one's discerning judgment! The radiance of wisdom illuminates all around: does it not grace the person?

Looking up without shame, looking down without embarrassment, one is composed and content beneath the heavens where kites fly and fish leap. How relaxed and at ease in movement and stillness! With no human censure and no reproach from spirits, one wanders freely and contentedly in a realm of clear breezes and a moon shining after rain. How open and unencumbered is one's heart! Plain drinking water tastes sweeter than a banquet arrayed in cauldrons; one does not covet others' rich fare. A padded hemp robe seems more splendid than jade pendants; one does not covet others' embroidered finery. Only when the gentleman's learning graces his person in this way does he fulfill his aspirations and do justice to what he has learned. This is precisely Yanzi's attainment of the whole substance of sagehood on a smaller scale, Zengzi's state of a broadened heart and a body at ease, and Mengzi's condition in which virtue shines in the face and fills out the back.

Extending from this, every application accords with the proper standard, and every action brings transformation. Inwardly, within the family, no household fails to be well ordered: this is what graces the family. Outwardly, within the state, no state fails to be well governed: what graces the state is this…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也遠而天下則天下無不平所以潤天下
者亦此也所謂盡人之性而盡物之性者
在是所謂贊天地之化育而與天地參者
在是是則君子潤身之學乃有用之實學
學之知其本者也視彼世之專事詞章與
夫功名空虛以為學者非惟不足以潤身
且不足以治人非惟不足以裕己且不足
以應物其於脩己治人應物之道胥失之
矣若是者謂之學且不可況可謂之善學
乎君子之學與此蓋天淵矣慨自世道湮
微聖賢潤身之學寥寥絕倡久矣不有先
覺孰啓我人君子之學以潤身為本誠千
萬世學者之指南歟論而至是則知同一
學也內外人己之分君子小人判焉務內
而為己則為君子而可以為聖為賢務外
而為人則為小人而流於愚不肖始雖相
近而終則相遠所謂毫釐之差千里之繆
者也後之學者尚當致謹於內外人己之
punctuated: 也。遠而天下，則天下無不平，所以潤天下者亦此也。所謂盡人之性而盡物之性者在是，所謂贊天地之化育而與天地參者在是。是則君子潤身之學，乃有用之實學，學之知其本者也。視彼世之專事詞章與夫功名空虛以為學者，非惟不足以潤身，且不足以治人；非惟不足以裕己，且不足以應物。其於脩己治人應物之道，胥失之矣。若是者，謂之學且不可，況可謂之善學乎？君子之學與此，蓋天淵矣。慨自世道湮微，聖賢潤身之學寥寥絕倡久矣。不有先覺，孰啓我人？君子之學以潤身為本，誠千萬世學者之指南歟！論而至是，則知同一學也，內外人己之分，君子小人判焉。務內而為己，則為君子，而可以為聖為賢；務外而為人，則為小人，而流於愚不肖。始雖相近，而終則相遠，所謂毫釐之差，千里之繆者也。後之學者，尚當致謹於內外人己之
translation_en:
…this is so. Extending farther to all under Heaven, none would fail to be brought to peace; this too is how one enriches all under Heaven. Herein lies what is meant by fully realizing human nature and thereby fully realizing the nature of things; herein lies what is meant by assisting Heaven and Earth in their transforming and nourishing work and forming a triad with them. Thus the gentleman’s learning that enriches his person is substantive learning with practical use: learning that recognizes its root. Consider those in the world who take exclusive devotion to literary composition and the hollow pursuit of achievement and fame to constitute learning. Not only is this insufficient to enrich their persons; it is also insufficient to govern others. Not only is it insufficient to bring fullness to themselves; it is also insufficient to respond to things. They have altogether lost the Way of cultivating oneself, governing others, and responding to things. Such pursuits cannot even be called learning; how much less can they be called learning well? The gentleman’s learning is as far removed from this as Heaven is from the depths.

Alas, since the Way in the world fell into obscurity and decline, the learning of the sages and worthies that enriches the person has long had scarcely anyone to champion it. Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten us? That the gentleman’s learning takes enriching the person as its foundation is truly a guide for learners through countless generations! Having carried the discussion this far, we understand that, although both are called learning, the distinction between inward and outward concerns, between learning for others and learning for oneself, separates the gentleman from the petty man. Attending to what is within and learning for oneself makes one a gentleman, capable of becoming a sage or worthy; attending to what is outward and learning for others’ approval makes one a petty man, sinking into folly and unworthiness. Though close at the outset, they end far apart. This is what is meant by a discrepancy of a hair’s breadth leading to an error of a thousand li. Learners in later generations should therefore exercise the utmost care regarding the distinction between inward and outward concerns, between learning for others and learning for oneself…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
間而致嚴於君子小人之戒為之柰何亦
曰學以潤身為本
表
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表
刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔得駢儷體〕
同考試官教諭等　批〔典雅〕
考試官教諭張　批〔典則可觀〕
考試官教諭李　批〔亲佳〕
===
伏以
神兵會府任隆翊賛之司天極環樞職專
靖密之寄班序近聯於三省事權高出於
六卿
禮遇同宰相之榮地分極人臣之貴非全材
如伊呂負荷奚堪必碩望若甫申登庸庶
稱顧兹
特授未遂堅辭竊念臣必大早歲孤窮爰鞠
母氏中年强學輒忝詞科偶受知於
punctuated:
間，而致嚴於君子小人之戒。為之柰何？亦曰：學以潤身為本。

表
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表
刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊，批〔得駢儷體〕。
同考試官教諭等，批〔典雅〕。
考試官教諭張，批〔典則可觀〕。
考試官教諭李，批〔亲佳〕。

伏以，神兵會府，任隆翊賛之司；天極環樞，職專靖密之寄。班序近聯於三省，事權高出於六卿。禮遇同宰相之榮，地分極人臣之貴。非全材如伊呂，負荷奚堪？必碩望若甫申，登庸庶稱。顧兹特授，未遂堅辭。竊念臣必大，早歲孤窮，爰鞠母氏；中年强學，輒忝詞科。偶受知於
translation_en:
…between these, and strictly heed the warning concerning the distinction between the gentleman and the petty man. How is this to be done? Simply put: learning must take the cultivation of oneself as its foundation.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the Song appointment of Zhou Bida as Military Affairs Commissioner
By Diao Yu
Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Achieves the parallel-prose style.〕
The Associate Examiners, Instructors and others, comment: 〔Classical and elegant.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Classically correct and worthy of appreciation.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“Intimate and fine” [?].〕

I humbly observe: the council in which the imperial forces are brought together bears the weighty responsibility of assisting the throne; like the pivot around which the celestial pole turns, its office is entrusted specifically with maintaining tranquillity and handling confidential affairs. Its place in the official hierarchy closely adjoins the Three Departments; its authority over affairs stands high above the Six Ministers. Its ceremonial treatment equals the honors accorded a Grand Councilor, and its standing reaches the highest distinction attainable by a subject. Without comprehensive talents like those of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, how could one bear this burden? Only with an outstanding reputation like that of the lords of Fu and Shen might one prove worthy of appointment. Yet this special appointment has been bestowed upon me, and my firm attempts to decline it have not succeeded.

I reflect that I, your servant Bida, lost my father and lived in poverty in my early years, nurtured by my mother [?]. In middle life I applied myself diligently to learning and undeservedly succeeded in the literary examination. By chance, I received recognition from …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
先朝爲堪掌制辛逍逢乎
昌運進侍
經筵應
詔陳謨頗切救時之弊講和索禮敢正敵國之
名既因事而請祠薦收録而捕外
召還翰苑前後幾及六年逆犯
龍鱗包容未至三黜論事本原於愚直蒙
恩殊出於尋常甫與知乎兵機遽正位於温省
制詞寛大誤重忠勞之
===
褒
天語丁寧豫隆宣撫之託
眷非意及愧與憂幷兹葢伏遇
○○○○
聰明神授
英毅天成
握符奮起於外藩受
命入承乎大統小心契周文之翼翼大孝符虞
舜之蘷蘷莚寀邇之天聰謹在兹之日監
punctuated: 先朝，爲堪掌制，辛逍逢乎昌運，進侍經筵。應詔陳謨，頗切救時之弊；講和索禮，敢正敵國之名。既因事而請祠，薦收録而捕外。召還翰苑，前後幾及六年；逆犯龍鱗，包容未至三黜。論事本原於愚直，蒙恩殊出於尋常。甫與知乎兵機，遽正位於温省。制詞寛大，誤重忠勞之褒；天語丁寧，豫隆宣撫之託。眷非意及，愧與憂幷。兹葢伏遇○○○○，聰明神授，英毅天成。握符奮起於外藩，受命入承乎大統。小心契周文之翼翼，大孝符虞舜之蘷蘷。莚寀邇之天聰，謹在兹之日監，
translation_en:
…under the former sovereign, I was deemed fit to draft imperial decrees. Fortunately encountering a flourishing reign [?], I advanced to attend the Classics Colloquium. In response to an imperial edict, I presented proposals earnestly directed toward remedying the evils of the age. In negotiating peace and seeking proper ceremonial treatment, I ventured to insist upon the designation of the opposing state as an equal. Subsequently, on account of an affair, I requested a temple sinecure; I was again taken into service and appointed outside the capital [?]. Recalled to the Hanlin Academy, I served there for nearly six years in all. Though I incurred imperial wrath by offending the dragon’s scales, Your Majesty’s forbearance spared me a third dismissal. My discussions of affairs sprang from simple-minded candor, yet the favor I received far exceeded the ordinary. Having only just begun to participate in military deliberations, I was abruptly installed in the chief position in the Secretariat [?]. The decree’s wording was generous, mistakenly lavishing praise upon my loyalty and service; Your Majesty’s earnest words placed great weight in advance upon the charge of military pacification. Such favor exceeded anything I had imagined, and shame mingles with anxiety.
This, I humbly recognize, is because I have encountered ○○○○: Your Majesty’s intelligence is divinely bestowed, and your heroic resolution is innate. Bearing the token of authority, you rose from a princely domain outside the capital; receiving the mandate, you entered the court to succeed to the imperial line. Your circumspection accords with the reverent care of King Wen of Zhou; your great filial devotion matches the solemn reverence of Shun of Yu. You extend your imperial hearing to those near you [?], keeping vigilant watch daily over what lies here before you…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
兩宮齊壽
帝心允恊予太和三載終喪
乾斷不揺於羣議思開拓而鋭志恢復念艱
難而留意守成攺稱謂以挫敵驕減歳幣
以定鄰好雖金人無可乘之釁而
皇朝有不戰之威猶以訓兵當謹於無形雪耻
終期於有待遂令重寄猥及非才圖籍周
知素乏曾宣靖之先見號令明審敢希王
文定之後塵力願竭於疲駑行恐儕于跛
鼈私憂過計不以治而忘危養鋭蓄威將
以全而取勝仰資
廟筭冀荅
鴻休伏願
王靈丕振於華夷
聖武布昭於遐邇
天戈遠指行見中原之肅清露布遥馳佇聽邉
塵之蕩掃〔臣必大〕無任瞻
天仰
punctuated:
兩宮齊壽，帝心允恊予太和；三載終喪，乾斷不揺於羣議。思開拓而鋭志恢復，念艱難而留意守成。攺稱謂以挫敵驕，減歳幣以定鄰好。雖金人無可乘之釁，而皇朝有不戰之威。猶以訓兵當謹於無形，雪耻終期於有待，遂令重寄猥及非才。圖籍周知，素乏曾宣靖之先見；號令明審，敢希王文定之後塵？力願竭於疲駑，行恐儕于跛鼈。私憂過計，不以治而忘危；養鋭蓄威，將以全而取勝。仰資廟筭，冀荅鴻休。
伏願王靈丕振於華夷，聖武布昭於遐邇。天戈遠指，行見中原之肅清；露布遥馳，佇聽邉塵之蕩掃。〔臣必大〕無任瞻天仰
translation_en:
…The two palace elders alike enjoy longevity, and Your Majesty’s heart accords fully with supreme harmony [?]. You completed the three years of mourning, your sovereign resolve unshaken by the many contrary opinions. Thinking of expanding the realm, you set your determination upon recovering lost territory; mindful of difficulties, you devote attention to preserving what has been achieved. You changed the forms of address to curb the enemy’s arrogance and reduced the annual tribute payments to secure friendly relations with our neighbor. Although the Jin offer no opening to exploit, our imperial dynasty commands awe without fighting. Yet you consider that troops must be trained diligently before danger takes shape, and that avenging our humiliation must ultimately await the right moment. Thus this weighty charge has undeservedly fallen upon one without talent.
In comprehensive knowledge of maps and records, I have always lacked the foresight of Zeng Xuanjing; in the clarity and judiciousness of commands, dare I hope to follow in Wang Wending’s footsteps? I wish to exhaust the strength of this weary, inferior horse, yet fear that my progress will match a lame turtle’s. In my private apprehension and anxious deliberation, I shall not forget danger amid good order. I shall nurture our fighting strength and build up our military might, seeking victory with our forces intact. Looking up for guidance to the court’s strategic counsels, I hope to requite your great favor.
I humbly wish that your sovereign might may resound magnificently among the Chinese and the foreign peoples, and that your sagely martial prowess may shine forth far and near. When the celestial spears point into the distance, we shall soon see the Central Plain pacified; when proclamations of victory speed from afar, we shall eagerly hear that the dust of frontier warfare has been swept away. 〔Your servant Bida〕 cannot contain his feelings as he gazes up at Heaven and looks reverently toward…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官訓導陸　批〔家傳人誦之書能條陳者亦〕
表擯
===
〔少惟此篇隨問隨對其熟於〕
〔當代制作者乎是用錄出〕
考試官教諭張　批〔條答詳明考據博通之士也〕
考試官教諭李　批〔數答詳明具有筆力〕
前聖迭興而治教之典已著後聖繼作而
治教之典益明蓋天能賦民以性而不能
使之全其性聖人者出任君師之大責爲
天民之先覺則其所以治而教之者當必
有道焉且又筆之於書以垂教後世先聖
punctuated:
聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場，策，第一問。
同考試官訓導陸批〔家傳人誦之書，能條陳者亦〕表擯〔少。惟此篇隨問隨對，其熟於〕〔當代制作者乎？是用錄出。〕
考試官教諭張批〔條答詳明，考據博通之士也。〕
考試官教諭李批〔數答詳明，具有筆力。〕
前聖迭興，而治教之典已著；後聖繼作，而治教之典益明。蓋天能賦民以性，而不能使之全其性。聖人者出，任君師之大責，爲天民之先覺，則其所以治而教之者，當必有道焉。且又筆之於書，以垂教後世。先聖
translation_en:
…toward Your Sagely Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling apprehension, I respectfully submit this memorial of thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session: Policy Essay, Question One.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor: “These writings are handed down in every household and recited by everyone, yet few can set out their contents systematically. This essay alone answers each question in turn. Might its author be thoroughly familiar with the institutions established by the present dynasty? It is therefore selected for inclusion.” [The intervening text 表擯 is unclear: ?]
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The answers are detailed and clear, revealing a scholar with broad mastery of textual evidence.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The several answers are detailed and clear, all displaying forceful writing.”
As the earlier sages arose in succession, the canons of government and instruction were already set forth; as later sages continued their work, those canons became still clearer. Heaven can endow the people with their nature, but cannot make them fully realize it. When a sage emerges, he assumes the great responsibility of ruler and teacher and becomes the first among Heaven’s people to attain understanding. There must therefore be a Way by which he governs and instructs them. Moreover, he commits it to writing to transmit instruction to later generations. The earlier sages…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
後聖其揆一也愚請為執事陳之天命之
謂性率性之謂道性則仁義禮智信是也
道則君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友五者之大
倫是也斯民之所以羣聚而不亂者以其
全此性由此道而各有倫序焉耳聚而無
倫則亂矣傳曰一失則為夷狄再失則為
禽獸此古今聖王之治天下所以雖有百
度萬幾之多而必以敦倫為之本也舍此
而求治教之具蓋亦遠且難矣稽之於經
若堯之親睦九族舜之慎徽五典湯之肇
脩人紀武王之重民五教其所以治教當
時者蓋可見矣洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝膺天明命肇造區夏條成大誥三
編
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒御製孝順事實以為善陰
騭二書
宣宗章皇帝繼志述事纘述五倫之書頒示天
下無非所以敦五倫以盡君師之責者斯
punctuated:
後聖，其揆一也。愚請為執事陳之：天命之謂性，率性之謂道。性則仁義禮智信是也，道則君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友五者之大倫是也。斯民之所以羣聚而不亂者，以其全此性、由此道，而各有倫序焉耳。聚而無倫，則亂矣。傳曰：「一失則為夷狄，再失則為禽獸。」此古今聖王之治天下，所以雖有百度萬幾之多，而必以敦倫為之本也。舍此而求治教之具，蓋亦遠且難矣。稽之於經，若堯之親睦九族、舜之慎徽五典、湯之肇脩人紀、武王之重民五教，其所以治教當時者，蓋可見矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天明命，肇造區夏，條成《大誥》三編。太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，御製《孝順事實》以《為善陰騭》二書。宣宗章皇帝繼志述事，纘述五倫之書，頒示天下，無非所以敦五倫，以盡君師之責者。斯
translation_en:
…and later sages shared the same standard. I venture to set this out for you, honored officials: what Heaven ordains is called human nature; following that nature is called the Way. Human nature consists of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness. The Way consists of the five cardinal human relationships: ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend. The people can live together without disorder because they preserve this nature intact and follow this Way, each maintaining the proper order of their relationships. If they gather without such relationships, disorder follows. The Commentary says: “Depart from them once, and one becomes a barbarian; depart from them again, and one becomes a bird or beast.” Thus, when the sage kings of antiquity and later ages governed the world, however numerous their institutions and myriad affairs, they invariably took strengthening human relationships as their foundation. To abandon this and seek the means of governing and teaching would surely be a roundabout and difficult undertaking. Examining the classics, we find Yao fostering affection and harmony among the nine degrees of kinship, Shun carefully promoting the five constant duties, Tang beginning to cultivate the ordering principles of human relationships, and King Wu attaching great importance to the five teachings for the people. From these examples, we can discern how they governed and taught in their times.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s illustrious mandate, founded his realm in the Chinese lands, and systematically compiled the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements. Emperor Taizong Wen continued the great imperial enterprise and personally composed the two books, True Accounts of Filial Obedience and [?] Doing Good and Hidden Virtue. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang carried forward his predecessors’ intentions and undertakings, compiled a book on the Five Relationships, and promulgated it throughout the realm. All these works served to strengthen the Five Relationships and thereby fulfill the responsibilities of ruler and teacher. This…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
世斯民家傳人誦服至教於忘言隆盛治
於千古其與堯舜湯武之治同符合轍誠
萬世不刊之盛典也迨我
英宗睿皇帝又有大明一統誌之頒其紀名宦
人物烈女之條蓋即
三誥三書之意欲人法之以敦五倫之重愚
嘗伏讀而知其說矣
大誥所載固多垂戒之事其所以戒之者蓋
欲使人之未敦五倫者有所警懼也如婚
姻之條有曰五倫先王之舊章民不知報
===
之章有曰去五教丟刑而民生者未之有
也所以五教育民之安其敦五倫之戒不
一而足也
陰騭書所載固多垂訓之事其所以訓之者
蓋欲使人之求敦五倫者有所矜式也如
載二徐成仙則言其忠君孝親同心爲善
載魏顆獲報則言其從治嫁妾以成父命
之類其敦五倫之訓不可悉舉也
punctuated:
世斯民，家傳人誦，服至教於忘言，隆盛治於千古，其與堯舜湯武之治同符合轍，誠萬世不刊之盛典也。迨我英宗睿皇帝，又有《大明一統誌》之頒，其紀名宦、人物、烈女之條，蓋即三誥三書之意，欲人法之，以敦五倫之重。愚嘗伏讀而知其說矣。
《大誥》所載，固多垂戒之事，其所以戒之者，蓋欲使人之未敦五倫者有所警懼也。如婚姻之條有曰：「五倫，先王之舊章。」民不知報之章有曰：「去五教丟刑而民生者，未之有也。」所以五教育民之安，其敦五倫之戒，不一而足也。
《陰騭書》所載，固多垂訓之事，其所以訓之者，蓋欲使人之求敦五倫者有所矜式也。如載二徐成仙，則言其忠君孝親，同心爲善；載魏顆獲報，則言其從治嫁妾，以成父命之類。其敦五倫之訓，不可悉舉也。
translation_en:
…the people of this age transmit these works in every household and recite them individually, embracing the highest teachings beyond the need for words and bringing flourishing government to a height unsurpassed through the ages. This accords perfectly with the government of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu; these are truly magnificent canons that shall stand unaltered for all time. In the reign of our Emperor Yingzong Rui, the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming was also promulgated. Its entries recording renowned officials, notable persons, and exemplary women embody the same intent as the three Admonitions and the three books: to have people follow their examples and give due weight to the Five Relationships. I have humbly read these works and come to understand their meaning.
The Great Admonition contains many accounts intended as warnings. Their purpose is to give those who have not upheld the Five Relationships cause for vigilance and fear. For example, the section on marriage states: “The Five Relationships are the established ordinances of the former kings.” The chapter “The People Do Not Know How to Repay” states: “Never have people survived when the Five Teachings were removed and punishments abandoned [?].” Thus the Five Teachings educate the people and secure their peace [?]; the warnings urging observance of the Five Relationships are too numerous to enumerate.
The Book of Hidden Virtue contains many accounts intended to impart instruction. Their purpose is to provide models for those seeking to uphold the Five Relationships. For example, in recording how the two Xu became immortals, it speaks of their loyalty to their ruler, their filial devotion to their parents, and their shared resolve to do good. In recording how Wei Ke received recompense, it speaks of his following the command his father gave while of sound mind and marrying off his father’s concubine, thereby fulfilling his father’s wishes. Its teachings urging observance of the Five Relationships cannot all be enumerated.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
孝順事實雖畢言孝也如紀考叔遺羹而感
君閔損孝母而及弟豈有不兼於餘倫者
乎
五倫書嘉言善行固備載五倫之事而獨詳
於君臣之倫者豈非以君臣為五倫之首
而治教之所關乎若夫
一統誌所載天下名宦人物烈女克盡五倫
之道者不可指數其在山東若大聖大賢
後先相望其道德高厚萬世景仰不可以
===
一方之人物觀者在所不必論矣兹以一
節之行有關於五倫最彰著者言之如王
祥之臥冰緹縈女之救父非敦於父子之
倫者乎廷式之娶瞽張義婦之歸夫骨非
敦於夫婦之倫者乎至如王蠋之不事二
君以盡臣節張公藝之九世同居以睦宗
族辛棄疾之往哭朱晦菴師友之義又何
如其克盡也之數人者皆有關乎五倫載
諸典籍昭耶乎最彰著者愚也幼而聞諸
punctuated:
《孝順事實》雖畢言孝也，如紀考叔遺羹而感君，閔損孝母而及弟，豈有不兼於餘倫者乎？
《五倫書》嘉言善行，固備載五倫之事，而獨詳於君臣之倫者，豈非以君臣為五倫之首，而治教之所關乎？若夫《一統誌》所載天下名宦、人物、烈女，克盡五倫之道者，不可指數。其在山東，若大聖大賢，後先相望，其道德高厚，萬世景仰，不可以一方之人物觀者，在所不必論矣。兹以一節之行有關於五倫最彰著者言之，如王祥之臥冰、緹縈女之救父，非敦於父子之倫者乎？廷式之娶瞽、張義婦之歸夫骨，非敦於夫婦之倫者乎？至如王蠋之不事二君以盡臣節，張公藝之九世同居以睦宗族，辛棄疾之往哭朱晦菴，師友之義，又何如其克盡也！之數人者，皆有關乎五倫，載諸典籍，昭耶乎最彰著者。愚也幼而聞諸
translation_en:
Although the Accounts of Filial Obedience deals throughout with filial piety, it records, for example, how Kaoshu moved his lord by setting aside some broth, and how Min Sun’s filial devotion to his mother extended to his younger brothers. How could such acts fail to embrace the other relationships as well?
The admirable sayings and exemplary deeds in the Book of the Five Relationships certainly provide a full record of matters concerning all five relationships. Yet it treats the relationship between ruler and minister in particular detail. Is this not because that relationship stands foremost among the five and bears upon governance and moral instruction? As for the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Unified Realm, the renowned officials, notable people, and exemplary women throughout the realm recorded there who fully fulfilled the Way of the five relationships are too numerous to enumerate. In Shandong, great sages and worthies arose in succession. Their moral stature was lofty and profound, commanding the admiration of all generations; they cannot be regarded merely as notable people of a single region. There is therefore no need to discuss them here. Let us instead speak of those most conspicuous for a particular act bearing upon the five relationships. Were not Wang Xiang’s lying upon the ice and the girl Tiying’s rescue of her father examples of devotion to the relationship between father and child? Were not Ting Shi’s [?] marriage to a blind woman and the righteous woman Zhang’s bringing home her husband’s bones examples of devotion to the relationship between husband and wife? As for Wang Zhu’s refusal to serve two rulers, thereby fulfilling a minister’s integrity; Zhang Gongyi’s nine generations dwelling together, thereby maintaining harmony within the lineage; and Xin Qiji’s going to mourn Zhu Hui’an, fulfilling the obligations between teachers and friends—how fully they discharged their duties! These several people all exemplified the five relationships; their deeds are recorded in the classics and other writings and stand among the most illustrious [?]. I, in my ignorance, heard of these from childhood from…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
父師之所言〻而考諸典籍之所載忻慕
嘆賞願學而未能者姑舉以塞明問之萬
一若夫備舉誌中所紀又有待於能者焉
生佩服
聖訓於五倫之道不敢不勉惟執事其與進之
第二問
同考試官教諭邵　批〔孝經小學二書非為教本之學作〕
杜珏
===
〔聖功大末始不基於此業舉者多不之講此篇能尋其原委而〕〔敷答詳明不於其目次第處的然有見殆士之涵養有素者乎〕
〔宜薦之〕
考試官教諭張　批〔詳悉閒意歷歷有據必熟〕
〔於二書者〕
考試官教諭李　批〔條答無遺足見策手〕
書有關於天經地義者當考究其本原書
有裨於聖經賢傳者當發明其指趣夫孝
經一書乃人道之大端小學一書實大學
之基本是皆脩身齊家治國平天下之道
punctuated:
父師之所言〻，而考諸典籍之所載，忻慕嘆賞，願學而未能者，姑舉以塞明問之萬一。若夫備舉誌中所紀，又有待於能者焉。生佩服聖訓，於五倫之道不敢不勉，惟執事其與進之。

第二問

同考試官教諭邵，批〔孝經小學二書非為教本之學作〕
杜珏
〔聖功大末始不基於此業舉者多不之講此篇能尋其原委而〕〔敷答詳明不於其目次第處的然有見殆士之涵養有素者乎〕〔宜薦之〕
考試官教諭張，批〔詳悉閒意歷歷有據必熟〕〔於二書者〕
考試官教諭李，批〔條答無遺足見策手〕

書有關於天經地義者，當考究其本原；書有裨於聖經賢傳者，當發明其指趣。夫孝經一書，乃人道之大端；小學一書，實大學之基本。是皆脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之道
translation_en:
…what my father and teachers have said, and have examined what the classical writings record. These are examples I joyfully admire and acclaim, wishing to emulate them but not yet able to do so. I offer them provisionally to answer the smallest part of your discerning question. As for giving a complete account of what the gazetteer records, that must await someone capable of doing so. I, your student, reverently embrace the sagely instructions and dare not fail to exert myself in the Way of the Five Relationships. I ask you, sir, to encourage my further progress.

Second Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔The Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning were not composed for learning that takes teaching as its foundation [?].〕
Du Jue
〔The work of sagehood has never failed to be founded upon this [?], yet those preparing for the examinations mostly do not study it. This essay can trace its origins and ramifications and〕〔set forth a detailed and lucid answer. In its treatment of the sequence of the headings [?], it shows definite insight. Surely this is a scholar whose self-cultivation is long established.〕〔He should be recommended.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Detailed and thorough, with composed expression [?]; each point has clear support. He must be well versed〕〔in the two books.〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔His answers address every point without omission, amply demonstrating his skill as a policy essay writer.〕

When a book concerns the constant principles of Heaven and the proper order of Earth, one should investigate its fundamental origins; when a book aids understanding of the sages’ classics and the worthies’ commentaries, one should elucidate its meaning and purport. The Classic of Filial Piety concerns the great essentials of the human Way; Elementary Learning is indeed the foundation of the Great Learning. These both embody the Way of cultivating oneself, ordering one’s family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
所寓也苟於此而不講明之則行矣不著
習矣不察終身由之而不知其道矣將何
以望古人之學哉執事以此下詢誠端本
之盛心也顧生雖愚敢不摭拾所聞以對
乎敢因明問而復之孝經之書成於曾子
門人之手而朱子為之刊誤誠以孝之
為經乃孔曾一時問答之詞首論孝之始
終中乃敷陳天子諸侯卿大夫士庶人之
孝而末結之曰自天子至於庶人孝無終
===
始而患不及者未之有也其首尾相應文
勢連屬同是一時之言後人乃分之為六
章而又增以子曰之字加以詩書之文皆
非孝經之舊也七章以後又皆後人雜引
傳記之格言而為之傳其間戾於經意者
如釋要道非若經文自己而推之意釋以
順天下而曰先之以博愛亦非立愛惟親
之序至於釋民用和睦上下無怨其言雖
善亦非經文之正意論嚴父配天又非為
punctuated:
所寓也。苟於此而不講明之，則行矣不著，習矣不察，終身由之而不知其道矣，將何以望古人之學哉？執事以此下詢，誠端本之盛心也。顧生雖愚，敢不摭拾所聞以對乎？敢因明問而復之。
孝經之書成於曾子門人之手，而朱子為之刊誤，誠以孝之為經，乃孔曾一時問答之詞。首論孝之始終，中乃敷陳天子、諸侯、卿大夫、士、庶人之孝，而末結之曰：「自天子至於庶人，孝無終始而患不及者，未之有也。」其首尾相應，文勢連屬，同是一時之言。後人乃分之為六章，而又增以「子曰」之字，加以詩書之文，皆非孝經之舊也。七章以後，又皆後人雜引傳記之格言而為之傳。其間戾於經意者，如釋「要道」，非若經文自己而推之意；釋「以順天下」而曰「先之以博愛」，亦非「立愛惟親」之序。至於釋「民用和睦，上下無怨」，其言雖善，亦非經文之正意。論「嚴父配天」，又非為
translation_en:
…are embodied. If one does not study and clarify these matters, one will act without understanding, practice without discernment, and follow this way throughout one’s life without knowing it. How, then, could one hope to attain the learning of the ancients? Your Honor’s inquiry on this subject truly manifests an admirable intention to set the foundations right. Though I, your student, am ignorant, how could I venture not to gather what I have heard and offer a reply? I therefore venture to respond to your illuminating question.
The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) was compiled by the disciples of Zengzi, and Master Zhu produced his Corrections of Errors for it. This was indeed because the canonical text on filial piety consists of the words exchanged between Confucius and Zengzi on a single occasion. It begins by discussing the beginning and completion of filial piety; in the middle it sets forth the filial piety of the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, ministers and grand masters, officers, and common people. It concludes by saying: “From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, there has never been anyone for whom filial piety had neither end nor beginning, yet who had cause to fear being unable to fulfill it.” Its beginning and ending correspond, and its wording runs continuously: it is all speech from a single occasion. Later people divided it into six chapters, inserted the words “The Master said,” and added passages from the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents. None of these belonged to the original Classic of Filial Piety. From chapter seven onward, later people likewise drew miscellaneous maxims from transmitted writings to create a commentary on it. Among the passages that conflict with the meaning of the canonical text is the explanation of “the essential way”: it does not convey the canonical text’s sense of extending outward from oneself. The explanation of “bringing all under Heaven into accord” says, “Lead them with universal love”; this, too, fails to follow the sequence expressed in “establishing love begins with one’s parents.” As for the explanation of “the people thereby live in harmony, and neither superiors nor inferiors harbor resentment,” although its words are good, they likewise do not convey the canonical text’s proper meaning. Its discussion of “honoring one’s father by associating him with Heaven” is, moreover, not something for…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
人臣子者所敢為其他所失尚多具載刋
誤難以悉舉而其書則頴註古文二十二
章孔壁所藏本也今文一十八章則河閒
王所得頴芝本也閨門一章乃唐開元間
勑議纂脩之時而為司馬貞之所去司馬
貞淺見陋識去此一章論者以為卒啓玄
宗無禮無度之禍是非較然矣小學雜出
於曲禮少儀內則弟子職諸篇子朱子蒐
輯以為內篇而又述嘉言善行以為外篇
===
內篇四立教明倫敬身稽古也外篇二嘉
言善行也內前三篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之
言也後一篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之行也故
皆謂之內篇雖許魯齋以前三篇立教明
倫敬身為小學之綱領而稽古一篇正所
以為立教明倫敬身之事實故皆謂之內
篇外篇所謂嘉言乃子朱子述漢以來賢
者所言之嘉言以廣立教明倫敬身也所
謂善行乃子朱子紀漢以來賢者所行之
punctuated:
人臣子者所敢為。其他所失尚多，具載《刋誤》，難以悉舉。而其書則頴註古文二十二章，孔壁所藏本也；今文一十八章，則河閒王所得頴芝本也。《閨門》一章，乃唐開元間勑議纂脩之時，而為司馬貞之所去。司馬貞淺見陋識，去此一章，論者以為卒啓玄宗無禮無度之禍，是非較然矣。
《小學》雜出於《曲禮》《少儀》《內則》《弟子職》諸篇，子朱子蒐輯以為內篇，而又述嘉言善行以為外篇。內篇四：立教、明倫、敬身、稽古也。外篇二：嘉言、善行也。內前三篇，乃虞夏商周聖賢之言也；後一篇，乃虞夏商周聖賢之行也，故皆謂之內篇。雖許魯齋以前三篇立教、明倫、敬身為《小學》之綱領，而稽古一篇正所以為立教、明倫、敬身之事實，故皆謂之內篇。外篇所謂嘉言，乃子朱子述漢以來賢者所言之嘉言，以廣立教、明倫、敬身也。所謂善行，乃子朱子紀漢以來賢者所行之
translation_en:
…something that those who are subjects and sons would dare to do. Its other errors are numerous and are recorded in full in Corrections of Errors; it is difficult to enumerate them all. As for the book itself, the twenty-two chapters of the old-script text with Ying’s commentary [?] constitute the version concealed in the wall of the Kong residence; the eighteen chapters of the modern-script text constitute the Yingzhi version [?] obtained by the Prince of Hejian. The chapter “Within the Inner Quarters” was removed by Sima Zhen during the compilation and revision undertaken by imperial command in the Kaiyuan reign of the Tang. Sima Zhen, with his shallow views and limited understanding, removed this chapter. Commentators consider that this ultimately opened the way to the calamities of Xuanzong’s disregard for ritual and restraint. Right and wrong are plainly evident.
Elementary Learning draws on various passages from such chapters as “Summary Rules of Propriety,” “Lesser Rules of Deportment,” “Domestic Regulations,” and “Duties of Disciples.” Master Zhu collected and compiled these to form the Inner Chapters, and further recounted commendable sayings and good deeds to form the Outer Chapters. There are four Inner Chapters: “Establishing Instruction,” “Clarifying Human Relationships,” “Maintaining Reverence for One’s Person,” and “Examining Antiquity.” There are two Outer Chapters: “Commendable Sayings” and “Good Deeds.” The first three Inner Chapters contain the words of sages and worthies of the Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou; the last contains the deeds of sages and worthies of those periods. Hence all are called Inner Chapters. Although Xu Luzhai regarded the first three chapters—“Establishing Instruction,” “Clarifying Human Relationships,” and “Maintaining Reverence for One’s Person”—as the guiding framework of Elementary Learning, the chapter “Examining Antiquity” supplies precisely the actual instances of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and maintaining reverence for one’s person. Thus all are called Inner Chapters. What the Outer Chapters call “Commendable Sayings” consists of Master Zhu’s recounting of commendable sayings uttered by worthies from the Han onward, to amplify establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and maintaining reverence for one’s person. What is called “Good Deeds” consists of Master Zhu’s recording of what worthies from the Han onward performed as…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
善行以實立教明倫敬身也內篇雖為嘉
言善行正古聖賢小學之支流餘裔亦若
孝經之經也外篇輯漢以來之嘉言善行
以廣以實前篇正若孝經之傳也安得無
別乎執事謂二書皆為脩身齊家治國平
天下之本皆切於學者之身故舉以為問
目盖懼學者於此二書有所忽略則所失
莫大矣愚生童而習之至今未知一言之
可用亦無怪乎執事之所甚懼者姑舉所
聞以復而益加勉焉
===
第三問
刀嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔孔氏家世源委歷數無遺於是乎見該博之學矣〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔孔氏世系人物學者皆當究心者也場中能悉此者絶少此作考據精詳條荅無遺且知上天所以厚報之意盖亦感佩聖教不忘所自者歟〕
考試官教諭張　批〔條答詳悉他卷所無者〕
punctuated:
善行，以實立教、明倫、敬身也。內篇雖為嘉言善行，正古聖賢小學之支流餘裔，亦若《孝經》之經也。外篇輯漢以來之嘉言善行，以廣以實前篇，正若《孝經》之傳也。安得無別乎？執事謂二書皆為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本，皆切於學者之身，故舉以為問目。盖懼學者於此二書有所忽略，則所失莫大矣。愚生童而習之，至今未知一言之可用，亦無怪乎執事之所甚懼者。姑舉所聞以復，而益加勉焉。

第三問
刀嵎

同考試官訓導楊　批〔孔氏家世源委，歷數無遺，於是乎見該博之學矣。〕

同考試官教諭朱　批〔孔氏世系人物，學者皆當究心者也。場中能悉此者絶少。此作考據精詳，條荅無遺，且知上天所以厚報之意，盖亦感佩聖教、不忘所自者歟！〕

考試官教諭張　批〔條答詳悉，他卷所無者。〕
translation_en:
…good deeds, to give concrete substance to establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and maintaining reverence in one’s conduct. Although the Inner Chapters consist of admirable sayings and good deeds, they are precisely the branches and surviving legacy of the elementary learning of the ancient sages and worthies; they also resemble the canonical text of the Classic of Filial Piety. The Outer Chapters collect admirable sayings and good deeds from the Han onward to expand upon and give concrete substance to the preceding chapters, just as a commentary does for the Classic of Filial Piety. How could there be no distinction?

You hold that both books are foundations for cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven, and that both bear directly upon the learner’s own person. You have therefore selected them as subjects for examination questions. Presumably you fear that, should learners neglect anything in these two books, the loss would be immense. I, your unworthy student, studied them as a child, yet even now I do not know how to put a single saying into practice. It is therefore no wonder that you are so deeply concerned. I have merely offered what I have heard in reply and shall exert myself still further.

Third Question
Dao Yu 刀嵎

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: 〔He recounts the origins and development of the Kong family’s history without omission. Here one sees his extensive learning.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔The lineage and individual members of the Kong family are matters that all learners should investigate attentively. Very few candidates in the examination hall know them fully. This essay is precise and detailed in its examination of the evidence, answering point by point without omission. Moreover, it understands Heaven’s intention in rewarding the family so generously. Surely its author, too, gratefully cherishes the sage’s teaching and does not forget its source!〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The answers are detailed and comprehensive, providing what other examination scripts lack.〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批〔孔氏家乘此作殆盡之矣〕
讀以似以續之詩則知天之衍聖嗣也爲
無窮讀報德報功之論則知天之厚聖人
也爲不偶聖人之生異矣天亦以異而待
之既厚其生也且厚其子孫也又厚其血
食於千萬世也聖人亦何以得之盖道在
聖人則功在聖人功在萬世則報在萬世
是知天之所以厚待聖人者亦報施之公
道宜然耳夫豈私厚之哉中庸曰天之生
===
物必因其材而篤焉况聖人之所以自培
植者如此其至則其得上天之厚報亦無
足恠者執事膺聘而来瞻仰道德之光忻
慕慶澤之遠感慨之意既發於中世系之
問遂形於策請以所聞見者言之先孔子
而聖者堯舜也堯之後不肖者丹朱孰如
鯉也詩禮之傳舜之後不肖者商均孰如
伋也性命之闡賢哉子孫豈無所自盖孔
子之先實由微子封於宋始於微仲衍自
punctuated:
考試官教諭李，批〔孔氏家乘，此作殆盡之矣。〕
讀「以似以續」之詩，則知天之衍聖嗣也爲無窮；讀報德報功之論，則知天之厚聖人也爲不偶。聖人之生異矣，天亦以異而待之：既厚其生也，且厚其子孫也，又厚其血食於千萬世也。聖人亦何以得之？盖道在聖人，則功在聖人；功在萬世，則報在萬世。是知天之所以厚待聖人者，亦報施之公道宜然耳，夫豈私厚之哉？《中庸》曰：「天之生物，必因其材而篤焉。」况聖人之所以自培植者如此其至，則其得上天之厚報，亦無足恠者。執事膺聘而来，瞻仰道德之光，忻慕慶澤之遠，感慨之意既發於中，世系之問遂形於策。請以所聞見者言之。先孔子而聖者，堯舜也。堯之後不肖者丹朱，孰如鯉也，詩禮之傳？舜之後不肖者商均，孰如伋也，性命之闡？賢哉子孫！豈無所自？盖孔子之先，實由微子封於宋，始於微仲衍，自
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔This essay covers virtually the whole of the Kong family's genealogical record.〕
Reading the poem's words, “to carry on and to continue,” one knows that Heaven extends the sage's line without end; reading the discussion of recompensing virtue and achievement, one knows that Heaven's generosity toward the sage is no accident. The sage's birth was extraordinary, and Heaven likewise treated him extraordinarily. It bestowed abundance upon him during his lifetime, extended its generosity to his descendants, and further granted him sacrificial offerings for countless generations. How did the sage obtain this? Because the Way resided in the sage, the achievement belonged to him; because his achievement benefits all generations, his recompense continues through all generations. Thus we know that Heaven's generous treatment of the sage is simply what the impartial principle of recompense properly requires. How could it be a matter of favoring him out of partiality? The Doctrine of the Mean says: “When Heaven brings things into being, it necessarily enriches them according to their capacities.” Moreover, the sage's cultivation of himself was so consummate that there is nothing surprising in his receiving Heaven's generous recompense.
You, honored examiners, have come in response to your appointments. Gazing reverently upon the radiance of his Way and virtue, you delight in and admire the enduring reach of his blessings. These feelings stirred within you and found expression in a policy question concerning his lineage. Allow me to speak from what I have heard and seen. The sages preceding Confucius were Yao and Shun. Yao's unworthy descendant was Danzhu: how could he compare with Li, who received the transmission of the Odes and the rites? Shun's unworthy descendant was Shangjun: how could he compare with Ji, who elucidated human nature and Heaven's mandate? Worthy indeed were these descendants! Could their worth have had no source? The ancestry of Confucius in fact derived from Weizi's enfeoffment in Song, with the line beginning with Weizhong Yan. From …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
衍而歷稽也中也共也弗父何也宋父周
也自周而歷世父勝也正考父也孔父嘉
也木金父也睪夷父也睪夷生防叔防叔
生伯夏伯夏者叔梁紇所從出也叔梁紇
者即孔子所由生也其生也有自來其聖
也有所爲雖曰間氣而生是亦本原厚積
之發也而孔子又從而培植之本益固矣
而末之茂也豈期然而然哉故自伋之後
名白者則相於齊名順者則相於魏名鮒
者則博士於秦戰國時之顯者也博極羣
書而還大將軍者曰延年授太子經而拜
太師者曰孔霸好學有大才而襲封關內
侯者曰孔均漢時之著者也孔鮮始爲奉
聖亭侯宋文帝改封崇聖侯崇有尊尚之
義進於奉也審矣非進侯者之秩也無非
褒加聖人也孔渠始爲恭聖侯隋煬帝改
封嗣哲紹聖侯紹有纘緒之意加於恭也
明矣非加侯者之爵也亦無非追隆聖人
punctuated: 衍而歷稽也、中也、共也、弗父何也、宋父周也。自周而歷世父勝也、正考父也、孔父嘉也、木金父也、睪夷父也。睪夷生防叔，防叔生伯夏，伯夏者叔梁紇所從出也。叔梁紇者，即孔子所由生也。其生也有自來，其聖也有所爲。雖曰間氣而生，是亦本原厚積之發也。而孔子又從而培植之，本益固矣，而末之茂也，豈期然而然哉？故自伋之後，名白者則相於齊，名順者則相於魏，名鮒者則博士於秦，戰國時之顯者也。博極羣書而還大將軍者曰延年，授太子經而拜太師者曰孔霸，好學有大才而襲封關內侯者曰孔均，漢時之著者也。孔鮮始爲奉聖亭侯，宋文帝改封崇聖侯。崇有尊尚之義，進於奉也審矣，非進侯者之秩也，無非褒加聖人也。孔渠始爲恭聖侯，隋煬帝改封嗣哲紹聖侯。紹有纘緒之意，加於恭也明矣，非加侯者之爵也，亦無非追隆聖人
translation_en:
…from Yan the succession passed through Ji, Zhong, Gong, Fufu He, and Songfu Zhou. From Zhou it passed through Shifu Sheng, Zhengkaofu, Kongfu Jia, Mujinfu [?], and Gaoyifu. Gaoyi begot Fangshu, and Fangshu begot Boxia; Boxia was the father of Shuliang He. Shuliang He, in turn, was the father of Confucius. His birth thus had its ancestral source, and his sagehood had its foundation. Although he is said to have been born of the rare, exceptional vital energy bestowed by Heaven, this too was the manifestation of virtue richly accumulated at its source. Confucius then further cultivated it, making the root still firmer. Was the flourishing of its branches something that required deliberate expectation before it came about?

Thus, among the descendants of Ji, the one named Bai served as Counselor-in-chief in Qi; the one named Shun served as Counselor-in-chief in Wei; and the one named Fu served as an Erudite in Qin. These were the eminent descendants of the Warring States period. The one who mastered the multitude of books and returned as General-in-chief [?] was called Yannian. The one who taught the classics to the heir apparent and was appointed Grand Preceptor was Kong Ba. The one who loved learning, possessed great talent, and inherited the title of Marquis within the Passes was Kong Jun. These were the distinguished descendants of the Han period.

Kong Xian initially held the title of Township Marquis for Serving the Sage. Emperor Wen of the Song changed his enfeoffment to Marquis for Exalting the Sage. “Exalting” carries the meaning of honoring and esteeming, and is assuredly an advance upon “serving.” This was not an advancement in the marquis’s official grade; it was entirely a means of bestowing further honor upon the Sage. Kong Qu initially held the title of Marquis for Revering the Sage. Emperor Yang of the Sui changed his enfeoffment to Marquis for Succeeding the Wise and Continuing the Sage’s Line. “Continuing” conveys the idea of carrying on an ancestral succession, and clearly adds to the meaning of “revering.” This was not an increase in the marquis’s noble rank; it too was entirely a means of bestowing posthumous honor upon the Sage…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也他如仕唐者則對策高第其孔昌寓乎
狀元及第其孔振乎明經及第其孔緣乎
一時文盛雖不敢追配先烈刪述之文是
亦奉先烈之遺矩者仕宋者則以剛毅直
諒名其道輔也以操行介潔稱其孔傳也
以介潔不阿許其孔端也一時高節雖不
敢竊擬先聖時中之行是亦守先聖之家
法者嗚呼鴻儒碩學大爵高官肩摩踵接
未易枚舉今之所陳者特如所問耳且往
===
古來今享王祀於無窮襲衍聖於無替愈
遠益昌誠非筆舌之所易紀追視堯舜之
後何寥寥無一可聞者耶蓋又有說也堯
舜有聖人之德得聖人之位盛極當時若
孔子有堯舜之德不得堯舜之位天之負
於前者正所以償之於後也况崇德報功
固在人所當盡又在天所不爽此其所以
歷千百世而人物迭興無有紀極也耶愚
也忝生是邦聖人之學固不敢洋望其一
punctuated:
也。他如仕唐者，則對策高第，其孔昌寓乎？狀元及第，其孔振乎？明經及第，其孔緣乎？一時文盛，雖不敢追配先烈刪述之文，是亦奉先烈之遺矩者。仕宋者，則以剛毅直諒名，其道輔也；以操行介潔稱，其孔傳也；以介潔不阿許，其孔端也。一時高節，雖不敢竊擬先聖時中之行，是亦守先聖之家法者。嗚呼！鴻儒碩學，大爵高官，肩摩踵接，未易枚舉。今之所陳者，特如所問耳。
且往古來今，享王祀於無窮，襲衍聖於無替，愈遠益昌，誠非筆舌之所易紀。追視堯舜之後，何寥寥無一可聞者耶？蓋又有說也。堯舜有聖人之德，得聖人之位，盛極當時。若孔子，有堯舜之德，不得堯舜之位，天之負於前者，正所以償之於後也。况崇德報功，固在人所當盡，又在天所不爽，此其所以歷千百世而人物迭興，無有紀極也耶？愚也忝生是邦，聖人之學，固不敢洋望其一
translation_en:
…as well. As for others who served under the Tang: was it not Kong Changyu who attained a high rank in answering the policy questions? Was it not Kong Zhen who passed as the top-ranked candidate? Was it not Kong Yuan who passed the Classicists examination (mingjing)? Though one would not presume to compare the literary brilliance of their day with their illustrious ancestor’s work of editing and transmitting the classics, they too upheld the standards he bequeathed. Among those who served under the Song, it was Daofu who was renowned for firmness, resolve, uprightness, and sincerity; Kong Chuan who was praised for principled and spotless conduct; and Kong Duan who was esteemed for integrity and refusal to bow to others. Though one would not presume to liken their lofty integrity to the ancient Sage’s conduct, which always accorded with the Mean as circumstances required, they too maintained his family’s principles. Ah! Great Confucian scholars and men of profound learning, holders of exalted noble ranks and high offices, followed one another in such numbers that they cannot easily be enumerated. Those presented here are merely those pertinent to the question.
Moreover, from antiquity down to the present, royal sacrifices have been enjoyed without end, and the title of Duke for Fulfilling the Sage (Yansheng) has been inherited without interruption. As time passes, this lineage flourishes ever more greatly: truly, neither pen nor tongue can readily record it. Looking back at the descendants of Yao and Shun, why are they so obscure that not a single one is heard of? There is an explanation for this too. Yao and Shun possessed the virtue of sages and attained the positions of sages, reaching the height of glory in their own time. Confucius, however, possessed the virtue of Yao and Shun but did not attain their positions. What Heaven withheld from him earlier was precisely what it would compensate for later. Moreover, honoring virtue and recompensing merit are duties that people must fully discharge, and principles in which Heaven never errs. Is this why, through hundreds and thousands of generations, outstanding figures have arisen in succession without any limit?
Unworthy though I am, I was born in this land. As for the Sage’s learning, I certainly dare not hope to attain even a fraction of it [?]…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
二然聖人遺蹟之陳世家之盛輩得濡於
耳涤於目也古人云觀羑墻則思堯覩河
洛則思禹今日聖人之墓於泗上瞻聖人
之廟於闕里獨無所思乎然思之要在學
之何如耳孟子曰乃所願則學孔子也愚
竊游歌於鄒魯之間敢不以此自勵
第四問
王崇獻
同考試官訓導李　批〔能即其人而論其得失足見斷〕
制之學非徒取其記問之長而已也
===
同考試官教諭王　批〔場中答此策者多得此失彼〕
求其事核文整如此篇者盖有數也
考試官教諭張　批〔論人物得失鑿鑿有見有〕
學有識之士也
考試官教諭李　批〔策善答所問〕
明於知人斯可立論以方人明於知己斯
可舉人以況己夫方人非難而明於知人
為難況己非難而明於知己為難苟無知
punctuated:
二。然聖人遺蹟之陳、世家之盛，輩得濡於耳、涤於目也。古人云：「觀羑墻則思堯，覩河洛則思禹。」今日聖人之墓於泗上，瞻聖人之廟於闕里，獨無所思乎？然思之要，在學之何如耳。孟子曰：「乃所願，則學孔子也。」愚竊游歌於鄒魯之間，敢不以此自勵？
第四問
王崇獻
同考試官訓導李批〔能即其人而論其得失，足見斷〕制之學，非徒取其記問之長而已也。
同考試官教諭王批〔場中答此策者，多得此失彼。〕求其事核文整如此篇者，盖有數也。
考試官教諭張批〔論人物得失，鑿鑿有見，有〕學有識之士也。
考試官教諭李批〔策善答所問。〕
明於知人，斯可立論以方人；明於知己，斯可舉人以況己。夫方人非難，而明於知人為難；況己非難，而明於知己為難。苟無知
translation_en:
…even a fraction of it. Yet the surviving traces of the Sage arrayed here, and the flourishing of his hereditary house, have steeped our ears and cleansed our eyes [?]. The ancients said: “Seeing the walls of You [?], one thinks of Yao; seeing the Yellow and Luo Rivers, one thinks of Yu.” Today, at the Sage’s tomb beside the Si River, and gazing upon his temple at Queli, could one alone have no thoughts stirred? Yet the essential point of such reflection lies in how one learns from him. Mencius said: “As for what I desire, it is to emulate Confucius.” As I wander and sing among Zou and Lu, dare I fail to encourage myself with this?
Fourth Question
Wang Chongxian
