title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
已知人之明則是非混淆於鑑別之中邪
正倒置於權衡之下差之毫釐繆以千里
而欲方人況己也不亦難哉請因明問而
陳其一二諸葛孔明之在蜀也膺三聘之
勤受付托之重出師二表忠貫日星八陣
一圖光昭海宇奚考其人乃伊吕之儔耳
自比管樂盖其謙詞賈似道之在宋也以
嫉妬之心秉鈞軸之任專權蠹政大失民
心積釁稔禍終亡宋祚奚考其人盖杞檜
===
之雄也自託伊周乃其誇誕恢廓大度才
明勇畧克復舊物於羣雄草竊之餘先訪
儒雅於天下甫定之際光武真中興之主
也石勒以為韓彭之流豈知光武者哉出
守雲中宰制閫外不私軍市之租遠遁匈
奴之騎魏尚真名世之将也馮唐以為頗
牧之屬其知魏尚者歟澶淵摧敵北門禦
寇丞相準之忠端可方唐之魏公徵也碩
德重望之王旦豈與馮道伍哉雖然美珠
punctuated: 已知人之明，則是非混淆於鑑別之中，邪正倒置於權衡之下，差之毫釐，繆以千里，而欲方人況己也，不亦難哉？請因明問而陳其一二。諸葛孔明之在蜀也，膺三聘之勤，受付托之重，出師二表，忠貫日星；八陣一圖，光昭海宇。奚考其人，乃伊吕之儔耳。自比管樂，盖其謙詞。賈似道之在宋也，以嫉妬之心，秉鈞軸之任，專權蠹政，大失民心，積釁稔禍，終亡宋祚。奚考其人，盖杞檜之雄也。自託伊周，乃其誇誕。恢廓大度，才明勇畧，克復舊物於羣雄草竊之餘，先訪儒雅於天下甫定之際，光武真中興之主也。石勒以為韓彭之流，豈知光武者哉？出守雲中，宰制閫外，不私軍市之租，遠遁匈奴之騎，魏尚真名世之将也。馮唐以為頗牧之屬，其知魏尚者歟？澶淵摧敵，北門禦寇，丞相準之忠，端可方唐之魏公徵也。碩德重望之王旦，豈與馮道伍哉？雖然，美珠
translation_en:
…clarity in knowing oneself and others, then right and wrong become confused in one’s discernment, and the wicked and upright are reversed in one’s weighing of them. An error of a hair’s breadth leads to a discrepancy of a thousand li. Would it not then be difficult to judge others by comparison or to compare oneself with them? Allow me to respond to your discerning question by setting forth one or two examples.

When Zhuge Kongming served in Shu, he received the earnest attention of three visits and accepted the weighty trust committed to him. In his two memorials on dispatching the army, his loyalty shone through to the sun and stars; his diagram of the Eight Formations cast its brilliance throughout the realm. On assessing the man [?], he was a peer of Yi Yin and Lü Shang. His comparison of himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi was surely an expression of modesty. When Jia Sidao served under the Song, he held the highest responsibility in government with a jealous heart. He monopolized power and corrupted administration, utterly losing the people’s allegiance. His accumulated offenses brought calamity to fruition and ultimately destroyed the Song dynasty. On assessing the man [?], he was a foremost figure among the likes of Lu Qi and Qin Hui. His placing himself alongside Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou was boastful exaggeration.

Broad-minded and magnanimous, gifted with intelligence, courage, and strategic ability, Guangwu recovered the former imperial dominion after rival warlords had seized power, and made seeking out learned scholars a priority when the realm had only just been pacified. He truly was a ruler who restored his dynasty. Shi Le considered him one of the likes of Han Xin and Peng Yue: how could he have understood Guangwu?

Serving as Governor of Yunzhong and exercising military command beyond the capital, Wei Shang did not appropriate the revenues of the military markets for himself and drove the Xiongnu cavalry far away. He truly was a general renowned in his age. Feng Tang considered him one of the likes of Lian Po and Li Mu: did he not understand Wei Shang?

Crushing the enemy at Chanyuan and repelling invaders at the northern gateway, Grand Councilor Kou Zhun displayed a loyalty that could indeed be compared to that of Wei Zheng, Duke of Wei, under the Tang. How could Wang Dan, with his great virtue and high reputation, be ranked alongside Feng Dao? Nevertheless, the beautiful pearls…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
受遺亦畧相似東攻張步北收上谷將軍
弇之勇端可擬漢之韓信也捫虱高談之
王猛夫豈孔明匹哉雖然魚水得君亦畧
相若好賢納諫尚文抑武金世宗賢則賢
矣贊爲堯舜或不免於過情神謨廟筭濟
世安民唐太宗賢則賢矣自况文宣或不
免於慚德宇量弘潤明遠好謀武帝乃晉
之英君劉毅方於桓靈亦箴規之詞耳勵
精求治去奢從儉文宗乃唐之誼辟自以
===
赧獻爲愧亦欝抑之懷耳深潛純粹具體
聖人顔子孔門大賢也黄憲何人荀淑亦
以顔子目之然汪汪德量澄不清而淆不
濁憲亦一時高士也運籌帷幄决勝千里
子房漢廷人傑也荀彧何人曹操亦以子
房稱之然表表才華擢賢能而詰軍旅彧
亦一代偉人也夫荷氊披毳者不足以語
綿絺之美咀藜含糗者不足以語牢醴之
佳低昂人物評品古今上智之事也是非
punctuated: 受遺亦畧相似。東攻張步，北收上谷，將軍弇之勇，端可擬漢之韓信也。捫虱高談之王猛，夫豈孔明匹哉？雖然，魚水得君亦畧相若。好賢納諫，尚文抑武，金世宗賢則賢矣，贊爲堯舜，或不免於過情。神謨廟筭，濟世安民，唐太宗賢則賢矣，自况文宣，或不免於慚德。宇量弘潤，明遠好謀，武帝乃晉之英君，劉毅方於桓靈，亦箴規之詞耳。勵精求治，去奢從儉，文宗乃唐之誼辟，自以赧獻爲愧，亦欝抑之懷耳。深潛純粹，具體聖人，顔子孔門大賢也。黄憲何人，荀淑亦以顔子目之？然汪汪德量，澄不清而淆不濁，憲亦一時高士也。運籌帷幄，决勝千里，子房漢廷人傑也。荀彧何人，曹操亦以子房稱之？然表表才華，擢賢能而詰軍旅，彧亦一代偉人也。夫荷氊披毳者，不足以語綿絺之美；咀藜含糗者，不足以語牢醴之佳。低昂人物，評品古今，上智之事也。是非
translation_en:
…in accepting a gift, too, they were somewhat alike. Attacking Zhang Bu in the east and securing Shanggu in the north, General Geng Yan displayed courage that could indeed be compared with that of Han Xin of the Han. But could Wang Meng, who discoursed loftily while picking lice, possibly rival Kongming? Even so, in finding a ruler with whom he enjoyed a relationship like that of fish and water, he was somewhat similar.

Honoring worthy men and accepting remonstrance, esteeming civil pursuits and restraining military ones, Emperor Shizong of the Jin was certainly worthy; yet praising him as a Yao or Shun may go beyond the truth. With inspired plans and deliberations at court, saving the age and bringing peace to the people, Emperor Taizong of the Tang was certainly worthy; yet in comparing himself with Emperors Wen and Xuan, he may have had cause to feel ashamed of his virtue. Generous and gracious in disposition, perceptive, farseeing, and fond of deliberation, Emperor Wu was an outstanding ruler of the Jin. Liu Yi’s comparison of him with Emperors Huan and Ling was merely an admonition. Applying himself earnestly to good government, abandoning extravagance and embracing frugality, Emperor Wenzong was a righteous sovereign of the Tang. His shame at considering himself inferior to King Nan and Emperor Xian merely expressed his feelings of frustration and constraint.

Profound, reserved, and wholly pure, embodying the qualities of a sage, Master Yan was a great worthy of Confucius’s school. Who was Huang Xian, that Xun Shu should likewise regard him as a Master Yan? Yet his virtue and magnanimity were like an immense body of water, which settling could not make clearer and stirring could not make turbid. Xian, too, was a lofty-minded scholar of his time. Devising strategies within the command tent and determining victory a thousand li away, Zifang was an outstanding man at the Han court. Who was Xun Yu, that Cao Cao should likewise call him a Zifang? Yet with his conspicuous talents, promoting the worthy and capable and putting military affairs in order, Yu, too, was a great man of his age.

Those who wear felt and coarse wool are not qualified to discuss the beauty of silk and fine ramie; those who chew goosefoot greens and dry grain are not qualified to discuss the excellence of fine meats and sweet wine. Ranking people high and low and appraising figures ancient and modern are tasks for those of the highest wisdom. As for right and wrong…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之公僅見董狐班馬而下不能不起人之
非議況數子言論之當否人品之高下聖
門之徒儒先之碩已嘗論之詳矣鯫生小
子豈容贅言雖然言及之而不言又恐取
侍君子之愆也謹對
第五問
逸貢
同考試官教諭張　批〔漕運一策正欲觀士子用世之學此篇條答詳悉斟酌得宜其識見出人一頭地他日施下有政必有可觀者噫得士如此可以增重矣〕
===
考試官教諭張　批〔觀此策非惟有傳古之學至於處置水利以便漕運一節允鑿鑿可行其識見不凡之士歟〕
考試官教諭李　批〔識時務者在俊傑非子其誰耶〕
對謀大事者必有周天下之慮成大功者
必有兼天下之材彼東南封疆財賦所出
天下事功未有大於是者茍偏執已見不
采衆論是之曰小小可以謀事乎患得患
失畏首畏尾是之曰弱弱可以成功乎必
punctuated:
之公，僅見董狐，班馬而下，不能不起人之非議。況數子言論之當否、人品之高下，聖門之徒、儒先之碩，已嘗論之詳矣。鯫生小子，豈容贅言？雖然，言及之而不言，又恐取侍君子之愆也。謹對。

第五問
逸貢

同考試官教諭張　批〔漕運一策，正欲觀士子用世之學。此篇條答詳悉，斟酌得宜，其識見出人一頭地。他日施下有政，必有可觀者。噫！得士如此，可以增重矣。〕

考試官教諭張　批〔觀此策，非惟有傳古之學，至於處置水利以便漕運一節，允鑿鑿可行。其識見不凡之士歟！〕

考試官教諭李　批〔識時務者在俊傑，非子其誰耶？〕

對：謀大事者，必有周天下之慮；成大功者，必有兼天下之材。彼東南封疆，財賦所出，天下事功未有大於是者。茍偏執已見，不采衆論，是之曰小，小可以謀事乎？患得患失，畏首畏尾，是之曰弱，弱可以成功乎？必
translation_en:
…impartiality in judging right and wrong is seen scarcely anywhere but in Dong Hu. From Ban Gu and Sima Qian onward, historians have inevitably provoked criticism. Moreover, the soundness of these men's pronouncements and the relative quality of their characters have already been discussed in detail by disciples of the Sage and eminent Confucian predecessors. How could an insignificant student such as myself presume to add anything? Nevertheless, if I remain silent when the subject has arisen, I fear committing a fault in attending upon a gentleman. Respectfully submitted.

Fifth Question
Yi Gong 逸貢 [?]

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔This policy question on grain transport was intended precisely to assess the candidates' learning for practical service. This essay answers each point fully and in detail, weighing matters appropriately; its insight stands head and shoulders above others. When he undertakes government in the future [?], there will surely be something worth seeing. Ah! Recruiting such a scholar can bring added distinction!〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Judging from this policy essay, he possesses more than learning that transmits antiquity. His discussion of managing waterways to facilitate grain transport is indeed concrete and practicable. Surely he is a scholar of exceptional insight!〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Those who understand the demands of the times are outstanding talents. If not you, who else?〕

Response: Those who plan great undertakings must think comprehensively about all under Heaven; those who achieve great accomplishments must possess abilities encompassing all under Heaven. The southeastern territories are the source of wealth and tax revenue: no undertaking in the realm is greater than this. If one stubbornly clings to one's own opinions and does not consider the views of others, this is called narrowness. Can a narrow-minded person plan an undertaking? To fret over gaining and losing, fearing what lies both ahead and behind, is called weakness. Can a weak person achieve success? It is essential …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也典籍之記載取之耳目之見聞亦取之
朝堂之議取之芻蕘之言亦取之合衆論
之公斷一己之獨則天下無遺策矣胼胝
之勞不憂盤錯之交不亂萬變之應不窮
千夫之撼不動左右逢原整暇有序則天
下無遺才矣何大事之不可謀大功之不
可成耶請因明問以對古者九州之域不
出中原江南嶺表皆為裔服江浙之地唐
虞何有焉封建之制王畿千里貢賦之來
===
不過五百里侯國百里貢賦之來不過五
十里漕運之法禹貢何錄焉下至春秋吳
於邗溝築城始穿城壕之水東北通射陽
湖西北至末口入淮以通粮道此漕運之
權輿也於民何病至秦始皇代匈奴飛芻
輓粟起於琅邪負海之郡轉輸河北率三
十鍾而致一石此漕運之桎梏也於民奚
堪漢之初年京師之需仰給近郡諸侯之
粟不歸天子當時關東之漕僅數十萬石
punctuated:
也，典籍之記載取之，耳目之見聞亦取之；朝堂之議取之，芻蕘之言亦取之。合衆論之公，斷一己之獨，則天下無遺策矣。胼胝之勞不憂，盤錯之交不亂，萬變之應不窮，千夫之撼不動，左右逢原，整暇有序，則天下無遺才矣。何大事之不可謀、大功之不可成耶？請因明問以對。
古者九州之域不出中原，江南嶺表皆為裔服，江浙之地，唐虞何有焉？封建之制，王畿千里，貢賦之來不過五百里；侯國百里，貢賦之來不過五十里。漕運之法，《禹貢》何錄焉？下至春秋，吳於邗溝築城，始穿城壕之水，東北通射陽湖，西北至末口入淮，以通粮道。此漕運之權輿也，於民何病？至秦始皇代匈奴，飛芻輓粟，起於琅邪負海之郡，轉輸河北，率三十鍾而致一石。此漕運之桎梏也，於民奚堪？漢之初年，京師之需仰給近郡，諸侯之粟不歸天子，當時關東之漕僅數十萬石
translation_en:
…one must draw upon the records in the classics and other writings, and also upon what one has seen and heard; draw upon deliberations at court, and also upon the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers. Combine the impartial judgment of many opinions and reach an independent decision oneself: then no sound plan under Heaven will be overlooked. Do not shrink from labor that raises calluses; do not become confused by entangled difficulties; respond inexhaustibly to myriad changes; remain unmoved when a thousand men try to shake you. Find resources on every side, remaining composed and orderly: then no talent under Heaven will go unused. What great undertaking could not be planned, what great achievement could not be accomplished? Allow me to reply to your illuminating question.
In antiquity, the territory of the Nine Provinces did not extend beyond the Central Plain. The lands south of the Yangzi and beyond the southern ranges were all outer domains. What place did the lands of Jiangsu and Zhejiang have under Yao and Shun? Under the system of enfeoffment, the royal domain measured a thousand li across, and tribute and taxes came from no farther than five hundred li away; a lord’s domain measured a hundred li across, and tribute and taxes came from no farther than fifty li away. What system of grain transport by water did the Tribute of Yu record? Later, in the Spring and Autumn period, Wu built a city at Hangou and first excavated waterways from its moat, connecting northeastward with Sheyang Lake and northwestward to Mokou, where they entered the Huai River, thus opening a grain supply route. This was the beginning of grain transport by water: what hardship did it cause the people? When the First Emperor of Qin campaigned against [?] the Xiongnu, fodder was rushed forward and grain hauled from Langye and other coastal commanderies to the lands north of the Yellow River. Typically, thirty zhong of grain were expended to deliver one shi. These were the fetters imposed by grain transport: how could the people endure them? In the early years of the Han, the capital relied on nearby commanderies for its supplies, while the grain of the feudal lords did not go to the Son of Heaven. At that time, grain transported by water from east of the passes amounted to only a few hundred thousand shi…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而已武帝時從河東守番系之請山東益
漕至百餘萬石繼而奴婢之沒禽獸之養
糜費無經遡益爲四百萬石又繼而北伐
匈奴西通月氏神仙土木纍纍相繼又增
爲六百萬石嗚呼漢武之末去秦寧幾何
耶雖然漢之財賦仰於山東唐之財賦則
仰於江淮德宗之時韓滉轉運江淮之米
未至六軍脫巾於道及其既至則喜謂太
子曰吾父子得生矣遂置酒相慶憂喜死
===
生如在目前唐人倚辦之急可知矣代宗
之時劉晏領漕江南之運積揚州汴河之
運積河陰河船積渭口渭船入太倉泝河
入渭隨處停貯唐人講畫之詳可見矣宋
有閉口之制十月則舟楫不行所以節民
力也王安石欲通冬運則以船艘數十設
碓擣氷役夫苦寒死者甚衆漕法其一變
也宋有轉般之法江不入汴汴不入江所
以習水勢也曾孝緒爲無代發遡令六路
punctuated: 而已。武帝時，從河東守番系之請，山東益漕至百餘萬石。繼而奴婢之沒、禽獸之養，糜費無經，遡益爲四百萬石。又繼而北伐匈奴，西通月氏，神仙土木纍纍相繼，又增爲六百萬石。嗚呼！漢武之末，去秦寧幾何耶？雖然，漢之財賦仰於山東，唐之財賦則仰於江淮。德宗之時，韓滉轉運江淮之米未至，六軍脫巾於道；及其既至，則喜謂太子曰：「吾父子得生矣！」遂置酒相慶。憂喜死生，如在目前，唐人倚辦之急可知矣。代宗之時，劉晏領漕，江南之運積揚州，汴河之運積河陰，河船積渭口，渭船入太倉。泝河入渭，隨處停貯，唐人講畫之詳可見矣。宋有閉口之制，十月則舟楫不行，所以節民力也。王安石欲通冬運，則以船艘數十，設碓擣氷，役夫苦寒，死者甚衆，漕法其一變也。宋有轉般之法，江不入汴，汴不入江，所以習水勢也。曾孝緒爲無代發，遡令六路
translation_en:
…and no more. In Emperor Wu’s reign, following the proposal of Fan Xi, governor of Hedong, grain shipments from Shandong increased to more than one million shi. Subsequently, the confiscation of male and female slaves and the keeping of birds and beasts entailed expenditure without restraint, and shipments increased further [?] to four million shi. Then came campaigns north against the Xiongnu and the opening of communications westward with the Yuezhi. Pursuits of immortality and construction projects followed one after another, and shipments increased again to six million shi. Alas! By the end of Emperor Wu’s reign, how far was the Han from the Qin? Nevertheless, whereas Han revenues depended on Shandong, Tang revenues depended on the Jiang–Huai region.

In Emperor Dezong’s reign, before the rice that Han Huang was transporting from the Jiang–Huai region had arrived, the soldiers of the Six Armies removed their headcloths in the roads. Once it arrived, the emperor joyfully told the heir apparent: “We, father and son, can live!” He then had wine set out to celebrate. Anxiety and joy, death and life, seemed immediately before their eyes: one can see how urgently the Tang depended on these supplies. In Emperor Daizong’s reign, Liu Yan directed grain transport. Shipments from Jiangnan were stored at Yangzhou; shipments along the Bian River were stored at Heyin; cargoes carried by Yellow River boats were stored at the mouth of the Wei; and Wei River boats entered the Court of the Imperial Granaries. Proceeding upstream along the Yellow River into the Wei, cargoes were held in storage at successive points. One can see how thoroughly the Tang planned these arrangements.

The Song had a system of closing the waterway entrances: in the tenth month, boats ceased to travel, thereby conserving the people’s labor. Wang Anshi wished to permit winter transport, so he equipped several dozen boats with trip-hammers to pound the ice. The laborers suffered bitter cold, and very many died. This was one change in the grain-transport system. The Song also had a system of transshipment: Yangzi River boats did not enter the Bian, and Bian River boats did not enter the Yangzi, so that crews would be familiar with the conditions of their waterways. Zeng Xiaoxu, because there were no replacement shipments [?], then ordered the six circuits …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
郡縣各總歲額雖湖南至遠之地亦直抵
京師漕法又一變也元都燕京注意河防
者有二初以伯顏之議造平底海船運糧
京師而韓仲暉等復言自安山開河北至
臨清凡二百五十餘里引汶絶濟直屬衛
漳度地高低建閘蓄洩名曰會通河以代
海運民甚便之我
太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵天下財賦悉趨南都北
運不興而會通河遂淤繼以郭守敬之議
===
鑿通州至大都為河引昌平白浮村一畝
玉泉之水注之設閘啓閉名曰通惠河運
舟自直沽而來者得以徑到大都民亦便
之尋以地高水淺隨脩隨罷
國朝因之興廢如故夫通州切近京師通惠
之河不講可也會通之河廼
國家糧運之咽喉講之容可緩乎我
太宗文皇帝都北之初遂脩是河復元之舊呈
十三年海運始罷然是河之水發源於萊
punctuated: 郡縣各總歲額，雖湖南至遠之地，亦直抵京師，漕法又一變也。元都燕京，注意河防者有二。初以伯顏之議，造平底海船運糧京師，而韓仲暉等復言，自安山開河北至臨清，凡二百五十餘里，引汶絶濟，直屬衛漳，度地高低，建閘蓄洩，名曰會通河，以代海運，民甚便之。我太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵，天下財賦悉趨南都，北運不興，而會通河遂淤。繼以郭守敬之議，鑿通州至大都為河，引昌平白浮村一畝玉泉之水注之，設閘啓閉，名曰通惠河。運舟自直沽而來者，得以徑到大都，民亦便之。尋以地高水淺，隨脩隨罷。國朝因之，興廢如故。夫通州切近京師，通惠之河不講可也；會通之河，廼國家糧運之咽喉，講之容可緩乎？我太宗文皇帝都北之初，遂脩是河，復元之舊，呈十三年海運始罷。然是河之水，發源於萊
translation_en:
…the prefectures and counties each took charge of their annual quotas; even shipments from places as distant as Hunan went directly to the capital. This was another change in the grain-transport system.

The Yuan established their capital at Yanjing and undertook two major initiatives concerning river management. Initially, on Bayan’s proposal, they built flat-bottomed seagoing vessels to transport grain to the capital. Han Zhonghui and others subsequently proposed digging a canal northward from Anshan to Linqing, a distance of more than 250 li, diverting the Wen River across the Ji River to connect directly with the Wei and Zhang rivers. They surveyed the elevations of the land and built sluices to retain and release water. This was named the Huitong Canal and replaced sea transport; the people found it very convenient.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao established his capital at Jinling. The empire’s tax revenues all flowed toward the southern capital, transport northward was not maintained, and the Huitong Canal consequently silted up. Subsequently, on Guo Shoujing’s proposal, a canal was excavated from Tongzhou to Dadu. Water from Baifu Village in Changping and from Yimu and Yuquan [?] was diverted into it, and sluices were installed to open and close the flow. It was named the Tonghui Canal. Transport vessels coming from Zhigu could thereby reach Dadu directly, and the people likewise found it convenient. Before long, because the terrain was high and the water shallow, repairs were repeatedly followed by abandonment. Our dynasty inherited this situation, and the same cycle of restoration and disuse continued.

Now Tongzhou is very close to the capital, so it might be permissible not to attend to the Tonghui Canal. But the Huitong Canal is the vital passage for the state’s grain transport: can attention to it possibly be delayed? When our Emperor Taizong Wen first established his capital in the north, he accordingly repaired this canal, restoring its former Yuan condition. Only in the thirteenth year [?] was sea transport discontinued. The water of this canal, however, originates at Lai…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山徂徠諸澗合流於汶泗洸濟諸河自濟
以南則合淮泗自濟以北則屬衛漳初與
黃河不相統也爲其不通黃河故水源淺
薄潞雨則溪澗漫溢旱乾則水脉微細運
舟通塞仰望天時近者黃陵岡一決於河
南而安平鎮口遂傾於東海幸而黃河源
深勢猛傾海之外餘波尚在故運舟經口
雖未免於費力而離口上下則自在乎中
流是害我漕運此黃河也利我漕運亦此
黃河也彼黃陵岡不塞則安平鎮口不得
收功固確論也舍安平鎮口而倡爲海運
之說固疎謀也以故二三年之間重㢄
聖慮疊遣重臣今黃陵岡已免奔決而安平鎮
口亦無傾注其功豈不偉歟但恐旱暵之
餘閘河乾淺視昔尤甚運舟之行比昔尤
艱明問及此可謂遠慮生之謬論則曰以
兩口未塞之先論之當於安山以北去處
通海隄岸多作減水壩以殺黃陵岡之奔
punctuated: 山、徂徠諸澗，合流於汶、泗、洸、濟諸河。自濟以南，則合淮、泗；自濟以北，則屬衛、漳。初與黃河不相統也。爲其不通黃河，故水源淺薄，潞雨則溪澗漫溢，旱乾則水脉微細，運舟通塞，仰望天時。近者黃陵岡一決於河南，而安平鎮口遂傾於東海。幸而黃河源深勢猛，傾海之外，餘波尚在，故運舟經口，雖未免於費力，而離口上下，則自在乎中流。是害我漕運，此黃河也；利我漕運，亦此黃河也。彼黃陵岡不塞，則安平鎮口不得收功，固確論也；舍安平鎮口而倡爲海運之說，固疎謀也。以故二三年之間，重㢄聖慮，疊遣重臣。今黃陵岡已免奔決，而安平鎮口亦無傾注，其功豈不偉歟？但恐旱暵之餘，閘河乾淺，視昔尤甚；運舟之行，比昔尤艱。明問及此，可謂遠慮。生之謬論則曰：以兩口未塞之先論之，當於安山以北去處，通海隄岸，多作減水壩，以殺黃陵岡之奔
translation_en: …the mountain and the various gullies of Culai, whose waters converge in the Wen, Si, Guang, and Ji rivers. South of the Ji, they join the Huai and Si; north of the Ji, they connect with the Wei and Zhang. Originally, they had no connection with the Yellow River. Because they were not connected to it, their water supply was scant: in rainy weather [?], streams and gullies overflowed, while in drought their flow dwindled to a trickle. Whether transport boats could pass depended upon the weather. Recently, once the Yellow River breached its banks at Huanglinggang in Henan, water poured through the opening at Anpingzhen toward the eastern sea. Fortunately, the Yellow River has an abundant source and a powerful current; beyond the water discharged into the sea, some flow still remained. Thus, although transport boats inevitably struggled to pass the opening, once clear of it they could move freely upstream and downstream in mid-channel. It is this Yellow River that harms our grain transport, and this same Yellow River that benefits it. The assertion that work at the Anpingzhen opening cannot succeed unless the breach at Huanglinggang is closed is certainly sound. To abandon the Anpingzhen opening and advocate maritime transport is certainly an ill-considered plan. Consequently, over the past two or three years this matter has repeatedly troubled [?] His Majesty, who has sent high ministers on successive missions. Now Huanglinggang is no longer subject to rushing floodwaters breaking through, and water no longer pours out through the Anpingzhen opening. Is this not a magnificent achievement? Yet I fear that after a drought, the canal controlled by sluices will be even drier and shallower than before, and passage for transport boats even more difficult. Your discerning question addresses this; it may indeed be called farsighted. This student's humble opinion is as follows: considering the situation before the two openings were closed, numerous overflow weirs should have been built along the embankments leading toward the sea in the area north of Anshan, to diminish the rushing waters from Huanglinggang…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
流平窪之地多作陂湖以收黃陵岡之餘
波如此則水勢既分其力自薄安平鎮口
之塞當不竢崇朝矣安平鎮既塞其口則
運船無虞黃陵岡既分其勢則漕河不竭
是黃河之水昔為我擾者今為我助此一
策也以兩口既塞之後論之天旱河乾理
勢或然又當於濟寧上下近河之所如南
旺湖積水澤鉅野澤悉皆去河咫尺且每
湖寬廣不啻百里若濬深其湖底高厚其
===
隄岸當河之面設閘閘閘俾四時雨澤皆
瀦積其中湖水視河勢高八九餘尺隨旱
分數起板濟河又於各方泉眼悉加挑濬
數泉所會亦要鑿為一湖高厚啓閉悉如
前法舊湖被人侵種者改正之新湖該納
稅糧者除豁之勿顧一時小利而忘百世
大功此又塞口之後緊要一良策也若或
不此之務而徒區區於挑淺築壩封閘起
夗是為無策也愚敢以是為終篇對將以
punctuated:
流，平窪之地多作陂湖，以收黃陵岡之餘波。如此，則水勢既分，其力自薄，安平鎮口之塞，當不竢崇朝矣。安平鎮既塞其口，則運船無虞；黃陵岡既分其勢，則漕河不竭。是黃河之水昔為我擾者，今為我助，此一策也。
以兩口既塞之後論之，天旱河乾，理勢或然。又當於濟寧上下近河之所，如南旺湖、積水澤、鉅野澤，悉皆去河咫尺，且每湖寬廣不啻百里。若濬深其湖底，高厚其隄岸，當河之面設閘閘閘，俾四時雨澤皆瀦積其中，湖水視河勢高八九餘尺，隨旱分數起板濟河。又於各方泉眼悉加挑濬，數泉所會，亦要鑿為一湖，高厚啓閉，悉如前法。舊湖被人侵種者，改正之；新湖該納稅糧者，除豁之。勿顧一時小利，而忘百世大功。此又塞口之後緊要一良策也。若或不此之務，而徒區區於挑淺、築壩、封閘、起夗，是為無策也。愚敢以是為終篇，對將以
translation_en:
…current; in flat, low-lying places, numerous reservoirs and lakes should be made to receive the surplus waters from Huanglinggang. In this way, once the flow has been divided, its force will naturally diminish, and closing the breach at Anpingzhen should not take even a full morning. Once the breach at Anpingzhen has been closed, transport vessels will be free from danger; once the force of the waters at Huanglinggang has been divided, the grain-transport canal will not run dry. Thus the waters of the Yellow River, which formerly troubled us, will now assist us. This is one policy.
Considering the situation after both breaches have been closed, drought and a dry river are entirely possible in the natural course of things. There are also places near the river above and below Jining, such as Nanwang Lake, Jishui Marsh, and Juye Marsh, all situated a mere stone’s throw from the river; moreover, each lake extends over no fewer than a hundred li. If their beds were dredged deeper, their embankments raised and thickened, and sluice gates installed on the side facing the river [the transcription repeats “gate” three times, ?], rainfall throughout the four seasons could all be stored within them. With the lake water eight or nine chi or more above the river level, the sluice boards could be raised according to the severity of the drought to replenish the river. Furthermore, all springs in the surrounding areas should be cleared and dredged. Wherever several springs converge, a lake should likewise be excavated; the height and thickness of its embankments and the opening and closing of its sluices should all follow the method described above. Where people have encroached upon existing lakes to cultivate them, this should be rectified; where land used for new lakes is liable for grain taxes, those obligations should be remitted. Do not attend to the small profits of a moment and forget a great achievement that will benefit a hundred generations. This is another sound policy of urgent importance after the breaches have been closed. If, instead of pursuing this, one merely busies oneself with dredging shallows, building dams, sealing sluices, and “raising wan” [?], this amounts to having no policy at all. I venture, in my humble judgment, to conclude this essay with these proposals, intending to offer this response as…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
為吾
聖天子
獻焉
punctuated: 為吾聖天子獻焉。
translation_en: …to offer it to our sage Son of Heaven.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
弘治乙卯秋山東循例舉士
士論定而小錄成澤竊序其
後曰昔人有言科目取士無
情如造化至公如權衡蓋以
防禁之嚴緘縢之密一付之
無心也以無心取士則取士
===
未有不得者而或又謂其徒
以言爾言果不足以取人乎
㦲孟子以知言自負謂知其
言則知其心而因有以知其
政事且期以聖人復起不能
易所論其自信之審如此非
無見也近世有讀范仲淹金
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

弘治乙卯秋，山東循例舉士。士論定而小錄成，澤竊序其後曰：昔人有言：「科目取士，無情如造化，至公如權衡。」蓋以防禁之嚴、緘縢之密，一付之無心也。以無心取士，則取士未有不得者。而或又謂其徒以言爾。言果不足以取人乎㦲？孟子以知言自負，謂知其言則知其心，而因有以知其政事，且期以聖人復起不能易所論。其自信之審如此，非無見也。近世有讀范仲淹《金
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the yimao year of the Hongzhi reign (1495), Shandong selected men according to established practice. Once the assessments of the candidates had been settled and this brief record completed, I, Ze, ventured to append this postface:

Someone of old said: “Selecting men through the examinations is as free from personal feeling as the workings of creation, and as perfectly impartial as a balance.” This is because strict safeguards and prohibitions, together with securely sealed papers, entrust the entire process to impersonal judgment. When men are selected without personal bias, the selection never fails to find suitable men. Yet some say that it relies merely on words. Are words indeed insufficient grounds for selecting men?

Mencius prided himself on understanding words. He held that knowing a person's words meant knowing his mind, and thereby provided a means of knowing his conduct of government. He was moreover confident that, even were a sage to arise again, that sage could not alter his conclusions. Such was the firmness of his conviction; it was not without insight. In more recent times, someone, on reading Fan Zhongyan's “Metal …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
在鎔賦則知其為文武全材
讀王孝先賦有物混成則知
其為宰相器讀蘇子瞻刑賞
忠厚之至論則知其為異人
因目之以國士讀文天祥廷
對策則知其忠肝如鐵石若
此者皆以言取也徵之他日
===
諸公名位之隆德業之盛文
章節義之高照耀人世果相
符而不相背孰謂言不足以
取人歟自有科目之法來豪
傑之士皆由此出歷千百年
而英君誼辟不能改其法非
不能改也設令外此而求士
punctuated: 在鎔賦》，則知其為文武全材；讀王孝先《賦有物混成》，則知其為宰相器；讀蘇子瞻《刑賞忠厚之至論》，則知其為異人，因目之以國士；讀文天祥廷對策，則知其忠肝如鐵石。若此者，皆以言取也。徵之他日，諸公名位之隆、德業之盛、文章節義之高，照耀人世，果相符而不相背，孰謂言不足以取人歟？自有科目之法來，豪傑之士皆由此出。歷千百年，而英君誼辟不能改其法，非不能改也，設令外此而求士，
translation_en:
…[Rhapsody on Metal] in the Crucible, one knew that its author possessed complete talents for both civil and military affairs. Reading Wang Xiaoxian’s rhapsody “There Is Something Undifferentiated and Complete,” one knew that he had the capacity of a chief councilor. Reading Su Zizhan’s “Discourse on the Utmost Loyalty and Generosity in Punishments and Rewards,” one knew that he was an extraordinary man and accordingly regarded him as a man of outstanding worth to the state. Reading Wen Tianxiang’s policy essay in response to questions at court, one knew that his loyalty was as firm as iron and stone. In such cases, men were all judged by their words. When tested against their later lives, the eminence of these gentlemen’s names and positions, the fullness of their virtue and achievements, and the loftiness of their writings, integrity, and righteousness shone upon the world. These indeed accorded with those judgments and did not contradict them. Who could say that words are insufficient grounds for selecting men?

Ever since the establishment of the examination system, men of outstanding ability have all emerged through it. Over hundreds and thousands of years, enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns have been unable to change this system. It is not that they lacked the power to change it: suppose they were to seek worthy men outside it…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
則必至於紛紜不激於遠嫌
必昵於比周果能如造化如
權衡爭夫科目本不為取士
之病徒以操其柄者自病之
耳誣經詭聖曲學阿世或至
於中選而平易說理立論正
大者或至於見黜此孰是而
===
議者得以張其喙焉苟操其
柄者虛心果能如造化如權
衡則不得人不為憂矣我
國家養士於學校而以言取士
於科目歷百有二十餘年而
不變士之遭逢其盛其所以
感奮磨礪期以應
punctuated:
則必至於紛紜，不激於遠嫌，必昵於比周。果能如造化、如權衡爭？夫科目本不為取士之病，徒以操其柄者自病之耳。誣經詭聖，曲學阿世，或至於中選；而平易說理、立論正大者，或至於見黜。此孰是而議者得以張其喙焉？苟操其柄者虛心，果能如造化、如權衡，則不得人不為憂矣。
我國家養士於學校，而以言取士於科目，歷百有二十餘年而不變。士之遭逢其盛，其所以感奮磨礪，期以應
translation_en:
…then confusion would inevitably ensue: unless driven to extremes in avoiding suspicion, one would inevitably become entangled in favoritism and cliques. Could one truly be like the workings of creation, like a weighing balance [?]? The examination system itself is no impediment to recruiting worthy men; it is simply those who wield its authority who introduce the faults. Those who misrepresent the Classics, distort the sages’ teachings, twist their learning, and flatter their age may be selected, while those who explain principles plainly and advance upright and honorable arguments may be rejected. Who is responsible for this [?], giving critics grounds to open their mouths? If those who wield this authority set aside their preconceptions and truly act like the workings of creation and a weighing balance, there will be no need to worry about failing to obtain worthy men.
Our dynasty nurtures scholars in schools and selects them through their written words in the examinations. This practice has remained unchanged for more than one hundred and twenty years. Scholars fortunate enough to encounter such flourishing times are therefore inspired to exert themselves and hone their abilities, hoping thereby to answer…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
上之求者固非徒能言而行不逮
者也况諸士生長鄒魯之邦
游歌大聖大賢之故鄉其風
聲氣習之所熏炙必將以聖
賢自期待言之所試實心之
所養焉浮艷不成令器如玉
師旦之所論者若遠去矣澤
===
濫竊校文之柄自分不能窮
理不敢以知言借擬至於所
取諸士得列名於是錄者則
敢以為范為王為蘇為文望
之也嗚呼諸士其肯負所望
以負
國家養士求士之盛心哉
punctuated:
上之求者，固非徒能言而行不逮者也。况諸士生長鄒魯之邦，游歌大聖大賢之故鄉，其風聲氣習之所熏炙，必將以聖賢自期待。言之所試，實心之所養焉。浮艷不成令器，如玉師旦之所論者，若遠去矣。
澤濫竊校文之柄，自分不能窮理，不敢以知言借擬。至於所取諸士得列名於是錄者，則敢以為范、為王、為蘇、為文望之也。嗚呼！諸士其肯負所望，以負國家養士求士之盛心哉？
translation_en:
…the demands of the throne are surely not men who merely speak well but fall short in their conduct. Moreover, these scholars were born and raised in the lands of Zou and Lu, studying and singing in the homeland of the great sage and the great worthy. Nurtured by its inherited moral influence and customs, they will surely aspire to become sages and worthies themselves. What is tested through their words is what they have cultivated in their hearts. Superficial brilliance that fails to produce men of worth, of the sort discussed by Yu Shidan [?], would seem far removed from them.
I, Ze, have undeservedly assumed authority over the assessment of examination writings. Knowing my own inability to fathom principles fully, I dare not claim the capacity to discern men through their words. Yet for the scholars I have selected, whose names appear in this record, I venture to hope that they will become men like Fan, Wang, Su, and Wen. Ah! Would these scholars willingly disappoint such hopes, and thereby betray the state's earnest intention in nurturing and seeking worthy men?

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
直隸滁州來安縣儒學教諭
張澤謹序
punctuated: 直隸滁州來安縣儒學教諭張澤謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully written by Zhang Ze, Instructor in the Confucian School of Lai’an County, Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試録序
弘治八年當天下賔興賢能
之期山東守臣豫以試事白
鎮守山東都知監太監李〔全〕
廵撫山東都察院右僉都御
史熊〔翀〕咸曰重事境内春夏
不雨恐費涉于民宜慎行之
===
又白於監察御史周津邵蕃
亦曰雨不時若舉茲大事宜
慎繼是監察御史曹鳳来按
茲土實專監臨之寄憫時不
雨百凡之務戒所司務存省
約故民心胥悅未幾天乃雨
仁等膺聘而来入其境見人
punctuated:
山東鄉試録序

弘治八年，當天下賔興賢能之期，山東守臣豫以試事白鎮守山東都知監太監李〔全〕、廵撫山東都察院右僉都御史熊〔翀〕，咸曰：「重事。境内春夏不雨，恐費涉于民，宜慎行之。」

又白於監察御史周津、邵蕃，亦曰：「雨不時若，舉茲大事宜慎。」繼是，監察御史曹鳳来按茲土，實專監臨之寄。憫時不雨，百凡之務，戒所司務存省約，故民心胥悅。未幾，天乃雨。仁等膺聘而来，入其境，見人
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the eighth year of Hongzhi [1495], when the time came for honoring and selecting worthy and capable men throughout the realm, the officials governing Shandong reported the examination arrangements in advance to Li Quan, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Palace Surveillance, stationed in Shandong as Regional Defender, and Xiong Chong, Grand Coordinator of Shandong and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. Both said: “This is a weighty undertaking. There has been no rain within the province throughout spring and summer. We fear that the expense may fall upon the people; the arrangements should be made with care.”

They also reported to Investigating Censors Zhou Jin and Shao Fan, who likewise said: “The rains have not come in due season. Care must be taken in conducting this great undertaking.” Subsequently, Investigating Censor Cao Feng came to inspect this territory and was entrusted with sole responsibility as Supervising Official. Concerned by the lack of rain at that time, he instructed the responsible authorities to practice economy in every aspect of their work. The people were therefore all pleased. Before long, Heaven sent rain. We—Ren and the others—came in response to our invitations, and upon entering the province saw the people …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
皆以得雨為喜然猶未饒洽
也比入院聞垤鸛有聲溽氣
鬱蒸而釀雨明日雨下沛然
又明日初場猶霏微弗止於
是優渥霑足穀秀而實上下
交相歡慶諸士在場屋握管
對雨亦躍躍有喜色著為文
===
章理以澤而詞以潤也迨後
二場天開雨霽士氣倍奮夫
陰陽氣上薄為雨乘空而墜
驟則為涷小則為霢霂皆足
以澤物我
國家養士於學校而取之以科
目優其廩復其家給人以代
punctuated:
皆以得雨為喜，然猶未饒洽也。比入院，聞垤鸛有聲，溽氣鬱蒸而釀雨。明日，雨下沛然；又明日，初場，猶霏微弗止。於是優渥霑足，穀秀而實，上下交相歡慶。諸士在場屋，握管對雨，亦躍躍有喜色，著為文章，理以澤而詞以潤也。迨後二場，天開雨霽，士氣倍奮。
夫陰陽氣上薄為雨，乘空而墜，驟則為涷，小則為霢霂，皆足以澤物。我國家養士於學校，而取之以科目，優其廩，復其家，給人以代
translation_en:
…everyone rejoiced at receiving rain, though it had not yet thoroughly soaked the land. By the time we entered the examination compound, we heard storks calling on their mounds; humid vapors rose thickly, brewing rain. The next day, rain fell abundantly. On the following day, when the first session was held, a fine drizzle still continued without cease. Thus the land received a generous and thorough soaking, and the grain flowered and filled out. Those above and below joined in joyful celebration. The candidates in the examination halls, brushes in hand as they faced the rain, likewise showed eager delight. This found expression in their compositions: their reasoning was enriched and their language imbued with freshness. By the latter two sessions, the sky had cleared and the rain had ceased, and the candidates’ spirits were redoubled.
Now, the vapors of yin and yang rise and meet to form rain, which falls through the air. When it comes violently, it is a downpour; when lightly, a drizzle. Both suffice to nourish things. Our dynasty nurtures scholars in its schools and selects them through the examinations. It provides them generous stipends, exempts their households from labor service, and supplies others to take their place in…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
其使令愛護匡翼靡不周至
正猶天之於嘉穀既沃以涷
又益以霡霂而所以資其發
生者厚也況諸齊魯之士生
長聖賢之鄉私淑乎時雨之
化而脩之已者亦自有素焉
則夫今日之登名是選信非
===
偶然耶盍亦思乎士之未遇
固如穀之未成日望乎雨澤
之加及其既遇則如穀之已
熟人將仰其澤以為生矣苟
徒僥倖於一得不思推厥素
如雨之施以澤物寧不有孤
國家養士之盛心哉故古之君
punctuated: 其使令，愛護匡翼，靡不周至。正猶天之於嘉穀，既沃以涷，又益以霡霂，而所以資其發生者厚也。況諸齊魯之士，生長聖賢之鄉，私淑乎時雨之化，而脩之已者亦自有素焉。則夫今日之登名是選，信非偶然耶？盍亦思乎？士之未遇，固如穀之未成，日望乎雨澤之加；及其既遇，則如穀之已熟，人將仰其澤以為生矣。苟徒僥倖於一得，不思推厥素，如雨之施以澤物，寧不有孤國家養士之盛心哉？故古之君
translation_en:
…their errands; in its care, protection, support, and assistance, nothing is left unattended. This is just like Heaven’s treatment of fine grain: having watered it with heavy rain, it adds gentle showers, generously providing what sustains its sprouting and growth. Moreover, the scholars of Qi and Lu have grown up in the homeland of sages and worthies. Though not taught by them directly, they have benefited from their transforming influence, like timely rain, and have long cultivated themselves [?]. Surely their names appearing among those selected today is no accident?

Should they not also reflect on this? Before scholars gain recognition, they are indeed like grain not yet mature, daily hoping for the blessing of rain. Once they gain recognition, however, they are like ripened grain: others will look to their beneficence for their livelihood. If they merely count themselves fortunate in a single success and fail to extend what they have long cultivated—bestowing benefits upon others as rain nourishes all things—would they not betray the dynasty’s generous intention in nurturing scholars? Thus the exemplary men of antiquity…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
子不以登名爲榮而以成功
爲慊繼自今諸士将爲時所
用必隨厥任盡厥職居民牧
則爲百里萬之隨車雨以蘇
一郡一邑之枯槁司風紀則
爲顔魯公之御史雨以洗一
道之寃滯處
===
廟堂則爲商相之三日雨以慰
四海九州之仰望飛甘灑澍
作休徵於治世上有以啓沃
乎
君心下有以膏澤乎民生此則大
丈夫之事固諸士之所當自
負亦
punctuated: 子不以登名爲榮，而以成功爲慊。繼自今，諸士将爲時所用，必隨厥任，盡厥職。居民牧，則爲百里萬之隨車雨，以蘇一郡一邑之枯槁；司風紀，則爲顔魯公之御史雨，以洗一道之寃滯；處廟堂，則爲商相之三日雨，以慰四海九州之仰望。飛甘灑澍，作休徵於治世，上有以啓沃乎君心，下有以膏澤乎民生。此則大丈夫之事，固諸士之所當自負，亦
translation_en: …gentlemen did not regard having their names entered on the list as glory, but found satisfaction in accomplishing their work. From this time forward, when you gentlemen are employed in the service of the age, you must fulfill the duties of whatever appointments you receive. If you serve as shepherds of the people, become like the rain that followed the carriage of Baili Wan [?], reviving what has withered in a prefecture or county. If you oversee official conduct and discipline, become like the censor’s rain of Yan, Duke of Lu, washing away the unresolved injustices of an entire circuit. If you serve at court, become like the three days’ rain of the Shang minister, fulfilling the hopes of all within the Four Seas and the Nine Provinces. Send sweet rain flying and scatter timely showers, becoming auspicious signs in a well-governed age: above, enlightening and nourishing the sovereign’s mind; below, bringing bounty to the people’s livelihoods. This is the work of a great man, a responsibility you gentlemen should assuredly take upon yourselves, and also…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
國家之有待於我者也仁昧於
知言辱諸士為集門杞梓敢
托諸雨致祝䂓之意以僣序
小錄之成凡有事于茲者仁
與教諭張〔澤〕為考試官教諭
張〔瀚〕朱〔文魁〕王〔翰〕邵〔清〕訓導
陸〔紳〕李〔士元〕楊〔勑〕為同考試
===
官左布政使吳〔琠〕按察使趙
〔鶴齡〕左叅政林〔元甫〕僉事馮
〔鎬〕則提調監試於內右布政
使柳〔淳〕左右叅政張〔銳〕劉〔聰〕
副使劉〔福〕陳〔璧〕廖〔中〕王〔紳〕郝
〔志義〕左右叅議杜〔整〕周〔紘〕僉
事陳〔寬〕鈕〔清〕陳〔嘉謨〕胡〔富〕則
punctuated:
國家之有待於我者也。仁昧於知言，辱諸士為集門杞梓，敢托諸雨致祝䂓之意，以僣序小錄之成。

凡有事于茲者，仁與教諭張〔澤〕為考試官，教諭張〔瀚〕、朱〔文魁〕、王〔翰〕、邵〔清〕，訓導陸〔紳〕、李〔士元〕、楊〔勑〕為同考試官。左布政使吳〔琠〕、按察使趙〔鶴齡〕、左叅政林〔元甫〕、僉事馮〔鎬〕則提調監試於內；右布政使柳〔淳〕、左右叅政張〔銳〕、劉〔聰〕，副使劉〔福〕、陳〔璧〕、廖〔中〕、王〔紳〕、郝〔志義〕，左右叅議杜〔整〕、周〔紘〕，僉事陳〔寬〕、鈕〔清〕、陳〔嘉謨〕、胡〔富〕則
translation_en:
…is also what the state expects of us. I, Ren, am deficient in discerning men through their words, yet you gentlemen have graciously gathered at my gate like fine timber fit for great service. I venture to invoke the rain to convey my wishes and admonitions, and thus presumptuously write this preface upon the completion of this modest record.

Those who served in this undertaking were as follows. I, Ren, and Zhang Ze, Instructor, served as Examiners. Zhang Han, Zhu Wenkui, Wang Han, and Shao Qing, all Instructors, and Lu Shen, Li Shiyuan, and Yang Chi, all Assistant Instructors, served as Associate Examiners.

Wu Tian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zhao Heling, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Lin Yuanfu, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; and Feng Gao, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, managed arrangements and supervised the examination within the compound.

Liu Chun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zhang Rui and Liu Cong, Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Liu Fu, Chen Bi, Liao Zhong, Wang Shen, and Hao Zhiyi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Du Zheng and Zhou Hong, Left and Right Administration Assistant Commissioners; and Chen Kuan, Niu Qing, Chen Jiamo, and Hu Fu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, for their part…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
防衛贊成於外至於印卷受
卷而下亦各擇人以供事與
試之士簡拔於提學副使楊
文卿者千三百人来自遼陽
者百八十人遵
制額取七十五人刻文之醇者
二十餘篇皆玉散珠聯如瑞
===
雨焉
直隸蘇州府吳縣儒學教諭
李仁謹序
punctuated:
防衛贊成於外。至於印卷、受卷而下，亦各擇人以供事。與試之士，簡拔於提學副使楊文卿者千三百人，来自遼陽者百八十人。遵制額取七十五人，刻文之醇者二十餘篇，皆玉散珠聯，如瑞雨焉。
直隸蘇州府吳縣儒學教諭李仁謹序。
translation_en:
…provided security and assistance outside. For printing and receiving examination papers and the subordinate duties, suitable persons were likewise selected for each task. Of the candidates sitting the examination, 1,300 had been selected by Yang Wenqing, Vice Commissioner for the Surveillance Commission in charge of education, and 180 came from Liaoyang. In accordance with the quota established by imperial decree, seventy-five were selected. More than twenty essays of refined quality were printed; all were like scattered jade and strung pearls, like an auspicious rain.
Preface respectfully written by Li Ren, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered territory.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
天下有道則庶人不議
庸德之行庸言之謹有所不足不敢不勉
有餘不敢盡
多助之至天下順之
易
上下交而其志同也
九五井冽寒泉食象曰寒泉之食中正也
===
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也
有大者不可以盈故受之以謙
書
惟動丕應徯志
惟曁乃僚罔不同心以匡乃辟
王厥有成命治民今休王先服殷御事比
介于我有周御事節性惟日其邁王
敬作所不可不敬德我不可不監于
有夏亦不可不監于有殷
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
天下有道，則庶人不議。
庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉；有餘，不敢盡。
多助之至，天下順之。

易
上下交而其志同也。
九五：井冽，寒泉食。象曰：「寒泉之食，中正也。」
夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。
有大者不可以盈，故受之以謙。

書
惟動丕應徯志。
惟曁乃僚，罔不同心，以匡乃辟。
王厥有成命治民，今休。王先服殷御事，比介于我有周御事。節性，惟日其邁。王敬作所，不可不敬德。我不可不監于有夏，亦不可不監于有殷。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
When the Way prevails throughout the realm, the common people do not debate affairs of government.
In practising ordinary virtues and exercising care in ordinary speech, wherever one falls short, one dares not fail to exert oneself; wherever one has a surplus, one dares not exhaust it.
When support reaches its fullest extent, all under Heaven submit to him.

Book of Changes
Those above and those below communicate, and their purposes are the same.
Nine in the fifth place: The well is clear and cold; its cool spring water is fit to drink. The Image Commentary says: “The drinking of the cool spring water signifies centrality and correctness.”
The Changes is the means by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the subtle beginnings of things.
Those who possess greatness must not become full of themselves; therefore, Great Possession is followed by Modesty.

Book of Documents
Whenever you act, respond fully to what the people await and desire.
Together with your colleagues, be of one mind in supporting and correcting your sovereign.
The king has an established mandate to govern the people; now there is blessing. Let the king first employ the officials of Yin, associating them with and having them assist the officials of our Zhou. Restrain their dispositions, so that they advance daily. Let the king reverently establish his dwelling; he must not fail to hold virtue in reverence. We must take warning from Xia, and we must also take warning from Yin.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭同
盟于戲〔襄公九年〕
西狩獲麟〔哀公十四年〕
禮記
凡居民材必因天地寒煖燥濕廣谷大川
異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕重遲
速異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異
宜脩其教不易其俗齊其政不易其
宜
故國有禮官有御事有職禮有序
脩身及家平均天下
父子有親而後君臣有正
===
第貳場
論
君子之學以潤身為本
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢令諸儒講五經同異詔〔甘露三年〕
擬唐以裴度為中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元〕
punctuated:
薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕。
西狩獲麟〔哀公十四年〕。
禮記
凡居民材，必因天地寒煖燥濕、廣谷大川異制。民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。
故國有禮，官有御，事有職，禮有序。
脩身及家，平均天下。
父子有親，而後君臣有正。
第貳場
論
君子之學，以潤身為本。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢令諸儒講五經同異詔〔甘露三年〕。
擬唐以裴度為中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元〕
translation_en:
…the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi 齊, attacked Zheng and together concluded a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕
During a hunt in the west, a qilin was captured. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Ai〕
Record of Rites
Whenever settling people and assessing their aptitudes, one must take account of differences in the configurations of heaven and earth: cold and warmth, dryness and moisture, broad valleys and great rivers. People born among these have different customs. Their dispositions differ in firmness and gentleness, gravity and levity, slowness and quickness; their blends of the five flavors differ; their implements differ in construction; and different clothing suits them. Improve their instruction without changing their customs; bring their government into order without changing what suits them.
Thus, the state has its rites, offices have their direction, affairs have their assigned duties, and rites have their proper sequence.
Cultivate oneself, extend this to the family, and bring peace and equitable order to all under heaven.
Only after there is affection between father and son can there be proper relations between ruler and minister.
Second Session
Discourse
The learning of the gentleman takes the cultivation of his person as its foundation.
Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question within these categories [?]〕
Compose, in the manner of the Han dynasty, an imperial edict ordering the Confucian scholars to discuss the agreements and differences among the Five Classics. 〔Third year of Ganlu〕
Compose, in the manner of the Tang dynasty, a proclamation appointing Pei Du Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs. 〔Yuan…〕

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
和十年
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表〔淳熙十一年〕
判語〔五條〕
濫設官吏
制書有違
隱蔽差役
服舍違式
飛報軍情
===
第叁場
策五道
問天之生民必有出類之才起而君師之
君以治之師以教之不越乎五倫之
敦而已稽之於經蓋可見也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏條成大誥三編
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒首製孝順事實為善陰
隲二書
宣宗章皇帝繼志述事纘述五倫書頒之天下
無非所以敦五倫也
punctuated:
和十年。
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表〔淳熙十一年〕。
判語〔五條〕：濫設官吏；制書有違；隱蔽差役；服舍違式；飛報軍情。
第叁場。
策五道。
問：天之生民，必有出類之才，起而君師之。君以治之，師以教之，不越乎五倫之敦而已。稽之於經，蓋可見也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，條成《大誥》三編；太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，首製《孝順事實》《為善陰隲》二書；宣宗章皇帝繼志述事，纘述《五倫書》，頒之天下，無非所以敦五倫也。
translation_en:
…the tenth year of Yuanhe [815].
Compose a memorial of thanks, as if in the Song dynasty, for the appointment of Zhou Bida as Military Affairs Commissioner. 〔Eleventh year of Chunxi [1184]〕
Legal judgments 〔five items〕: Unauthorized establishment of official posts and appointment of personnel; violations of imperial decrees; concealment to evade service obligations; clothing and dwellings contrary to prescribed standards; urgent reporting of military intelligence.
Third Session.
Five policy questions.
Question: When Heaven brings forth the people, there must be men of outstanding ability who arise to serve as their rulers and teachers. As rulers they govern them; as teachers they instruct them. This amounts to nothing more than strengthening the Five Human Relationships. Examination of the classics makes this clear. We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm and compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three parts; Emperor Taizong Wen succeeded to the great imperial enterprise and, at its outset, produced the two books Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan Yinzhi); and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang carried forward their intentions and undertakings, compiling the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun Shu) and distributing it throughout the realm. All these were means of strengthening the Five Human Relationships.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
英宗睿皇帝又有大明一統誌之頒其紀名宦
人物烈女亦皆五倫攸繫但
大誥所載多垂戒後世之事其敦五倫之條
何見
爲善陰隲所載多垂訓後世之實其敦五倫
之事何在
孝順事實專言孝也其中亦有兼於餘倫者
乎
五倫書備載嘉言善行也其中何獨詳於君
臣之倫乎
===
大明一統誌所載名宦人物烈女克盡五倫之
道者不可指數其在山東最彰著者
幾人諸士子佩服
聖訓有年矣願悉陳之
問孝經小學之書皆紀載先王之所以脩
身齊家治國平天下之本孝經成於
曾子門人之手而朱子爲之刋誤小
學雜出於曲禮少儀內則弟子職諸
punctuated:
英宗睿皇帝又有《大明一統誌》之頒，其紀名宦、人物、烈女，亦皆五倫攸繫。但《大誥》所載，多垂戒後世之事，其敦五倫之條何見？《爲善陰隲》所載，多垂訓後世之實，其敦五倫之事何在？《孝順事實》專言孝也，其中亦有兼於餘倫者乎？《五倫書》備載嘉言善行也，其中何獨詳於君臣之倫乎？《大明一統誌》所載名宦、人物、烈女，克盡五倫之道者不可指數，其在山東最彰著者幾人？諸士子佩服聖訓有年矣，願悉陳之。

問：《孝經》《小學》之書，皆紀載先王之所以脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本。《孝經》成於曾子門人之手，而朱子爲之刋誤；《小學》雜出於《曲禮》《少儀》《內則》《弟子職》諸
translation_en:
…Emperor Yingzong Rui also promulgated the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi). Its accounts of notable officials, eminent persons, and exemplary women likewise all concern the Five Relationships. Yet the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao) chiefly records matters intended as warnings to later generations: where are its provisions for strengthening the Five Relationships to be found? Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Wei shan yinzhi) chiefly records deeds intended as instruction for later generations: where does it present actions that strengthen the Five Relationships? Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) treats filial piety specifically: does it also contain material concerning the other relationships? The Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu) comprehensively records admirable sayings and virtuous conduct: why does it give particularly detailed treatment to the relationship between ruler and minister? Among the notable officials, eminent persons, and exemplary women recorded in the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming, those who fully fulfilled the Way of the Five Relationships are too numerous to count. Which individuals in Shandong were the most illustrious? You candidates have reverently upheld the imperial instructions for many years. We ask you to set all this forth in detail.

Question: The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) and Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) both record the foundations by which the former kings cultivated themselves, regulated their families, governed their states, and brought peace to all under Heaven. The Classic of Filial Piety was compiled by the disciples of Zengzi, and Master Zhu corrected its errors. Elementary Learning draws variously upon such chapters as “Summary of the Rules of Propriety” (Quli), “Minor Rules of Deportment” (Shaoyi), “Domestic Regulations” (Neize), and “Duties of Disciples” (Dizi zhi)…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
篇而朱子為之蒐輯故今皆授之童
蒙資其講習誠大切要之書也諸士
子誦習有年試相與講明之孝經六
章之書果皆舊文而無離析增加之
失歟七章以後又皆何人所作而無
戾於孔曾傳受之意歟孔壁所藏者
何本河間王所得者何書閨門一章
不知何人所去其所去者是歟非歟
小學有內篇有外篇內篇所紀者何
===
道外篇所紀者何事抑二篇何以有
內外之別乎或者謂立教明倫敬身
為小學之綱領而稽古非綱領何以
入於內篇歟嘉言善行何以為小學
外篇而內篇何莫非嘉言善行歟願
為我言之
問古之聖賢世系之遠惟孔氏為最雖堯
舜之盛不能過也遡其先世為宋人
中葉遷魯遂為魯人歷十四世而生
punctuated:
篇，而朱子為之蒐輯，故今皆授之童蒙，資其講習，誠大切要之書也。諸士子誦習有年，試相與講明之。《孝經》六章之書，果皆舊文而無離析增加之失歟？七章以後，又皆何人所作，而無戾於孔曾傳受之意歟？孔壁所藏者何本？河間王所得者何書？閨門一章，不知何人所去，其所去者是歟非歟？《小學》有內篇，有外篇，內篇所紀者何道？外篇所紀者何事？抑二篇何以有內外之別乎？或者謂立教、明倫、敬身為《小學》之綱領，而稽古非綱領，何以入於內篇歟？嘉言、善行何以為《小學》外篇，而內篇何莫非嘉言善行歟？願為我言之。
問：古之聖賢，世系之遠，惟孔氏為最，雖堯舜之盛，不能過也。遡其先世，為宋人，中葉遷魯，遂為魯人，歷十四世而生
translation_en:
…chapters, which Master Zhu compiled and collected. Thus both books are now taught to young beginners to support their study and practice; they are indeed works of the greatest importance. You candidates have recited and studied them for years. Now let us elucidate them together. Are the six chapters of the Classic of Filial Piety all truly ancient text, free from errors of division or addition? Who composed the seventh and subsequent chapters, and do they remain faithful to the meaning transmitted between Confucius and Zengzi? Which version was concealed in the wall of Confucius’s residence? What text did the Prince of Hejian obtain? It is not known who removed the chapter “Within the Inner Quarters”; was its removal right or wrong? Elementary Learning has Inner and Outer Sections. What principles do the Inner Sections record, and what affairs do the Outer Sections record? Why, moreover, are the two distinguished as inner and outer? Some say that “Establishing Instruction,” “Clarifying Human Relationships,” and “Maintaining Reverence for One’s Person” form the organizing framework of Elementary Learning. Since “Examining Antiquity” is not part of this framework, why is it included in the Inner Sections? Why do “Worthy Sayings” and “Good Deeds” constitute the Outer Sections of Elementary Learning, when everything in the Inner Sections is likewise a worthy saying or a good deed? Please explain these matters to me.
Question: Among the sages and worthies of antiquity, none has a lineage extending so far as that of the Kong family. Even the illustrious lineages of Yao and Shun cannot surpass it. Tracing their ancestry, we find that they were people of Song; in an intermediate generation they moved to Lu and thus became people of Lu. After fourteen generations was born…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
孔子源亦遠矣可追論歟然源遠則
流長浚其流也自伋以後無代無人
無人弗耀戰國時有為齊相者有為
魏相者有為秦博士者其人何名炎
漢時有遷大將軍者有拜太師者有
襲封關內侯者其人何𠎀歷晉宋梁
隋間或為奉聖亭侯後改封崇聖侯
曰奉曰崇累有輕重乎或為恭聖侯
後改封紹聖侯曰恭曰紹亦有差等
===
乎及唐宋時或對策高第或狀元及
第或明經及第一時文運蓋莫盛也
可得聞歟或以剛毅直諒名或以操
行介潔稱或以介潔不阿許一時節
義蓋莫尚也可歷指歟世之論常者
必曰豐於前者嗇於後如孔子之亶
生不為不豐而其後又自不嗇果堯
舜獨憮於孔子乎抑別有其說乎諸
生挺生東魯幸與孔氏同邦其世系
punctuated: 孔子，源亦遠矣，可追論歟？然源遠則流長，浚其流也，自伋以後，無代無人，無人弗耀。戰國時，有為齊相者，有為魏相者，有為秦博士者，其人何名？炎漢時，有遷大將軍者，有拜太師者，有襲封關內侯者，其人何𠎀？歷晉宋梁隋間，或為奉聖亭侯，後改封崇聖侯，曰奉曰崇，累有輕重乎？或為恭聖侯，後改封紹聖侯，曰恭曰紹，亦有差等乎？及唐宋時，或對策高第，或狀元及第，或明經及第，一時文運蓋莫盛也，可得聞歟？或以剛毅直諒名，或以操行介潔稱，或以介潔不阿許，一時節義蓋莫尚也，可歷指歟？世之論常者必曰：「豐於前者，嗇於後。」如孔子之亶生，不為不豐，而其後又自不嗇，果堯舜獨憮於孔子乎？抑別有其說乎？諸生挺生東魯，幸與孔氏同邦，其世系
translation_en:
…Confucius was born: the lineage’s origins were indeed remote. Can you trace and discuss them? Yet a distant source makes for a long stream. As that stream deepened, from Ji onward no generation lacked outstanding men, and none failed to shine. During the Warring States period, some served as chief minister of Qi, some as chief minister of Wei, and some as erudite in Qin. What were their names? During the Han dynasty, associated with fire, some were promoted to General-in-chief, some appointed Grand Preceptor, and some inherited the title of Marquis Within the Passes. Who were these men [?]? Through the Jin, Song, Liang, and Sui dynasties, some held the title Marquis of Fengsheng Precinct, subsequently changed to Marquis Chongsheng. Did these successive designations, “Serving the Sage” and “Exalting the Sage,” differ in weight? Others held the title Marquis Gongsheng, subsequently changed to Marquis Shaosheng. Did “Revering the Sage” and “Continuing the Sage” likewise differ in rank?

By the Tang and Song periods, some attained high standing through their responses to policy questions, some passed as the top candidate, and some passed the examination in elucidating the classics. Surely literary fortunes could scarcely have flourished more greatly in their day. May I hear about them? Some were renowned for firmness, resolution, uprightness, and trustworthiness; some were praised for principled and pure conduct; and some were commended for incorruptibility and refusal to bend to others. Surely integrity and righteousness could scarcely have stood higher in their day. Can you identify these men one by one?

Those who discuss the regular patterns of the world invariably say, “Abundance in earlier generations is followed by scarcity in later ones.” The birth of Confucius [?] can hardly be called anything less than abundant, yet his descendants likewise suffered no scarcity. Were Yao and Shun indeed left disconsolate before Confucius [?]? Or is there another explanation? You students have arisen as outstanding men in eastern Lu and are fortunate to share the homeland of the Kong lineage. Its genealogy…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
人物知之素矣毋吝告我
問人莫難於知人亦莫難於自知知人則
哲堯所難也何敢望回孔子與馮後
世無帝堯之智子貢之識而立論以
方人舉人以自況誇誕者不免失於
自高溺愛者不免失於過許豈能無
罅隙之可議哉敢以史冊所紀者與
諸士商之三顧馳驅者嘗以管樂自
居三朝勤勞者嘗以伊周自許恢復
===
之君或擬之於韓彭罪謫之守或擬
之於頗牧忘身殉國者目為魏徵似
矣碩德重望者果似乎馮道平齊定
蓟者目為韓信肖矣捫虱高談者果
肖乎孔明或賛金世宗為堯舜或方
晉武帝為桓靈其論孰優或自況於
文宣或自愧於赧獻其見孰當澄之
不清淆之不濁視顏子為孰賢舉賢
用能厲兵訓卒視子房為孰勝考䆮
punctuated:
人物，知之素矣，毋吝告我。
問：人莫難於知人，亦莫難於自知。「知人則哲，堯所難也。」「何敢望回？」孔子與馮。後世無帝堯之智、子貢之識，而立論以方人，舉人以自況，誇誕者不免失於自高，溺愛者不免失於過許，豈能無罅隙之可議哉？敢以史冊所紀者與諸士商之。三顧馳驅者，嘗以管樂自居；三朝勤勞者，嘗以伊周自許。恢復之君，或擬之於韓彭；罪謫之守，或擬之於頗牧。忘身殉國者，目為魏徵，似矣；碩德重望者，果似乎馮道？平齊定蓟者，目為韓信，肖矣；捫虱高談者，果肖乎孔明？或賛金世宗為堯舜，或方晉武帝為桓靈，其論孰優？或自況於文宣，或自愧於赧獻，其見孰當？澄之不清，淆之不濁，視顏子為孰賢？舉賢用能，厲兵訓卒，視子房為孰勝？考䆮
translation_en:
…and its notable figures, you have long known them well. Do not hesitate to tell me.
Question: Nothing is harder than knowing others, and nothing is harder than knowing oneself. “To know others is wisdom; even Yao found this difficult.” “How would I dare hope to equal Hui?” Confucius approved [?]. People of later ages lack Emperor Yao’s wisdom and Zigong’s discernment, yet pronounce judgments comparing others and invoke other people as their own equals. The boastful inevitably err by exalting themselves; those blinded by affection inevitably err by praising too highly. How could their judgments have no flaws open to criticism? I venture to discuss with you gentlemen some cases recorded in the histories.
The man who exerted himself in service after receiving three visits once considered himself the equal of Guan Zhong and Yue Yi; the man who labored diligently through three reigns once claimed to match Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. A ruler who restored his realm was compared by some to Han Xin and Peng Yue; a prefect banished for an offense was compared by some to Lian Po and Li Mu. The man who disregarded his own life and died for his country was called another Wei Zheng: the resemblance seems apt. But did the man of great virtue and commanding reputation really resemble Feng Dao? The man who subdued Qi and pacified Ji was called another Han Xin: the likeness seems apt. But did the man who picked lice while discoursing loftily really resemble Kongming?
Some praised Emperor Shizong of Jin as another Yao or Shun; others compared Emperor Wu of Jin to Emperors Huan and Ling. Which judgment is better? Some compared themselves to Emperor Wenxuan; others felt ashamed of themselves beside King Nan and Emperor Xian. Whose assessment was sound? The man who could not be made clear by settling or turbid by stirring—how did his worth compare with Master Yan’s? The man who promoted the worthy, employed the capable, readied weapons, and trained troops—how did his abilities compare with Zifang’s? Examine [?]…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
以論賢其材智之短長莫逃原心以
量德其人品之高下易見若徒因仍
於古人之言槩稜於臧否之際曾次
略無定見何足以尚論古人
問國用取給於東南財賦必資於漕運此
古今之通論也然唐虞之時江浙無
聞禹貢之書漕運不錄何歟三代而
下城穿邗溝湖通射陽其民固未甚
病也而又有負海之粟三十鍾而致
===
一石何歟關東之漕僅數十萬石尋
而益至百餘萬石其漕亦未甚費也
其後既益為四百萬石又益為六百
萬石何歟脫巾置酒倚辦之急者何
人泝河入渭講畫之詳者何代閉口
之制何如孰變為擣氷轉般之法何
似孰變為直達開會通河以代海運
便矣何時而後淤疏通惠河以免陸
運當矣何為而隨廢至我
punctuated:
以論賢，其材智之短長莫逃；原心以量德，其人品之高下易見。若徒因仍於古人之言，槩稜於臧否之際，曾次略無定見，何足以尚論古人？
問：國用取給於東南，財賦必資於漕運，此古今之通論也。然唐虞之時，江浙無聞；禹貢之書，漕運不錄，何歟？三代而下，城穿邗溝，湖通射陽，其民固未甚病也，而又有負海之粟三十鍾而致一石，何歟？關東之漕僅數十萬石，尋而益至百餘萬石，其漕亦未甚費也。其後既益為四百萬石，又益為六百萬石，何歟？脫巾置酒，倚辦之急者何人？泝河入渭，講畫之詳者何代？閉口之制何如？孰變為擣氷？轉般之法何似？孰變為直達？開會通河以代海運，便矣，何時而後淤？疏通惠河以免陸運，當矣，何為而隨廢？至我
translation_en:
…to assess worthiness, the strengths and weaknesses of their abilities and intelligence cannot escape scrutiny; by examining their underlying intentions to measure their virtue, the relative standing of their character is readily apparent. If one merely follows the judgments of the ancients, equivocates between praise and blame [?], and has scarcely any settled judgment [?], how can one adequately appraise the men of antiquity?
Question: That state expenditure draws its supplies from the southeast, and that fiscal revenues necessarily depend on grain transport by water, is a view generally accepted both past and present. Yet in the time of Tang and Yu, nothing was heard of Jiang and Zhe, and the Tribute of Yu does not record grain transport. Why was this? After the Three Dynasties, a city was built and the Hangou Canal excavated [?], and the lakes were connected with Sheyang. The people certainly did not yet suffer severely from this. Yet there was also the case in which thirty zhong of grain from the coastal region yielded only one shi delivered. Why was this?
Grain transported from east of the passes amounted to only several hundred thousand shi, and soon increased to over a million shi; the transport was still not excessively costly. Later, the amount increased to four million shi, and then again to six million shi. Why was this? Who was it who removed his headcloth and set out wine, so urgently relying on the task being accomplished? In which dynasty were plans discussed in detail for proceeding upstream along the Yellow River and entering the Wei River? What was the system of closing the canal mouths? Who changed it to breaking the ice? What was the method of transport by successive transfers? Who changed it to direct delivery? Opening the Huitong Canal to replace sea transport was convenient: when did it subsequently silt up? Dredging the Tonghui Canal to avoid overland transport was appropriate: why was it then abandoned? Coming to our…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝
太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵東南財賦如探囊物
太宗文皇帝駐蹕燕京初猶海運何時而罷然
自古運河之水不通黃河近年黃陵
岡一決而安平鎮口遂開運舟經口
或有不虞黃河入運亦得其力或謂
黃陵岡不塞則安平鎮口不得收功
今兩口既塞功甚偉矣但天雨或不
時未免淺阻之患不可憂耶或謂不
必強塞安平鎮而但旋脩海運計亦
似矣但舟師非素習未免風波之險
又何策耶諸生長育齊魯博考圖籍
漕河之法目見而心融者幸明言之
以觀用世之學
punctuated: 朝太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵，東南財賦如探囊物。太宗文皇帝駐蹕燕京，初猶海運，何時而罷？然自古運河之水不通黃河，近年黃陵岡一決，而安平鎮口遂開。運舟經口，或有不虞；黃河入運，亦得其力。或謂黃陵岡不塞，則安平鎮口不得收功。今兩口既塞，功甚偉矣，但天雨或不時，未免淺阻之患，不可憂耶？或謂不必強塞安平鎮，而但旋脩海運，計亦似矣，但舟師非素習，未免風波之險，又何策耶？諸生長育齊魯，博考圖籍，漕河之法，目見而心融者，幸明言之，以觀用世之學。
translation_en: …our dynasty, Emperor Gao, Taizu, established his capital at Jinling, and the tax revenues of the southeast were as readily accessible as objects taken from a bag. Emperor Wen, Taizong, took up residence at Yanjing. At first, grain was still transported by sea; when was this discontinued? From ancient times, however, the waters of the Grand Canal had not connected with the Yellow River. In recent years, once the embankment at Huanglinggang breached, an opening consequently formed at Anpingzhen. Grain-transport boats passing through this opening sometimes encountered unforeseen dangers; yet the Yellow River’s entry into the canal also provided useful assistance. Some said that unless the breach at Huanglinggang was closed, work at the Anpingzhen opening could not achieve its intended result. Now both openings have been closed—a very great accomplishment. But if rain does not fall at the proper times, there will inevitably be difficulties from shallow water obstructing passage. Is this not cause for concern? Some say that there is no need to insist on closing the opening at Anpingzhen, and that sea transport should simply be promptly restored. This plan, too, seems plausible. But since the crews lack long-standing practice, the dangers of wind and waves would be unavoidable. What further strategy is there? You students have grown up in the lands of Qi and Lu and have consulted maps and texts widely. Please clearly explain what you have witnessed and thoroughly understood concerning the methods of canal grain transport, so that we may assess your learning for service in the world.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
天下有道則庶人不議
刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔寫出有道氣象宛然在目〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔題本冠冕作者多襲陳言今〕
〔人厭觀求其化腐為新使人心目者僅見此篇允宜前寘〕
考試官教諭張　批〔析理明白〕
考試官教諭李　批〔平順得旨〕
===
世際隆平之日共無非間之言蓋民心之是非
顧上之政治何如耳天下有道則上無失政矣
民何間然之有哉昔聖人通論天下之勢及此
蓋謂人君臨馭天下統理民物紀綱整肅四方
仰一統於無虞海宇昇平萬國戴一人之有慶
君出治而臣輔治自朝廷而方岳有穆穆明明
之休君出命而臣奉命自王國而萬邦有皇皇
師師之風禮樂大政掌握於一人之手而政無
多門也征伐大權綱維於朝廷之上而權無下
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

天下有道，則庶人不議。

刁嵎

同考試官訓導楊　批〔寫出有道氣象，宛然在目。〕

同考試官教諭朱　批〔題本冠冕，作者多襲陳言，今人厭觀。求其化腐為新，使人心目者，僅見此篇，允宜前寘。〕

考試官教諭張　批〔析理明白。〕

考試官教諭李　批〔平順得旨。〕

世際隆平之日，共無非間之言。蓋民心之是非，顧上之政治何如耳。天下有道，則上無失政矣，民何間然之有哉？昔聖人通論天下之勢及此，蓋謂人君臨馭天下，統理民物，紀綱整肅，四方仰一統於無虞；海宇昇平，萬國戴一人之有慶。君出治而臣輔治，自朝廷而方岳，有穆穆明明之休；君出命而臣奉命，自王國而萬邦，有皇皇師師之風。禮樂大政，掌握於一人之手，而政無多門也；征伐大權，綱維於朝廷之上，而權無下
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When the Way prevails throughout All-under-Heaven, the common people do not debate affairs of government.”

Diao Yu 刁嵎

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: “He depicts the atmosphere of an age when the Way prevails so vividly that it seems before our eyes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The topic is inherently grand, but writers mostly repeat stale expressions that readers today tire of seeing. In seeking an essay that transforms the stale into something fresh and [refreshes?] the reader’s mind and eyes, I have found only this one. It certainly deserves a high placing.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The analysis of principle is clear.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Smooth and coherent, it captures the intended meaning.”

When the world enjoys an age of flourishing peace, all refrain from words of criticism. For the people’s judgments of right and wrong depend simply upon the character of the government above them. When the Way prevails throughout All-under-Heaven, those above commit no errors in government. What grounds, then, could the people have for criticism? Long ago, the Sage touched upon this in his comprehensive discussion of the condition of All-under-Heaven. His meaning was that the ruler presides over All-under-Heaven and governs its people and affairs as a whole. The guiding principles and regulations are orderly and strict, and the four quarters look up to a unified rule free from anxiety. Peace flourishes within the seas, and the myriad states uphold the blessings enjoyed by the One Man.

The ruler initiates government and his ministers assist him in governing; from the court to the regional authorities, there is the excellence of solemn dignity and luminous discernment. The ruler issues commands and his ministers carry them out; from the royal domain to the myriad states, there is a spirit of august majesty and mutual emulation. The great affairs of rites and music are held in the hands of the One Man, so government does not issue from multiple sources. The great authority to undertake punitive expeditions is maintained at the imperial court, so that power does not pass downward …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
移也天下有道如此但見生斯世也爲斯民也
莫不慶王綱之丕振翕然同文同軌之天喜王
化之大同蕩然遵道遵路之俗號令一布帖耳
聽命之恐後閭閻里巷無異心也何嘗有所私
議以非其上哉所以然者非箝其口也盖上無
失政自不容於議耳政教一施心悅誠服之不
暇市井草莽無異志也何嘗有所私議以毀其
上哉所以爾者非捫其舌也盖上無失政自無
事於議耳吁下無私議而由乎上無失政如此
===
爲人君者可不強於自治以一斯民之心哉大
抵此章夫子雖通論天下之勢實所以爲當時
發也盖是時三家強公室弱君臣失道綱常淪
沒禮樂名分蕩然無復存矣故夫子歷論有道
而及無道之得失以見爲君者不可無自治之
計爲臣者不可萌僭竊之心其扶世立教挽今
返古之意藹然溢於言表矣
庸德之行庸言之謹有所不足不敢不勉
有餘不敢盡
punctuated:
移也。天下有道如此，但見生斯世也，爲斯民也，莫不慶王綱之丕振，翕然同文同軌之天；喜王化之大同，蕩然遵道遵路之俗。號令一布，帖耳聽命之恐後，閭閻里巷無異心也，何嘗有所私議以非其上哉？所以然者，非箝其口也，盖上無失政，自不容於議耳。政教一施，心悅誠服之不暇，市井草莽無異志也，何嘗有所私議以毀其上哉？所以爾者，非捫其舌也，盖上無失政，自無事於議耳。吁！下無私議，而由乎上無失政如此，爲人君者可不強於自治，以一斯民之心哉？大抵此章，夫子雖通論天下之勢，實所以爲當時發也。盖是時三家強，公室弱，君臣失道，綱常淪沒，禮樂名分蕩然無復存矣。故夫子歷論有道而及無道之得失，以見爲君者不可無自治之計，爲臣者不可萌僭竊之心。其扶世立教、挽今返古之意，藹然溢於言表矣。

庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉；有餘，不敢盡。
translation_en:
…shifted downward. Such is the condition of the realm when the Way prevails. All who are born into this age and belong to its people celebrate the great flourishing of royal order, united in a world sharing the same script and the same carriage tracks. They rejoice in the universal reach of royal moral influence, with customs everywhere conforming to the proper way and path. Once commands are issued, they listen submissively, fearing only that they may be late to obey; throughout the villages and lanes, no one harbors a contrary heart. When would they ever engage in private criticism to condemn those above them? This is not because their mouths have been sealed: it is because those above commit no errors in government, leaving no room for criticism. Once government and moral instruction are put into effect, the people wholeheartedly submit, eagerly and sincerely; in marketplaces and the countryside, none harbors a contrary purpose. When would they ever engage in private criticism to disparage those above them? This is not because their tongues have been restrained: it is because those above commit no errors in government, leaving nothing to criticize. Ah! If the absence of private criticism below thus derives from the absence of misgovernment above, can a ruler fail to exert himself in putting his own governance in order, so as to unite the hearts of the people? Broadly speaking, although in this chapter the Master discusses the condition of the realm in general, his words were really prompted by the circumstances of his own time. At that time the three great houses were powerful and the ducal house was weak. Ruler and ministers had lost the Way; the cardinal relationships and constant moral norms had fallen into oblivion; rites, music, and the distinctions of title and station had utterly disappeared. Thus the Master discussed in turn the gains and losses associated with the presence and absence of the Way, showing that rulers must have a plan for putting their own governance in order, and that ministers must not entertain thoughts of usurpation. His intention to sustain the age and establish moral instruction, to turn the present back toward antiquity, abundantly shines through his words.

In practicing ordinary virtues and being careful in ordinary speech, where one falls short, one dares not fail to strive; where one has more than enough, one dares not give it full expression.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
王崇獻
同考試官訓導李　批〔拈書出題此其平易而佳〕
作獨步是篇詞潔理明宜在所取
同考試官教諭王　批〔認理精措詞當可取〕
考試官教諭張　批〔措詞雅健他作所不及〕
考試官教諭李　批〔詞不贅而意自足佳作也〕
君子自脩於言行之常而益容其功焉夫道不
遠人自脩之功所當盡也君子致勉乎此而言
行不已其功焉共不遠人以為道也豈不於斯
===
而可見乎昔中庸是章論道不遠人至此而言
君子自責自脩之事蓋謂道本不遠於人人自
有以遠乎道君子於此宜何如哉亦惟不遠人
以為道耳彼其孝弟忠信之道乃日用常行之
理吾之所當然也行之不力則道於我乎遼邈
矣蓋必以是道之責於人者于以自脩於庸德
之間躬行之允迪之而孝弟忠信必求踐乎其
實不苟焉以虛行也言之不謹則道於我乎扞
格矣蓋必以是道之責於彼者于以自脩於庸
punctuated:
王崇獻

同考試官訓導李批〔拈書出題，此其平易而佳〕作獨步，是篇詞潔理明，宜在所取。
同考試官教諭王批〔認理精，措詞當，可取〕
考試官教諭張批〔措詞雅健，他作所不及〕
考試官教諭李批〔詞不贅而意自足，佳作也〕

君子自脩於言行之常，而益容其功焉。夫道不遠人，自脩之功所當盡也。君子致勉乎此，而言行不已其功焉，共不遠人以為道也，豈不於斯而可見乎？昔《中庸》是章論道不遠人，至此而言君子自責自脩之事。蓋謂道本不遠於人，人自有以遠乎道。君子於此宜何如哉？亦惟不遠人以為道耳。彼其孝弟忠信之道，乃日用常行之理，吾之所當然也。行之不力，則道於我乎遼邈矣。蓋必以是道之責於人者，于以自脩於庸德之間，躬行之，允迪之，而孝弟忠信必求踐乎其實，不苟焉以虛行也。言之不謹，則道於我乎扞格矣。蓋必以是道之責於彼者，于以自脩於庸
translation_en:
Wang Chongxian

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“The topic is drawn from the book; it is straightforward and fine.”〕 The composition stands unrivaled. Its language is concise and its reasoning clear; it deserves selection.
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔“His grasp of principle is precise and his phrasing appropriate. Worth selecting.”〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The phrasing is elegant and vigorous, beyond what other compositions achieve.”〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“The language is economical, yet the meaning is complete. A fine composition.”〕

The gentleman cultivates himself in ordinary speech and conduct, further developing his efforts therein [?]. The Way is not far from human beings, and one ought to exert oneself fully in self-cultivation. The gentleman strives at this and never ceases his efforts in speech and conduct. Is it not evident here that he practices the Way without departing from what is human [?]?

In this chapter, the Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the Way is not far from human beings; at this point it addresses the gentleman’s holding himself accountable and cultivating himself. Its meaning is that the Way is fundamentally not far from people, but people themselves do things that distance them from it. What, then, should the gentleman do? Simply practice the Way without departing from what is human.

The way of filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and trustworthiness consists of principles for ordinary daily conduct: these are what I ought to fulfill. If I fail to practice them diligently, the Way becomes remote from me. I must therefore take what I demand of others according to this Way and apply it to cultivating myself in ordinary virtues. I must practice it personally and follow it faithfully, seeking to realize filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and trustworthiness in substance, rather than carelessly performing empty acts.

If I am not careful in speech, the Way encounters obstruction in me. I must therefore take what I demand of others according to this Way and apply it to cultivating myself in ordinary …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
言之際無易焉無茍焉而孝弟忠信務求擇乎
其可不泛焉以徒言也夫庸德之行雖云力矣
然力行難常失於不足使不足而不勉焉不幾
於行之不力乎又必於孝弟未能也而勉焉以
能之忠信未盡也而強焉以盡之行之弗篤弗
措也行孝不益力哉庸言之發雖云謹矣然放
言易常至於有餘使有餘而不訒焉不幾於謹
之未至乎又必欲言夫孝弟也恥躬不逮則訒
之而不敢盡言夫忠信也恐未能行則訒之而
不敢發言之弗謹弗措也謹之不益至哉吁德
之行已力而益力言之謹已至而益至君子不
===
遠人以為道如此此道之所以不遠於人也歟
大抵道也者原於天命具於人心見於行事本
近而且易不待勉強而能也但人於道不求諸
近而求諸遠不求之易而求之難則反失其道
矣故夫子於此首言道不遠人而又歷論治人
愛人責己之道無非所以明道不遠人人不可
遠人以為道也子思子引之以明道之費隱其
punctuated:
言之際，無易焉，無茍焉，而孝弟忠信務求擇乎其可，不泛焉以徒言也。夫庸德之行，雖云力矣，然力行難，常失於不足。使不足而不勉焉，不幾於行之不力乎？又必於孝弟未能也，而勉焉以能之；忠信未盡也，而強焉以盡之。行之弗篤弗措也，行孝不益力哉？庸言之發，雖云謹矣，然放言易，常至於有餘。使有餘而不訒焉，不幾於謹之未至乎？又必欲言夫孝弟也，恥躬不逮，則訒之而不敢盡；言夫忠信也，恐未能行，則訒之而不敢發。言之弗謹弗措也，謹之不益至哉？吁！德之行已力而益力，言之謹已至而益至。君子不遠人以為道如此，此道之所以不遠於人也歟！

大抵道也者，原於天命，具於人心，見於行事，本近而且易，不待勉強而能也。但人於道，不求諸近而求諸遠，不求之易而求之難，則反失其道矣。故夫子於此首言道不遠人，而又歷論治人、愛人、責己之道，無非所以明道不遠人，人不可遠人以為道也。子思子引之以明道之費隱，其
translation_en:
…in ordinary speech, being neither careless nor heedless, and, in matters of filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness, taking care to choose what is fitting, rather than speaking loosely with empty words. Although one may be said to exert oneself in practicing ordinary virtues, sustained practice is difficult, and one often falls short. If one falls short yet makes no further effort, does this not amount to insufficient exertion in practice? Thus, where one is not yet capable of filial devotion and fraternal respect, one must strive to become capable; where one has not fully realized loyalty and trustworthiness, one must exert oneself to realize them fully. One must not desist until one’s practice is earnest. Would the practice of filial devotion [?] not thereby become still more vigorous? Although one may be said to be cautious in ordinary speech, unrestrained speech comes easily, and one often says too much. If one says too much yet does not restrain one’s words, does this not amount to insufficient caution? Thus, when wishing to speak of filial devotion and fraternal respect, shame that one’s own conduct falls short must make one hesitant, so that one dares not say everything; when speaking of loyalty and trustworthiness, fear that one cannot put them into practice must make one hesitant, so that one dares not utter the words. One must not desist until one’s speech is cautious. Would that caution not thereby become still more complete? Ah! Already vigorous in practicing virtue, one becomes still more vigorous; already thorough in caution over words, one becomes still more thorough. This is how the gentleman pursues the Way without departing from human concerns. Is this not why the Way is never far from people?

Generally speaking, the Way originates in Heaven’s mandate, is fully present in the human heart, and manifests itself in conduct. It is inherently near at hand and easy, and can be practiced without forced exertion. Yet if people seek the Way in what is distant rather than near, and in what is difficult rather than easy, they instead lose it. Thus the Master here begins by saying that the Way is not far from people, and then discusses in turn the ways of governing others, loving others, and holding oneself accountable. All this serves to make clear that the Way is not far from people, and that people must not depart from human concerns in pursuing it. title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
示人體道之功何其深切而著明哉
多助之至天下順之
杜珽
同考試官教諭邵　批〔此題作者多不知天下順之即多助之至徃徃岐而二之惟此篇一破便見題意且終篇文彩燁然堪〕
式後學
考試官教諭張　批〔語官平實可錄〕
考試官教諭李　批〔說出孟子立言之意〕
===
大賢論人和之極而天下無不歸焉蓋天下之
心未易得也今多助之至而天下歸心如此非
得道之君其何以致之哉吾想孟子因論夫時
地利之不如人和而推言及此謂夫民心向背
而國之治亂係焉政治得失而民之從違關焉
善圖治者亦惟得道以得人心焉耳誠能發號
施令而巨細必得其道由是庶民小子而遠迩
自罔不服殆必丕應徯志翕然起夫助我之念
心悅誠服翕然與夫助我之心助不徒助助而
有以極其多焉多不徒多多而有以極其至焉
punctuated:
示人體道之功，何其深切而著明哉！

多助之至，天下順之。
杜珽
同考試官教諭邵，批〔此題作者多不知天下順之即多助之至，徃徃岐而二之。惟此篇一破便見題意，且終篇文彩燁然，堪〕式後學。
考試官教諭張，批〔語官平實，可錄。〕
考試官教諭李，批〔說出孟子立言之意。〕

大賢論人和之極，而天下無不歸焉。蓋天下之心未易得也，今多助之至，而天下歸心如此，非得道之君，其何以致之哉？吾想孟子因論夫時、地利之不如人和，而推言及此，謂夫民心向背，而國之治亂係焉；政治得失，而民之從違關焉。善圖治者，亦惟得道以得人心焉耳。誠能發號施令，而巨細必得其道，由是庶民小子，而遠迩自罔不服，殆必丕應徯志，翕然起夫助我之念；心悅誠服，翕然與夫助我之心。助不徒助，助而有以極其多焉；多不徒多，多而有以極其至焉。
translation_en:
…How profound, earnest, and clear is his instruction to people in the work of embodying the Way!

“When support reaches its utmost, all under Heaven submit to him.”
By Du Ting.

Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: “Most who write on this topic do not understand that ‘all under Heaven submit to him’ is precisely what ‘support reaches its utmost’ means; they repeatedly separate the two. This essay alone reveals the meaning of the topic in its opening exposition. Moreover, its literary brilliance shines throughout: it deserves to serve as a model for later students.”

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The language [?] is straightforward and substantial; it merits inclusion.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It brings out Mencius’s intention in making this statement.”

The great worthy discusses the utmost degree of harmony among people, at which none under Heaven fail to give their allegiance. The hearts of all under Heaven are not easily won. Now, when support reaches its utmost and all under Heaven give their hearts in this way, how could anyone but a ruler who has attained the Way bring this about? I imagine that Mencius, in discussing how favorable timing and the advantages of terrain fall short of harmony among people, extended his argument to this point. He meant that a state’s order or disorder depends upon whether the people’s hearts turn toward it or away from it, and that the people’s obedience or disobedience is bound up with the successes and failures of governance. Those skilled at seeking good government need only attain the Way in order to win people’s hearts.

If, in issuing commands and promulgating orders, a ruler truly accords with the Way in matters great and small, then among the common people and the young, far and near, none will fail to submit. Surely they will respond wholeheartedly and await the fulfillment of his intentions, unanimously conceiving the thought of supporting him. Delighted in their hearts and sincerely convinced, they will unanimously offer their hearts in his support. Such support is no mere support: it reaches the utmost in its abundance. Such abundance is no mere abundance: it reaches the very highest degree.…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
然多助之至何如彼其盤率土而東焉以西天
下如彼其大也望雲霓而來順者濟濟乎惟恐
吾之或後環天下而南焉以北疆域如彼其廣
也避水火而來歸者祁祁乎惟恐人之或先不
必封疆是界歸之者合天下而一心無離德也
多助之至何如哉不必山谿是險順之者罄率
土而一志無叛心也多助之至何若哉是則得
道多助而天下皆歸如此人和無以加矣戰必
無不勝矣尚何天時地利之足恃哉大抵戰國
之時聖賢道否功利日滋用兵者往往以天時
地利為務而不知得道以為之本徒事乎小而
不務乎大齊其末而不揣其本未足以言善治
者也故孟子於此發為天時地利不如人和之
論至此又以得道為人和之本使當時國君果
能得道以得人心則地利之險人為之守天時
之善人為之乘有所不戰戰必勝矣惜乎終不
能聽徒使孟子託之空言也可慨已夫
===
易
punctuated:
然多助之至何如？彼其盤率土而東焉以西，天下如彼其大也，望雲霓而來順者濟濟乎，惟恐吾之或後；環天下而南焉以北，疆域如彼其廣也，避水火而來歸者祁祁乎，惟恐人之或先。不必封疆是界，歸之者合天下而一心，無離德也，多助之至何如哉？不必山谿是險，順之者罄率土而一志，無叛心也，多助之至何若哉？是則得道多助，而天下皆歸如此，人和無以加矣，戰必無不勝矣，尚何天時地利之足恃哉？大抵戰國之時，聖賢道否，功利日滋，用兵者往往以天時地利為務，而不知得道以為之本，徒事乎小而不務乎大，齊其末而不揣其本，未足以言善治者也。故孟子於此發為天時地利不如人和之論，至此又以得道為人和之本。使當時國君果能得道以得人心，則地利之險，人為之守；天時之善，人為之乘。有所不戰，戰必勝矣。惜乎終不能聽，徒使孟子託之空言也。可慨已夫！

易
translation_en:
But what is it like when abundant support reaches its utmost extent? Across all the land, from east to west [?], vast as the world is, those who come to submit, as people look for clouds and rainbows in a drought, gather in multitudes, each fearing only that he may fall behind. Throughout the world, from south to north, broad as its territories are, those who come to give their allegiance, as people flee flood and fire, arrive in throngs, each fearing only that others may precede him. There is no need to rely on territorial boundaries to delimit the realm: those who give their allegiance unite all under Heaven in a single heart, with none divided in loyalty. What could surpass this utmost abundance of support? There is no need to rely on mountains and ravines as defenses: those who submit share a single purpose throughout the land, with no thought of rebellion. What could compare with this utmost abundance of support? Thus, one who attains the Way gains abundant support, and all under Heaven give their allegiance in this manner. Harmony among the people can reach no higher point, and every battle must end in victory. Why, then, should favorable timing and advantageous terrain still be regarded as things to rely upon?

In general, during the Warring States period, the Way of the sages and worthies was obstructed, while the pursuit of achievement and profit increased daily. Those who employed military force often devoted themselves to favorable timing and advantageous terrain, without understanding that attaining the Way must provide their foundation. They concerned themselves only with minor matters and neglected the greater ones, putting secondary details in order without examining the root. Such men hardly deserve to be called skilled in governing. Thus Mengzi advanced here his argument that favorable timing and advantageous terrain are inferior to harmony among the people; at this point he further made attaining the Way the foundation of that harmony. Had the rulers of that time truly been able to attain the Way and thereby win the people's hearts, the people would have defended their advantageous terrain and exploited favorable timing for them. They might refrain from battle, but whenever they fought, they would surely win. Alas, in the end they could not heed him, leaving Mengzi to entrust his teaching to empty words alone. How lamentable!

Book of Changes (Yi)
