考試官教諭張批〔不煩繩削而無自精到，當是作手。〕
考試官教諭李批〔有源委，有發越，諸之於篇猶有餘地者，手也。〕
學之道，有本有末，得其本則末自隨之。何則？人之一身，人物之本。學者必於其本焉圖之，則舉近以及遠，守約而施博，措之於治人應物，亦無乎不順且利矣。否則大本一失，更學何事？秖見夫人之衆、物之夥，治之而不能治，應之而不能應，徒自紛擾耳。君子知其然，其學汲汲，其心皇皇，一理未明，求以知之；一理未備，求以體之。所以然者何也？無非為潤身計耳。故身潤而本立，本立而末隨，天下之事可徐就吾之條理矣。噫！此君子之究本後末，所以為善學歟？邵子曰：「君子之學以潤身為本。」請因是而
translation_en:
…is secondary. Writers in the examination hall fail to investigate the origins and full implications of the topic; most force connections and wander into tangents, which is particularly tiresome. This essay can trace the subject to its source and set it down in writing. Its reasoning has firm foundations, and its language has movement and variety. Its emphasis, midway through, on the word “root” is especially significant. The author is probably a man of mature learning and discernment. This piece should be recorded to correct the prevailing habits of examination writing.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Without requiring correction or pruning, it achieves precision and depth of itself [?]. Surely this is an accomplished writer.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “There are origins and ramifications, and there is expansive expression. Even after setting these into an essay [?], the author still has resources to spare: this is a practiced hand.”

The way of learning has a root and branches. Once its root is grasped, the branches follow of themselves. Why is this? One’s own person is the root of one’s dealings with people and things. A learner must direct his efforts toward this root. Then, proceeding from what is near to reach what is distant, and holding to what is essential while applying it broadly, he will find that, when put into practice in governing others and responding to things, everything proceeds smoothly and advantageously. Otherwise, once the great root is lost, what else is there to learn? One sees only the multitude of people and the profusion of things: one tries to govern them but cannot, and tries to respond to them but cannot. One merely entangles oneself in confusion.

The gentleman understands this. He pursues learning urgently, his mind ever concerned. If a single principle remains unclear, he seeks to understand it; if a single principle is not fully realized in himself, he seeks to embody it. Why does he do so? It is entirely for the sake of enriching his own person. Thus, when his person is enriched, the root is established; when the root is established, the branches follow. The affairs of the world can then gradually be brought into accord with the ordered principles within himself. Ah! Is it not the gentleman’s thorough investigation of the root and subordination of the branches that makes him adept at learning?

Master Shao said: “The gentleman’s learning takes enriching his own person as its foundation.” Allow me, on this basis, to…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
論焉夫天下之事莫不有本一事有一事
之本一物有一物之本物本於萌藪本於
一發生本於一陽之後斂穫本於一陰之
還水本於源之遠山本於基之厚學之本
獨不在於潤身乎是故面墻之立豈屋之
蔀不學過也舍己之田耘人之田不知本
也然則人必貴於學學必貴於務本君子
可少忽也哉嘗試以吾身自列於天地者
而遥觀之未嘗不嘆吾身之大而不知學
===
者小之也夫天地者萬物之父母也人與
我雖共為父母之子而本末緩急亦未嘗
混焉者也何者明己之德而後民可新成
己之德而後物可成身不行道不能行於
妻子己身罔治豈能治乎國人此理也亦
勢也君子知吾身為天下人物之本是以
不屑屑於他事惟以潤身為急固非欲獨
善也知本之在此而所務亦在此也不遑
遑於他務獨以潤身為心抑非欲忘世也
punctuated: 論焉。夫天下之事莫不有本，一事有一事之本，一物有一物之本。物本於萌，藪本於一，發生本於一陽之後，斂穫本於一陰之還；水本於源之遠，山本於基之厚。學之本獨不在於潤身乎？是故面墻之立，豈屋之蔀？不學過也。舍己之田，耘人之田，不知本也。然則人必貴於學，學必貴於務本，君子可少忽也哉？嘗試以吾身自列於天地者而遥觀之，未嘗不嘆吾身之大，而不知學者小之也。夫天地者，萬物之父母也。人與我雖共為父母之子，而本末緩急亦未嘗混焉者也。何者？明己之德而後民可新，成己之德而後物可成。身不行，道不能行於妻子；己身罔治，豈能治乎國人？此理也，亦勢也。君子知吾身為天下人物之本，是以不屑屑於他事，惟以潤身為急，固非欲獨善也，知本之在此，而所務亦在此也。不遑遑於他務，獨以潤身為心，抑非欲忘世也。
translation_en:
…discuss this. Nothing among the affairs of the world is without a root: each affair has its own root, and each thing has its own root. Things are rooted in their sprouts; thickets are rooted in the one [?]. Growth originates with the emergence of the first yang; gathering and harvesting originate with the return of the first yin. Water depends upon the remoteness of its source, and mountains upon the depth of their foundations. Can the root of learning alone fail to lie in enriching one’s person?

Thus, when one stands as though facing a wall, is it because the house is screened from light [?]? The fault lies in failing to learn. To abandon one’s own field and weed another’s is to be ignorant of the root. People must therefore value learning, and in learning they must value attending to the root. Can the gentleman afford the slightest neglect of this? Whenever I try to view from afar my own person standing between Heaven and Earth, I cannot but marvel at its greatness, and at how those who do not understand learning diminish it.

Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things. Although others and I are alike their children, distinctions between root and branch, and between what may wait and what is urgent, have never thereby been confused. Why is this? Only after making one’s own virtue bright can the people be renewed; only after perfecting one’s own virtue can other things be brought to fulfillment. If one does not personally practice the Way, it cannot prevail even among one’s wife and children. If one’s own person is not well governed, how can one govern the people of the state? This follows both from principle and from the circumstances of things.

The gentleman knows that his own person is the root of his dealings with the people and things of the world. Thus he does not busy himself with other affairs, but regards enriching his person as urgent. Certainly this is not because he wishes merely to perfect himself alone: he knows that the root lies here, and so directs his efforts here as well. He does not anxiously pursue other tasks, but sets his mind solely upon enriching his person. Nor is this because he wishes to forget the world.…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
知所急者在此而所學亦在此也春絃夏
誦學非不勤也無非為潤身而設左詩右
書學非不富也圖非為潤身而謀於大學
而學焉必知脩身為本而格致誠正之功
無少忽於中庸而學焉必知誠身為本而
博審慎篤之功無少息學於易以求潤身
於時學於書以求潤身於中學於詩禮春
秋以求潤身於正於敬義不敢以貪為學
懼其侈吾身而泛也不敢以固為學懼其
===
迂吾身而僻也不敢以傲為學懼其卓鶩
吾身而孫也不敢以夸為學懼其猖獗吾
身而惟也盤有銘几有誡將以潤此身也
左準繩右規矩將以潤此身也襲絅於錦
闇然日章芟茅於徑介然成路將以潤此
身也曾子曰心廣體胖孟子曰睟面盎背
君子有之矣由是推吾潤身者以潤家推
吾潤身者以潤國推吾潤身者以潤天下
使人由其誠教人盡其材其施之也不悖
punctuated: 知所急者在此，而所學亦在此也。春絃夏誦，學非不勤也，無非為潤身而設；左詩右書，學非不富也，圖非為潤身而謀。於大學而學焉，必知脩身為本，而格致誠正之功無少忽；於中庸而學焉，必知誠身為本，而博審慎篤之功無少息。學於易，以求潤身於時；學於書，以求潤身於中；學於詩禮春秋，以求潤身於正、於敬義。不敢以貪為學，懼其侈吾身而泛也；不敢以固為學，懼其迂吾身而僻也；不敢以傲為學，懼其卓鶩吾身而孫也；不敢以夸為學，懼其猖獗吾身而惟也。盤有銘，几有誡，將以潤此身也；左準繩，右規矩，將以潤此身也；襲絅於錦，闇然日章，芟茅於徑，介然成路，將以潤此身也。曾子曰：「心廣體胖。」孟子曰：「睟面盎背。」君子有之矣。由是推吾潤身者以潤家，推吾潤身者以潤國，推吾潤身者以潤天下，使人由其誠，教人盡其材，其施之也不悖
translation_en: …knowing that what requires urgent attention lies here, he likewise directs his learning here. In spring he plays the strings, and in summer he recites: his study is certainly diligent, and all of it is arranged to enrich his person. With the Odes on his left and the Documents on his right, his learning is certainly abundant; his plans, too, aim to enrich his person [?]. In studying the Great Learning, he must recognize cultivating the person as the foundation, never neglecting the work of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind. In studying the Doctrine of the Mean, he must recognize making his person sincere as the foundation, never ceasing the work of broad learning, careful inquiry, thoughtful reflection, and earnest practice. He studies the Changes to enrich his person through timeliness; the Documents to enrich his person through the mean; and the Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals to enrich his person through correctness, reverence, and righteousness. He dares not pursue learning acquisitively, fearing that it would make him extravagant and diffuse. He dares not pursue learning obstinately, fearing that it would make him impractical and one-sided. He dares not pursue learning arrogantly, fearing that it would drive him into lofty striving and make him ‘submissive’ [?]. He dares not pursue learning boastfully, fearing that it would make him unruly and lead him into an uncertain further fault [?]. Inscriptions on his basin and admonitions on his desk serve to enrich this person of his. A leveling instrument and marking cord on his left, a compass and square on his right, serve to enrich this person of his. Wearing a plain gauze robe over brocade, his virtue grows daily more manifest despite its unobtrusiveness; cutting the thatch from a footpath, he makes a distinct road. These things serve to enrich this person of his. Zengzi said, ‘The mind is broad and the body at ease.’ Mencius said, ‘It shines clearly in the face and fills the back.’ The gentleman possesses these qualities. From this, he extends what enriches his own person to enrich his family, his state, and all under Heaven. He enables people to follow their sincerity and teaches them to develop their capacities fully; in putting this into practice, he does not run counter to what is right…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
其求之也不拂源泉混混有本者固如是
乎嗚呼學之道有本有末達之天下國
家本係於一人之身使身不潤抑亦末矣
本之則無如之何多聞適以為泛博學適
以為僻求之愈峻適以為孫造之愈深適
以為悖不學之加一道之累也一事之窮
一本之失也安於自肆難於自檢趨道之
名而自逸於形器之外取學之末而自淪
於妄誕之歸無悖乎致遠則泥矣雖然君
===
子所務之本其義甚大在易謂之元在春
秋謂之一在子思謂之大本在仲舒謂之
大始邵堯夫以內聖外王之學為抑末反
本之論其知此義矣不然演河圖何以以
中五為本制圓圖何以以天根為言愚於
此又有以知堯夫知本之本焉因併及之
同前
同考試官教諭張 批此作議論精切筆勢雄健
邃貢
punctuated:
其求之也不拂，源泉混混，有本者固如是乎！嗚呼！學之道有本有末，達之天下國家，本係於一人之身。使身不潤，抑亦末矣，本之則無如之何。多聞適以為泛，博學適以為僻，求之愈峻，適以為孫，造之愈深，適以為悖。不學之加，一道之累也；一事之窮，一本之失也。安於自肆，難於自檢，趨道之名，而自逸於形器之外；取學之末，而自淪於妄誕之歸。無悖乎？致遠則泥矣。雖然，君子所務之本，其義甚大。在易謂之元，在春秋謂之一，在子思謂之大本，在仲舒謂之大始。邵堯夫以內聖外王之學為抑末反本之論，其知此義矣。不然，演河圖何以以中五為本？制圓圖何以以天根為言？愚於此又有以知堯夫知本之本焉，因併及之。
同前。
同考試官教諭張批：此作議論精切，筆勢雄健。
邃貢
translation_en:
…and what he seeks does not run counter to it. Like a spring flowing ceaselessly, surely this is how one who has a root must be! Alas! The way of learning has a root and branches. Extend it to the world, the state, and the family: its root remains bound to the person of a single individual. If that person is not enriched, one is merely attending to the branches, and can do nothing about the root. Hearing much serves only to make one diffuse; extensive learning serves only to make one eccentric. The more exacting the pursuit, the more it leads to timidity [?]; the deeper the attainment, the more it leads to perversity. This is no enhancement of learning, but a burden upon the Way [?]; the exhaustive investigation of a single matter entails the loss of the root. Comfortable with self-indulgence and finding self-restraint difficult, such people pursue the name of the Way while letting themselves wander beyond tangible forms and objects. They seize upon the branches of learning and sink into delusion and absurdity. Is this not perverse? In attempting to reach far, they become mired.
Nevertheless, the root to which the gentleman devotes himself has very great significance. In the Book of Changes it is called the Primal; in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the One; by Zisi, the Great Root; and by Zhongshu, the Great Beginning. Shao Yaofu used the learning of inward sagehood and outward kingliness to argue for subordinating the branches and returning to the root. He surely understood this meaning. Otherwise, why, in expounding the River Chart, did he take the central five as the root? Why, in constructing the Circular Diagram, did he speak of the Root of Heaven? From this I, in my humble view, have further grounds to know that Yaofu understood the root of the root. I have therefore discussed this as well.
Same as above.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: This composition's arguments are penetrating and precise, and its writing vigorous and forceful.
Sui Gong [?].

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
〔博而約甚而實非論場之巨擘歟〕
考試官教諭張　批〔論得邵子意旨章勢圓活循循〕
考試官教諭李　批〔意甚高學蔽今有諸條特之作〕
善為學者不于其末而于其本焉學不可
以不知本也學知所本則為已而不為人
務內而不務外其所學也大矣若不究其
本而惟末是圖則為人矣為人而學將何
以有成哉善學君子所以致嚴於此而學
===
以潤身為本焉學本潤身則知所以為己
而積中發外之盛自有不可遏者彼治人
應物君子何暇為哉然亦非故置人物於
度外也蓋以治已為重而治人在所輕治
已為急而應物在所緩況吾之學能潤身
則治人應物特舉而措之耳噫學以潤身
為本此君子所以為善學者歟請因邵子
之言而論之人之生也五行之秀鍾之二
氣之精孕之其體則天地之塞其性則天
punctuated:
〔博而約，甚而實，非論場之巨擘歟？〕
考試官教諭張，批〔論得邵子意旨，章勢圓活，循循。〕
考試官教諭李，批〔意甚高，學蔽今，有諸條特之作。〕
善為學者，不于其末，而于其本焉。學不可以不知本也。學知所本，則為已而不為人，務內而不務外，其所學也大矣。若不究其本，而惟末是圖，則為人矣。為人而學，將何以有成哉？善學君子所以致嚴於此，而學以潤身為本焉。學本潤身，則知所以為己，而積中發外之盛，自有不可遏者。彼治人應物，君子何暇為哉？然亦非故置人物於度外也。蓋以治已為重，而治人在所輕；治已為急，而應物在所緩。況吾之學能潤身，則治人應物，特舉而措之耳。噫！學以潤身為本，此君子所以為善學者歟？請因邵子之言而論之。人之生也，五行之秀鍾之，二氣之精孕之。其體則天地之塞，其性則天
translation_en:
〔…Broad yet concise, profound [?] yet substantial—is this not the work of a master of examination discourse?〕
Examiner Zhang, a Director of Studies, comments: 〔The discussion captures Master Shao’s meaning; the composition flows smoothly and flexibly, proceeding in an orderly manner.〕
Examiner Li, a Director of Studies, comments: 〔The conception is very lofty; the learning surpasses that of the present day [?]. This is a work of outstanding distinction [?].〕
Those skilled in learning attend to its root rather than its branches. In learning, one must know the root. When learners know what to take as their foundation, they learn for themselves rather than for others, directing their efforts inward rather than outward. Great indeed is such learning! If they do not investigate its root but pursue only its branches, they learn for others. How could learning for others bring any accomplishment? This is why gentlemen skilled in learning are so exacting on this point and take the enrichment of their own persons as the foundation of learning. When learning has this foundation, they understand how to learn for themselves, and the abundance accumulated within and manifested without naturally becomes impossible to restrain. As for governing others and responding to external affairs, what leisure does the gentleman have to attend to these? Yet neither does he deliberately exclude other people and affairs from his consideration. Rather, he regards governing himself as weighty and governing others as less weighty; governing himself as urgent and responding to external affairs as less pressing. Moreover, if my learning can enrich my own person, then governing others and responding to affairs require only that I put it into practice. Ah! Taking the enrichment of one’s person as the foundation of learning—is this not what makes the gentleman skilled in learning? Allow me to discuss this on the basis of Master Shao’s words. When human beings are born, the finest qualities of the Five Phases gather in them, and the essence of the two vital forces gives them life. Their bodily substance is that which fills Heaven and Earth; their nature is Heaven’s…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
闡一貫心廣體胖曾之學有以潤其身矣
知言養氣孟子之學以潤身為本也故充
塞天地睟面盎背孟之學有以潤其身矣
聖賢之學皆以潤身為本故能為天地立
心為生民立命為萬世開太平其事業耿
耿不磨何莫不自潤身中來耶君子以聖
賢為標的以潤身為根本仁義可以潤身
也吾則於仁義而學焉禮智可以潤身也
吾則於禮智而學焉必格物必致知學之
不已其功必誠意必正心學之不怠其力
以誠敬為入門以踐履為實地不忠不信
不習日學曾子之三省勿視勿聽勿言勿
動日學顏子之四勿窮理盡性學孟氏之
知言直養無害學孟氏之養氣道理無往
而不在君子無往而不學非為誇人也非
為應物也惟欲以潤身為本焉但見欲淨
而理還人泯而天定非念不足以喪其所
養外物不足以奪其所守心與理融理與
punctuated: 闡一貫，心廣體胖，曾之學有以潤其身矣。知言養氣，孟子之學以潤身為本也。故充塞天地，睟面盎背，孟之學有以潤其身矣。聖賢之學皆以潤身為本，故能為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平，其事業耿耿不磨，何莫不自潤身中來耶？君子以聖賢為標的，以潤身為根本。仁義可以潤身也，吾則於仁義而學焉；禮智可以潤身也，吾則於禮智而學焉。必格物，必致知，學之不已其功；必誠意，必正心，學之不怠其力。以誠敬為入門，以踐履為實地。不忠、不信、不習，日學曾子之三省；勿視、勿聽、勿言、勿動，日學顏子之四勿。窮理盡性，學孟氏之知言；直養無害，學孟氏之養氣。道理無往而不在，君子無往而不學。非為誇人也，非為應物也，惟欲以潤身為本焉。但見欲淨而理還，人泯而天定，非念不足以喪其所養，外物不足以奪其所守。心與理融，理與
translation_en:
…elucidating the single thread that runs through the Way, with the mind broadened and the body at ease: Zengzi’s learning thus served to enrich his person. Understanding words and nourishing vital energy: Mengzi’s learning took enriching the person as its foundation. Thus his vital energy filled Heaven and Earth, and his virtue shone in his face and suffused his back: Mengzi’s learning thus served to enrich his person. The learning of sages and worthies all takes enriching the person as its foundation. Hence they could establish a heart for Heaven and Earth, establish a destiny for the people, and inaugurate supreme peace for all generations. Their achievements shine brightly and cannot be effaced. Which of these did not arise from enriching the person?

The gentleman takes the sages and worthies as his models and enriching his person as his foundation. Benevolence and righteousness can enrich the person, so I devote myself to learning benevolence and righteousness; ritual propriety and wisdom can enrich the person, so I devote myself to learning ritual propriety and wisdom. One must investigate things and extend knowledge, never ceasing one’s efforts in learning; one must make one’s intentions sincere and rectify one’s mind, never slackening one’s exertions in learning. One takes sincerity and reverence as the gateway, and putting learning into practice as firm ground. Each day one learns Zengzi’s threefold self-examination: whether one has been disloyal, untrustworthy, or failed to practice what one has learned. Each day one learns Master Yan’s four prohibitions: do not look, listen, speak, or act contrary to ritual propriety. By fully investigating principle and realizing one’s nature, one learns Mengzi’s understanding of words; by nourishing vital energy through uprightness without harming it, one learns Mengzi’s cultivation of vital energy. There is nowhere that the principles of the Way are absent, and nowhere that the gentleman does not learn. He does so neither to impress others nor to respond to external affairs, but solely to make enriching his person the foundation.

Then one sees desires cleared away and principle restored, human selfishness extinguished and Heaven’s order established. Improper thoughts cannot destroy what he has cultivated, and external things cannot wrest away what he holds fast. The mind merges with principle, and principle with…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
心會仁義根於心其發見自不可禦禮智
本於内其生色自不可遏包含徧覆無所
不愛其氣象一春風和氣之可挹仁之潤
身何如耶稱量裁度無所不宜其氣象一
秋霜烈日之可畏義之潤身何如耶左準
繩右規矩肅肅乎其威儀禮之英華發越
不其潤身乎判是非别邪正昭昭乎其藻
鑑智之光彩旁燭不其潤身乎仰不愧俯
不怍從容自得於鳶飛魚躍之天動静何
===
舒泰也無入非無鬼責優游自適於光風
霽月之鄉襟懷何灑落也飲水甘於列鼎
不願乎人之膏粱緼袍華於珮玉不願乎
人之文繡君子之學至於潤身如此始不
負其所期不負其所學矣其即顏子具體
而微之日曾子心廣體胖之時孟子睟面
盎背之境也由是推無不準動無不化内
焉而家則家無不齊所以潤其家者此也
外焉而國則國無不治所以潤其國者此
punctuated: 心會。仁義根於心，其發見自不可禦；禮智本於内，其生色自不可遏。包含徧覆，無所不愛，其氣象一春風和氣之可挹，仁之潤身何如耶？稱量裁度，無所不宜，其氣象一秋霜烈日之可畏，義之潤身何如耶？左準繩，右規矩，肅肅乎其威儀，禮之英華發越，不其潤身乎？判是非，别邪正，昭昭乎其藻鑑，智之光彩旁燭，不其潤身乎？仰不愧，俯不怍，從容自得於鳶飛魚躍之天，動静何舒泰也！無入非，無鬼責，優游自適於光風霽月之鄉，襟懷何灑落也！飲水甘於列鼎，不願乎人之膏粱；緼袍華於珮玉，不願乎人之文繡。君子之學至於潤身如此，始不負其所期，不負其所學矣。其即顏子具體而微之日，曾子心廣體胖之時，孟子睟面盎背之境也。由是推無不準，動無不化。内焉而家，則家無不齊，所以潤其家者此也；外焉而國，則國無不治，所以潤其國者此
translation_en: …unites with the mind. Benevolence and righteousness take root in the mind, and their manifestation naturally cannot be restrained; ritual propriety and wisdom are grounded within, and their radiant expression naturally cannot be suppressed. Embracing and sheltering all, leaving nothing unloved, his bearing is like a spring breeze whose gentle warmth one can drink in. How great is the enrichment of the person through benevolence! Weighing and judging, finding what is fitting in every case, his bearing is like autumn frost and the blazing sun in their awesomeness. How great is the enrichment of the person through righteousness! With the plumb line to his left and compass and square to his right, how solemn is his dignified bearing! The flowering excellence of ritual propriety shines forth: does it not enrich his person? Distinguishing right from wrong and separating the deviant from the upright, how luminous is his discerning judgment! The brilliance of wisdom casts its light in every direction: does it not enrich his person? Looking up without shame and looking down without embarrassment, he is composed and at ease in the realm where kites soar and fish leap. How relaxed and at peace he is, whether active or still! With no censure from others [?] and no reproach from spirits, he wanders freely and contentedly in the realm of clear breezes and the moon after rain. How open and unburdened is his heart! Drinking water tastes sweeter to him than delicacies arrayed in ritual cauldrons; he does not covet others’ rich fare. A robe padded with hemp floss seems more splendid than jade pendants; he does not covet others’ embroidered finery. Only when the gentleman’s learning enriches his person in this way does he fulfill his aspirations and do justice to what he has learned. This is the stage at which Master Yan possessed the full substance of sagehood, though in lesser measure; the time when Master Zeng’s mind was broad and his body at ease; the state in which Master Meng’s virtue shone in his face and filled his back. Proceeding from this, every extension of his virtue accords with the proper standard, and every action transforms others. Inwardly, within the family, the family is invariably brought into order: this is what enriches his family. Outwardly, within the state, the state is invariably well governed: what enriches his state is this…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也遠而天下則天下無不平所以潤天下
者亦此也所謂盡人之性而盡物之性者
在是所謂贊天地之化育而與天地叅者
在是是則君子潤身之學乃有用之實學
學之知其本者也視彼世之專事詞章與
夫功名空虛以為學者非惟不足以潤身
且不足以治人非惟不足以裕己且不足
以應物其於脩己治人應物之道胥失之
矣若是者謂之學且不可况可謂之善學
===
乎君子之學與此蓋天淵矣慨自世道湮
微聖賢潤身之學寥寥絕倡久矣不有先
覺孰啓我人君子之學以潤身為本誠千
萬世學者之指南與論而至是則知同一
學也內外人己之分君子小人判焉務內
而為己則為君子而可以為聖為賢務外
而為人則為小人而流於愚不肖始雖相
近而終則相遠所謂毫釐之差千里之繆
者也後之學者尚當致謹於內外人己之
punctuated: 也。遠而天下，則天下無不平，所以潤天下者亦此也。所謂盡人之性而盡物之性者在是，所謂贊天地之化育而與天地叅者在是。是則君子潤身之學，乃有用之實學，學之知其本者也。視彼世之專事詞章與夫功名空虛以為學者，非惟不足以潤身，且不足以治人；非惟不足以裕己，且不足以應物。其於脩己治人應物之道，胥失之矣。若是者，謂之學且不可，况可謂之善學乎？君子之學與此蓋天淵矣！慨自世道湮微，聖賢潤身之學寥寥絕倡久矣。不有先覺，孰啓我人？君子之學以潤身為本，誠千萬世學者之指南與！論而至是，則知同一學也，內外人己之分，君子小人判焉。務內而為己，則為君子，而可以為聖為賢；務外而為人，則為小人，而流於愚不肖。始雖相近，而終則相遠，所謂毫釐之差、千里之繆者也。後之學者，尚當致謹於內外人己之
translation_en:
…Extending farther to all under Heaven, none will remain unpacified; this, too, is how one enriches all under Heaven. Herein lies what is meant by fully realizing human nature and the nature of things; herein lies what is meant by assisting the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth and forming a triad with them. Thus the gentleman’s learning, which enriches his person, is substantive learning of practical use: learning that recognizes its root. Consider those in the world who regard exclusive devotion to literary composition and the empty pursuit of achievement and fame as learning. Not only is this insufficient to enrich their persons; it is also insufficient to govern others. Not only is it insufficient to cultivate their own resources; it is also insufficient to respond to things. They have altogether lost the way of cultivating oneself, governing others, and responding to things. Such pursuits cannot even be called learning; how much less can they be called learning well? The difference between the gentleman’s learning and these pursuits is indeed as great as that between Heaven and the abyss!

Alas, since the ways of the world fell into obscurity and decline, the sages’ and worthies’ learning that enriches the person has long had scarcely anyone to champion it. Without those who awaken first, who would enlighten us? That the gentleman’s learning takes enriching his person as its foundation is truly a compass for learners through countless generations! Having pursued the discussion thus far, we see that, although all alike engage in learning, the distinction between inward and outward concerns, between learning for others and learning for oneself, separates the gentleman from the petty man. Those who attend to what is inward and learn for themselves become gentlemen and may become sages and worthies. Those who attend to what is outward and learn for others become petty men and lapse into folly and unworthiness. Though close together at the outset, they end far apart. This is what is meant by a discrepancy of a hair’s breadth leading to an error of a thousand li. Learners of later times should therefore exercise the utmost care in distinguishing between inward and outward concerns, between learning for others and learning for oneself…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
間而致嚴於君子小人之戒為之柰何亦
曰學以潤身為本
表
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表　刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔得駢儷體〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔典雅〕
考試官教諭張　批〔典則可觀〕
考試官教諭李　批〔表佳〕
===
伏以
神兵會府任隆翊贊之司天極環樞職專
靖密之寄班序近聯於三省事權高出於
六卿
禮遇同宰相之榮地分極人臣之貴非全材
如伊呂負荷奚堪必碩望若甫由登庸庶
稱顧茲
特授未遂堅辭竊念臣必大早歲孤窮爰鞠
母氏中年強學輒忝詞科偶受知於
punctuated:
間，而致嚴於君子小人之戒。為之柰何？亦曰：學以潤身為本。

表
擬宋以周必大為樞密使謝表　刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔得駢儷體〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔典雅〕
考試官教諭張　批〔典則可觀〕
考試官教諭李　批〔表佳〕

伏以：神兵會府，任隆翊贊之司；天極環樞，職專靖密之寄。班序近聯於三省，事權高出於六卿。禮遇同宰相之榮，地分極人臣之貴。非全材如伊呂，負荷奚堪？必碩望若甫由，登庸庶稱。顧茲特授，未遂堅辭。竊念臣必大，早歲孤窮，爰鞠母氏；中年強學，輒忝詞科。偶受知於
translation_en:
…between these distinctions, and strictly heed the warning that separates the gentleman from the petty man. How is this to be done? Simply put: learning takes the cultivation of oneself as its foundation.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks in the person of Zhou Bida upon his appointment as Military Affairs Commissioner under the Song. By Diao Yu.
Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Achieves the parallel-prose form.”
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Classically correct and worthy of admiration.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “A fine memorial.”

I humbly submit: In the office where the imperial armies’ affairs converge, weighty is the responsibility of assisting the sovereign; at the pivot about which the celestial pole revolves, the charge is devoted to matters of security and secrecy. Its ceremonial rank stands close to the Three Departments; its authority over affairs rises above the Six Ministers. The honors accorded it equal those of a Grand Councilor; its standing reaches the highest distinction attainable by a subject. Without comprehensive ability like that of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, how could one bear this burden? Only with outstanding prestige like that of Shen Fu and Zhong You might one prove worthy of appointment.

Yet this special appointment has come to me, and my firm efforts to decline it have not prevailed. I reflect that I, your servant Bida, was fatherless and poor in my early years, nurtured by my mother. In middle life I applied myself diligently to learning and undeservedly succeeded in the literary examination. By chance I received recognition from …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
先朝爲堪掌制辛占追逢乎
呂運進侍
經筵應
詔陳謨頗切救時之弊講和索禮敵正敵國之
名既因事而請祠薦收錄而補外
召還翰苑前後幾及六年逆犯
龍鱗包容未至三黜論事本原於愚直蒙
恩殊出於尋常甫與知乎兵機遽正位於溫省
制詞寬大誤重忠勞之
===
天語丁寧豫隆宣撫之託
眷非意及愧與憂并茲蓋伏遇
褒
○○○○
聰明神授
英毅天成
握符奮起於外藩受
命入承乎大統小心契周文之翼翼大孝符虞
舜之夔夔達聰明之天聰謹在茲之日監
punctuated:
先朝，爲堪掌制，辛占追逢乎呂運，進侍經筵，應詔陳謨，頗切救時之弊。講和索禮，敵正敵國之名。既因事而請祠，薦收錄而補外。召還翰苑，前後幾及六年；逆犯龍鱗，包容未至三黜。論事本原於愚直，蒙恩殊出於尋常。甫與知乎兵機，遽正位於溫省。制詞寬大，誤重忠勞之；天語丁寧，豫隆宣撫之託。眷非意及，愧與憂并。
茲蓋伏遇褒○○○○，聰明神授，英毅天成。握符奮起於外藩，受命入承乎大統。小心契周文之翼翼，大孝符虞舜之夔夔。達聰明之天聰，謹在茲之日監。
translation_en:
…under the former emperor, I was deemed capable of drafting imperial decrees. I was fortunate to encounter an auspicious reign [?] and advanced to attend the Classics Colloquium. Responding to an imperial command, I presented proposals that closely addressed the remedying of contemporary abuses. In negotiating peace and seeking proper ceremonial treatment, I sought to establish the designation of the opposing state as an equal [?]. Subsequently, on account of an affair, I requested a temple sinecure; I was again taken into service and appointed to a post outside the capital. Recalled to the Hanlin Academy, I served there for nearly six years in all. Though I offended the imperial majesty, I was treated with forbearance and did not suffer three dismissals. My discussion of affairs sprang from simple-minded candor, yet the favor I received far exceeded the ordinary. No sooner had I begun to participate in directing military affairs than I was elevated to the principal position in the “Wen Secretariat” [?]. The decree’s wording was generous, mistakenly giving great weight to my loyal service [text doubtful]; Your Majesty’s words were earnest, already laying upon me the weighty charge of military pacification. Such favor exceeded my expectations; shame and anxiety came together.
This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty [褒○○○○: text unclear], whose intelligence is divinely bestowed and whose heroic resolution is innate. Holding the tally of authority, you rose from an outlying princely domain; receiving the mandate, you entered the court to inherit the imperial succession. Your cautious care accords with the reverence of King Wen of Zhou; your great filial devotion matches the respectful awe of Shun of Yu. You extend your heaven-given powers of perception and understanding, remaining mindful that Heaven’s daily scrutiny rests here…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
兩宮齊壽
帝心允恊予太和三載終喪
乾斷不揺於羣議思開拓而銳志恢復念艱
難而留意守成改稱謂以挫敵驕減歲幣
以定鄰好雖金人無可乘之釁而
皇朝有不戰之威猶以訓兵當謹於無形雪耻
終期於有待遂令重寄猥及非才圖籍周
知素乏曾宣靖之先見號令明審敢希王
文定之後塵力願竭於疲駑行恐儕于跛
鼈私憂過計不以治而忘危養銳蓄威將
以全而取勝仰資
===
廟筭冀荅
鴻休伏願
王靈丕振於華夷
聖武布昭於遐邇
天戈遠指行見中原之肅清露布遥馳佇聽邊
塵之蕩掃〔臣必大無任瞻〕
天仰
punctuated:
兩宮齊壽，帝心允恊予太和；三載終喪，乾斷不揺於羣議。思開拓而銳志恢復，念艱難而留意守成。改稱謂以挫敵驕，減歲幣以定鄰好。雖金人無可乘之釁，而皇朝有不戰之威。猶以訓兵當謹於無形，雪耻終期於有待，遂令重寄猥及非才。圖籍周知，素乏曾宣靖之先見；號令明審，敢希王文定之後塵。力願竭於疲駑，行恐儕于跛鼈。私憂過計，不以治而忘危；養銳蓄威，將以全而取勝。仰資廟筭，冀荅鴻休。
伏願王靈丕振於華夷，聖武布昭於遐邇。天戈遠指，行見中原之肅清；露布遥馳，佇聽邊塵之蕩掃。〔臣必大無任瞻〕天仰
translation_en:
…Both palaces enjoy longevity, and Your Majesty’s heart accords truly with supreme harmony [?]. When the three years of mourning ended, your sovereign resolve remained unshaken by the many opinions offered. Contemplating expansion, you set your determination firmly upon recovery of the lost territories; mindful of hardship, you attend carefully to preserving what has been achieved. You changed the forms of address to curb the enemy’s arrogance and reduced the annual payments to secure amicable relations with our neighbor. Although the Jin offer no opening to exploit, our imperial dynasty possesses an awe-inspiring power that requires no battle. Nevertheless, you consider that troops must be trained diligently before any danger takes shape, and that wiping away humiliation must ultimately await the proper occasion. Thus you have allowed this weighty charge to fall upon one so unworthy as myself.
In comprehensive knowledge of maps and records, I have always lacked the foresight of Zeng, posthumously titled Xuanjing; in the clarity and discernment of commands, I venture to hope that I may follow in the footsteps of Wang, posthumously titled Wending. Though a weary, inferior horse, I wish to exhaust my strength; yet I fear that my progress will match that of a lame turtle. My private anxiety prompts excessive deliberation: I shall not forget danger amid good order. I shall nurture our vigor and accumulate our might, intending to secure victory with our forces intact. Looking up for the support of the court’s strategic counsels, I hope to requite your great favor.
I humbly wish that your royal majesty may resound mightily among Chinese and foreign peoples alike, and that your sagely martial power may shine forth far and near. Wherever Heaven’s weapons point afar, may we soon see the Central Plain pacified; as victory proclamations speed from distant places, may we await news that the dust of warfare along the frontier has been swept away. 〔Your servant Bida cannot contain his feelings as he gazes toward〕 Heaven and looks up toward…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
同考試官訓導陸　批〔家傳人誦之書能條陳者亦少惟此篇隨問隨對其熟於〕
當代制作者乎是用録出
考試官教諭張　批〔究心當代典制者考據博通之士也〕
考試官教諭李　批〔敷某詳明具有筆力〕
前聖迭興而治教之典已著後聖繼作而
治教之典益明蓋天能賦民以性而不能
使之全其性聖人者出任君師之大責為
天民之先覺則其所以治而教之者當必
有道焉且又筆之於書以垂教後世先聖
punctuated:
聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場，策，第一問。
同考試官訓導陸批〔家傳人誦之書，能條陳者亦少，惟此篇隨問隨對，其熟於〕當代制作者乎？是用録出。
考試官教諭張批〔究心當代典制者，考據博通之士也。〕
考試官教諭李批〔敷某詳明，具有筆力。〕
前聖迭興，而治教之典已著；後聖繼作，而治教之典益明。蓋天能賦民以性，而不能使之全其性。聖人者出，任君師之大責，為天民之先覺，則其所以治而教之者，當必有道焉。且又筆之於書，以垂教後世。先聖
translation_en:
…toward Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling reverence, I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to you.
Third Session. Policy Essay. First Question.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor: “Though these books are handed down in every household and recited by everyone, few can set out their contents systematically. This essay alone answers each point as it is asked. Its author must be well versed in the institutions of the present dynasty! It has therefore been selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “One who devotes his attention to the statutes and institutions of the present dynasty is a scholar of broad learning and thorough command of textual evidence.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The exposition [?] is detailed and clear, and displays forceful writing.”
The sages of earlier times arose in succession, and the canons of government and instruction were already established; later sages followed them, and these canons became still clearer. Heaven can endow the people with their nature, but cannot make them fully realize that nature. When a sage emerges, he takes on the great responsibility of ruler and teacher and becomes the first among Heaven’s people to attain understanding. There must therefore be a Way by which he governs and instructs them. Moreover, he commits it to writing to transmit instruction to later generations. The earlier sages…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
後聖其揆一也愚請為執事陳之天命之
謂性率性之謂道性則仁義禮智信是也
道則君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友五者之大
倫是也斯民之所以羣聚而不亂者以其
全此性由此道而各有倫序焉耳聚而無
倫則亂矣傳曰一失則為夷狄再失則為
禽獸此古今聖王之治天下所以雖有百
度萬幾之多而必以敦倫為之本也舍此
而求治教之具蓋亦遠且難矣稽之於經
若堯之親睦九族舜之慎徽五典湯之肇
脩人紀武王之重民五教其所以治教當
時者蓋可見矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺天明命肇造區夏條成大誥三
編
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒御製孝順事實為善陰
騭二書
宣宗章皇帝繼志述事纘述五倫之書頒示天
下無非所以敦五倫以盡君師之責者斯
punctuated:
後聖，其揆一也。愚請為執事陳之。天命之謂性，率性之謂道。性則仁義禮智信是也，道則君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友五者之大倫是也。斯民之所以羣聚而不亂者，以其全此性、由此道，而各有倫序焉耳。聚而無倫則亂矣。傳曰：「一失則為夷狄，再失則為禽獸。」此古今聖王之治天下，所以雖有百度萬幾之多，而必以敦倫為之本也。舍此而求治教之具，蓋亦遠且難矣。稽之於經，若堯之親睦九族、舜之慎徽五典、湯之肇脩人紀、武王之重民五教，其所以治教當時者，蓋可見矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，膺天明命，肇造區夏，條成《大誥》三編。太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，御製《孝順事實》《為善陰騭》二書。宣宗章皇帝繼志述事，纘述五倫之書，頒示天下，無非所以敦五倫，以盡君師之責者。斯
translation_en:
…and the later sages followed the same standard. I venture to set this out for you, honored examiners. What Heaven ordains is called human nature; following that nature is called the Way. Human nature consists of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness. The Way consists of the five great human relationships: ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend. The people can gather together without disorder because they preserve this nature intact and follow this Way, each occupying an ordered place within these relationships. If they gather without such relationships, disorder results. A commentary says: “Once these are lost, people become barbarians; lost again, they become birds and beasts.” This is why the sage kings of ancient and recent times, in governing the realm, invariably made strengthening human relationships their foundation, despite the multitude of institutions and affairs demanding their attention. To abandon this and seek the means of government and instruction elsewhere would surely be a remote and difficult undertaking. Examining the classics, we find Yao bringing the nine degrees of kinship into affectionate harmony, Shun carefully promoting the five constant norms, Tang first putting human relationships in order, and King Wu attaching importance to the five teachings for the people. From these examples we can discern how they governed and instructed their contemporaries.
We reverently consider how our Emperor Gao of the Taizu temple name received Heaven’s illustrious mandate, founded his rule over the Chinese realm, and compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three parts. Emperor Wen of the Taizong temple name continued this great enterprise and personally composed the two books, True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Hidden Virtue (Weishan Yinzhi). Emperor Zhang of the Xuanzong temple name carried forward his predecessors’ intentions and undertakings, compiled the book on the Five Relationships, and promulgated it throughout the realm. All these works served to strengthen the five relationships and thereby fulfill the responsibilities of ruler and teacher. In this…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
世斯民家傳〻誦服至教於忘言隆盛治
於千古其與堯舜湯武之治同符合轍誠
萬世不刊之盛典也迨我
英宗睿皇帝又有大明一統誌之頒其紀名宦
人物烈女之條蓋即
三誥五書之意欲人法之以敦五倫之重愚
嘗伏讀而知其說矣
大誥所載固多垂戒之事其所以戒之者蓋
欲使人之未敦五倫者有所警懼也如婚
===
姻之條有曰五倫先王之舊章民不知報
之章有曰去五教五刑而民生者未之有
也所以五教育民之安其敦五倫之戒不
一而足也
陰騭書所載固多垂訓之事其所以訓之者
蓋欲使人之求敦五倫者有所矜式也如
載三徐成仙則言其忠君孝親同心為善
載魏顒獲報則言其從治嫁妾以成父命
之美其敦五倫之訓不可悉舉也
punctuated:
世斯民，家傳〻誦，服至教於忘言，隆盛治於千古，其與堯舜湯武之治同符合轍，誠萬世不刊之盛典也。迨我英宗睿皇帝，又有《大明一統誌》之頒，其紀名宦、人物、烈女之條，蓋即三誥五書之意，欲人法之，以敦五倫之重。愚嘗伏讀而知其說矣。
《大誥》所載，固多垂戒之事，其所以戒之者，蓋欲使人之未敦五倫者有所警懼也。如婚姻之條有曰：「五倫，先王之舊章。」民不知報之章有曰：「去五教五刑而民生者，未之有也。所以五教育民之安。」其敦五倫之戒，不一而足也。
《陰騭書》所載，固多垂訓之事，其所以訓之者，蓋欲使人之求敦五倫者有所矜式也。如載三徐成仙，則言其忠君孝親，同心為善；載魏顒獲報，則言其從治嫁妾，以成父命之美。其敦五倫之訓，不可悉舉也。
translation_en:
…in this age, among these people, these works are handed down in every household and recited by all. The people embrace the highest teachings beyond the need for words, bringing flourishing government to an eminence enduring through the ages. This accords perfectly with the government of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu: these are truly splendid canons that shall stand unaltered for ten thousand generations. In the reign of our Emperor Yingzong Rui, the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi) was also promulgated. Its entries recording distinguished officials, notable persons, and women of steadfast virtue embody the same intent as the Three Admonitions and Five Books: to have people emulate them and thereby strengthen the weighty obligations of the Five Relationships. I have humbly read these works and come to understand their meaning.
The Grand Admonition (Da gao) indeed records many cautionary events. Its warnings are intended to inspire vigilance and fear in those who have yet to fulfill the Five Relationships. For example, the section on marriage says: “The Five Relationships are the established ordinances of the former kings.” The chapter “The People Do Not Know How to Repay” says: “There has never been a case in which the people could live without the Five Teachings and Five Punishments. Thus the Five Teachings instruct the people in how to live in peace.”[?] Its admonitions to strengthen the Five Relationships are too numerous to enumerate.
The Book of Hidden Recompense (Yinzhi shu) indeed records many instructive events. Its teachings are intended to provide models for those seeking to fulfill the Five Relationships. Thus, in recording how the three Xu became immortals, it speaks of their loyalty to their ruler, filial devotion to their parents, and shared commitment to doing good. In recording how Wei Yong received recompense, it speaks of his following the instructions his father gave while of sound mind and marrying off his father’s concubine, thereby fulfilling the goodness of his father’s command. Its teachings on strengthening the Five Relationships cannot all be enumerated.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
孝順事實雖專言孝也如紀考叔遺羹而感
君閔損孝母而及弟豈有不兼於餘倫者
乎
五倫書嘉言善行固備載五倫之事而獨詳
於君臣之倫者豈非以君臣爲五倫之首
而治教之所關乎若夫
一統誌所載天下名宦人物烈女克盡五倫
之道者不可指數其在山東若大聖大賢
後先相望其道德高厚萬世景仰不可以
===
一方之人物觀者在所不必論矣姑以一
節之行有關於五倫最彰著者言之如王
祥之卧氷緹縈女之救父非敦於父子之
倫者乎廷式之娶瞽張義婦之歸夫骨非
敦於夫婦之倫者乎至如王蠋之不事二
君以盡臣節張公藝之九世同居以睦宗
族辛棄疾之往哭朱晦菴師友之義史何
如其克盡也之數人者皆有關乎五倫載
諸典籍昭昭乎最彰著者愚也幼而聞諸
punctuated:
《孝順事實》雖專言孝也，如紀考叔遺羹而感君、閔損孝母而及弟，豈有不兼於餘倫者乎？
《五倫書》嘉言善行固備載五倫之事，而獨詳於君臣之倫者，豈非以君臣爲五倫之首，而治教之所關乎？若夫《一統誌》所載天下名宦、人物、烈女，克盡五倫之道者，不可指數。其在山東，若大聖大賢，後先相望，其道德高厚，萬世景仰，不可以一方之人物觀者，在所不必論矣。姑以一節之行有關於五倫最彰著者言之，如王祥之卧氷、緹縈女之救父，非敦於父子之倫者乎？廷式之娶瞽、張義婦之歸夫骨，非敦於夫婦之倫者乎？至如王蠋之不事二君，以盡臣節；張公藝之九世同居，以睦宗族；辛棄疾之往哭朱晦菴，師友之義，史何如其克盡也！之數人者，皆有關乎五倫，載諸典籍，昭昭乎最彰著者。愚也幼而聞諸
translation_en:
Although Accounts of Filial Conduct treats filial piety specifically, it records, for example, how Kaoshu moved his ruler by saving some broth for his mother, and how Min Sun’s filial devotion to his mother also benefited his younger brothers. How could such deeds fail to embrace the other relationships as well?
The Book of the Five Relationships fully records exemplary words and good deeds concerning all five relationships. Yet it treats the relationship between ruler and minister in particular detail. Is this not because that relationship stands foremost among the five and bears upon government and moral instruction? As for the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Unified Realm, the renowned officials, notable persons, and exemplary women it records throughout the realm who fully fulfilled the Way of the five relationships are too numerous to count. In Shandong, great sages and worthies followed one another in succession. Their moral excellence was lofty and profound, admired for ten thousand generations; they cannot be regarded merely as notable persons of a single region. There is no need to discuss them here.
Let us speak instead of those most conspicuous for a particular act of virtue concerning the five relationships. Were not Wang Xiang’s lying on the ice and the maiden Tiying’s saving her father examples of devotion to the relationship between father and child? Were not Tingshi’s marrying a blind woman and the righteous woman Zhang’s bringing home her husband’s bones examples of devotion to the relationship between husband and wife? Then there was Wang Zhu, who would not serve two rulers and thus fulfilled a minister’s integrity; Zhang Gongyi, whose family lived together for nine generations, maintaining harmony among his kin; and Xin Qiji, who went to mourn Zhu Hui’an, fulfilling the obligations binding teachers and friends. How completely they fulfilled these duties! [?] These several people all exemplified the five relationships, and their deeds, recorded in the classics and other writings, are conspicuous and illustrious. From childhood, I, in my ignorance, heard of them from …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
父師之所言〻衣而考諸典籍之所載忻慕
嘆賞願學而未能者姑舉以塞明問之萬
一若夫倫擧誌中所紀又有待於能者焉
生佩服
聖訓於五倫之道不敢不勉惟執事其與進之
第二問
杜珏
同考試官教諭邵　批〔孝經小學二書乃教本之學作聖功夫未始不基於此業舉者多不之講此篇能尋其原委而〕
〔數答詳明尤於其目次第處的然有見殆士之涵養有素者乎〕
===
考試官教諭張　批〔詳采心開意歷歷有據必熟〕
〔宜爲之〕
考試官教諭李　批〔條答無遺是只□□〕
〔於□書者〕
書有關於天經地義者當考究其本原書
有裨於聖經賢傳者當發明其指趣夫孝
經一書乃人道之大端小學一書實大學
之基本是皆脩身齊家治國平天下之道
punctuated:
父師之所言〻衣，而考諸典籍之所載，忻慕嘆賞，願學而未能者，姑舉以塞明問之萬一。若夫《倫擧誌》中所紀，又有待於能者焉。生佩服聖訓，於五倫之道不敢不勉，惟執事其與進之。
第二問
杜珏
同考試官教諭邵批〔《孝經》《小學》二書，乃教本之學，作聖功夫未始不基於此。業舉者多不之講，此篇能尋其原委，而〕〔數答詳明，尤於其目次第處的然有見，殆士之涵養有素者乎？〕
考試官教諭張批〔詳采心開意，歷歷有據，必熟〕〔宜爲之。〕
考試官教諭李批〔條答無遺，是只□□〕〔於□書者。〕
書有關於天經地義者，當考究其本原；書有裨於聖經賢傳者，當發明其指趣。夫《孝經》一書，乃人道之大端；《小學》一書，實《大學》之基本。是皆脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之道
translation_en:
…what my father and teachers said [?], and checked it against the accounts in the canonical and historical writings. These are deeds I have admired and praised, wishing to emulate them but as yet unable to do so. I venture to cite them to answer even a tiny part of your discerning question. As for the accounts recorded in the Record of Exemplary Human Relationships (Lunju zhi) [?], these must await someone more capable. I, your student, reverently embrace the sage’s teachings and dare not fail to exert myself in the Way of the Five Relationships. I ask you, sir, to encourage my progress.
Second Policy Question
Du Jue
Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔The Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning are works concerned with the foundations of education; the effort to become a sage has always rested upon them. Those pursuing examination studies often neglect to study them. This essay traces their origins and development, and〕〔its several answers are detailed and clear. In particular, its treatment of the sequence of their headings shows definite insight. Surely this is a scholar who has long cultivated himself?〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Its detailed selections open up the meaning [?], and every point has supporting evidence. It must have been thoroughly〕〔and fittingly composed [?].〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The answers address every item without omission. This is [illegible]〕〔in relation to the [illegible] book [?].〕
When a book concerns the constant principles of Heaven and the proper order of Earth, one should investigate its fundamental sources; when a book contributes to understanding the sages’ classics and the worthies’ commentaries, one should elucidate its purport. The Classic of Filial Piety concerns the great essentials of the human Way; Elementary Learning is indeed the foundation of the Great Learning. These both embody the Way of cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
所寓也苟於此而不講明之則行矣不著
習矣不察終身由之而不知其道矣將何
以望古人之學哉執事以此下詢誠端本
之盛心也顧生雖愚敢不摭拾所聞以對
乎敢因明問而復之孝經之書成於曾子
門人之手而子朱子為之刋誤誠以孝之
為經乃孔曾一時問答之詞首論孝之始
終中乃敷陳天子諸侯卿大夫士庶人之
孝而末結之曰自天子至於庶人孝無終
===
始而患不及者未之有也其首尾相應文
勢連屬同是一時之言後人乃分之為六
章而又增以子曰之字加以詩書之文皆
非孝經之舊也七章以後又皆後人雜引
傳記之格言而為之傳其間戾於經意者
如釋要道非若經文自己而推之意釋以
順天下而曰先之以博愛亦非立愛惟親
之序至於釋民用和睦上下無怨其言雖
善亦非經文之正意論嚴父配天又非為
punctuated:
所寓也。苟於此而不講明之，則行矣不著，習矣不察，終身由之而不知其道矣，將何以望古人之學哉？執事以此下詢，誠端本之盛心也。顧生雖愚，敢不摭拾所聞以對乎？敢因明問而復之。

《孝經》之書成於曾子門人之手，而子朱子為之《刋誤》，誠以孝之為經，乃孔曾一時問答之詞。首論孝之始終，中乃敷陳天子、諸侯、卿、大夫、士、庶人之孝，而末結之曰：「自天子至於庶人，孝無終始而患不及者，未之有也。」其首尾相應，文勢連屬，同是一時之言。後人乃分之為六章，而又增以「子曰」之字，加以《詩》《書》之文，皆非《孝經》之舊也。七章以後，又皆後人雜引傳記之格言而為之傳。其間戾於經意者，如釋「要道」，非若經文自己而推之意；釋「以順天下」，而曰「先之以博愛」，亦非「立愛惟親」之序。至於釋「民用和睦，上下無怨」，其言雖善，亦非經文之正意。論「嚴父配天」，又非為
translation_en:
…are embodied. If one does not study and clarify these matters, one will act without understanding, grow accustomed to them without examining them, and follow them throughout life without knowing their Way. How, then, could one hope to attain the learning of the ancients? Your inquiry into these matters truly expresses a noble desire to set the foundations right. Though I, a student, am ignorant, how could I fail to gather what I have heard and offer a reply? I venture, then, to respond to your discerning question.

The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) was compiled by the disciples of Zengzi, and Master Zhu produced his Corrections of Errors for it. This was indeed because the classic’s text consists of an exchange of questions and answers between Confucius and Zengzi on a single occasion. It begins by discussing the beginning and culmination of filial piety; in the middle it expounds the filial piety of the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, ministers, grand masters, gentlemen, and common people; and it concludes: “From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, there has never been anyone who failed to carry filial piety through from beginning to end yet worried about being unable to fulfill it.” Its beginning and ending correspond, and its wording flows continuously: all are words spoken on the same occasion. Later people divided it into six chapters, inserted the words “The Master said,” and added passages from the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. None of these belonged to the original Classic of Filial Piety.

From chapter seven onward, later people likewise assembled exemplary sayings from commentaries and other records to form a commentary on the classic. Some passages contradict the classic’s meaning. For example, the explanation of “the essential Way” does not convey the classic’s sense of extending outward from oneself. In explaining “thereby bringing all under Heaven into harmony,” it says, “Lead them with universal love”; this likewise departs from the sequence expressed in “In establishing love, give primacy to one’s parents.” As for its explanation of “the people thereby live in harmony, and neither superiors nor inferiors harbor resentment,” although its words are good, they too fail to convey the proper meaning of the classic. Its discussion of “honoring one’s father by associating him with Heaven” is, moreover, not something for …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
人臣子者所取為其他所失尚多具載刋
誤難以悉舉而其書則顏註古文二十二
章孔壁所藏本也今文一十八章則河間
王所得顏芝本也閨門一章乃唐開元間
勑議纂脩之時而為司馬貞之所去司馬
貞淺見陋識去此一章論者以為卒啓玄
宗無禮無度之禍是非較然矣小學雜出
於曲禮少儀內則弟子職諸篇子朱子蒐
輯以為內篇而又述嘉言善行以為外篇
===
內篇四立教明倫敬身稽古也外篇二嘉
言善行也內前三篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之
言也後一篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之行也故
皆謂之內篇雖許魯齋以前三篇立教明
倫敬身為小學之綱領而稽古一篇正所
以為立教明倫敬身之事實故皆謂之內
篇外篇所謂嘉言乃子朱子述漢以來賢
者所言之嘉言以廣立教明倫敬身也所
謂善行乃子朱子紀漢以來賢者所行之
punctuated:
人臣子者所取為。其他所失尚多，具載《刋誤》，難以悉舉。而其書則顏註古文二十二章，孔壁所藏本也；今文一十八章，則河間王所得顏芝本也。閨門一章，乃唐開元間勑議纂脩之時，而為司馬貞之所去。司馬貞淺見陋識，去此一章，論者以為卒啓玄宗無禮無度之禍，是非較然矣。
小學雜出於曲禮、少儀、內則、弟子職諸篇，子朱子蒐輯以為內篇，而又述嘉言善行以為外篇。內篇四：立教、明倫、敬身、稽古也。外篇二：嘉言、善行也。內前三篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之言也，後一篇乃虞夏商周聖賢之行也，故皆謂之內篇。雖許魯齋以前三篇立教、明倫、敬身為小學之綱領，而稽古一篇正所以為立教、明倫、敬身之事實，故皆謂之內篇。外篇所謂嘉言，乃子朱子述漢以來賢者所言之嘉言，以廣立教、明倫、敬身也。所謂善行，乃子朱子紀漢以來賢者所行之
translation_en:
…what those serving as subjects and sons should adopt and put into practice. Its other errors are numerous; they are recorded in full in the Corrections of Errors (Kanwu) and cannot all be enumerated here. As for the text itself, the twenty-two chapters of the ancient-script version annotated by Yan constitute the text hidden in the wall of Confucius’s residence; the eighteen chapters of the modern-script version constitute Yan Zhi’s text, obtained by the Prince of Hejian. The chapter “Within the Family Gates” was removed by Sima Zhen when deliberations and compilation were undertaken by imperial command during the Kaiyuan era of the Tang. Sima Zhen, with his shallow views and limited understanding, removed this chapter; commentators considered that this ultimately opened the way to the calamity of Xuanzong’s disregard for ritual and restraint. Right and wrong are plainly evident.
The Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) draws on various chapters, including “Summary of Ritual,” “Lesser Rules of Deportment,” “Domestic Rules,” and “Duties of Disciples.” Master Zhu collected these materials to form the Inner Chapters, and further recounted admirable sayings and good deeds to form the Outer Chapters. There are four Inner Chapters: “Establishing Instruction,” “Clarifying Human Relationships,” “Reverence for the Person,” and “Examining Antiquity.” There are two Outer Chapters: “Admirable Sayings” and “Good Deeds.” The first three Inner Chapters contain the words of sages and worthies of the Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou periods; the last contains the deeds of sages and worthies of those periods. Hence all are called Inner Chapters. Although Xu Luzhai regarded the first three chapters—“Establishing Instruction,” “Clarifying Human Relationships,” and “Reverence for the Person”—as the guiding framework of the Elementary Learning, “Examining Antiquity” supplies precisely the actual instances of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and maintaining reverence for the person. Thus all are called Inner Chapters. What the Outer Chapters call “Admirable Sayings” consists of Master Zhu’s recounting of admirable sayings uttered by worthies from the Han onward, expanding upon establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and maintaining reverence for the person.
