title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
善行以實立教明倫敬身也內篇雖為嘉
言善行正古聖賢小學之支流餘裔亦若
孝經之經也外篇輯漢以来之嘉言善行
以廣以實前篇正若孝經之傳也安得無
別乎執事謂二書皆為脩身齊家治國平
天下之本皆切於學者之身故舉以為問
目盖懼學者於此二書有所忽略則所失
莫大矣愚生童而習之至今未知一言之
可用亦無怪乎執事之所甚懼者姑舉所
===
聞以復而益加勉焉
第三問　　　　　　刁嵎
同考試官訓導楊　批〔孔氏家世源委歷歷數無遺於是乎見該博之學矣〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔孔氏世系人物學者皆當究心者也場中能悉此者絶少此作考據精詳條答無遺且知上天所以〕
考試官教諭張　批〔條答詳悉他卷所無者厚報之言忠盡亦感佩聖教不忘所自者歟〕
punctuated:
善行，以實立教、明倫、敬身也。內篇雖為嘉言善行，正古聖賢小學之支流餘裔，亦若《孝經》之經也。外篇輯漢以来之嘉言善行，以廣以實前篇，正若《孝經》之傳也，安得無別乎？執事謂二書皆為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本，皆切於學者之身，故舉以為問目。盖懼學者於此二書有所忽略，則所失莫大矣。愚生童而習之，至今未知一言之可用，亦無怪乎執事之所甚懼者。姑舉所聞以復，而益加勉焉。
第三問，刁嵎。
同考試官訓導楊，批〔孔氏家世源委，歷歷數無遺，於是乎見該博之學矣。〕
同考試官教諭朱，批〔孔氏世系人物，學者皆當究心者也。場中能悉此者絶少，此作考據精詳，條答無遺，且知上天所以〕
考試官教諭張，批〔條答詳悉，他卷所無者。厚報之言忠盡，亦感佩聖教、不忘所自者歟？〕
translation_en:
…good deeds, thereby giving substance to establishing instruction, elucidating human relationships, and maintaining reverence for oneself. Although the Inner Chapters consist of admirable sayings and good deeds, they are precisely the tributaries and surviving legacy of the elementary learning of the ancient sages and worthies [?], and correspond to the canonical text of the Classic of Filial Piety. The Outer Chapters collect admirable sayings and good deeds from the Han onward to amplify and substantiate the preceding chapters, corresponding precisely to the commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety. How could there be no distinction?
You maintain that both books provide the foundation for cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven, and that both bear directly upon the learner’s own person. You have therefore made them the subject of an examination question. Presumably you fear that, should learners neglect these two books, their loss would be unsurpassed. I, an unworthy student, have studied them since childhood, yet even now I do not know how to put a single saying into practice. It is thus no wonder that you harbor such profound concern. I have ventured to set forth what I have learned in reply and shall redouble my efforts.
Third policy question. Diao Yu 刁嵎.
Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The origins and development of the Kong family’s lineage are enumerated clearly, with nothing omitted. Here we see broad and comprehensive learning.”
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The lineage and individuals of the Kong family are matters that all learners ought to investigate attentively. Extremely few in the examination hall can know these matters fully. This essay’s examination of the evidence is meticulous and detailed, and its answers address each point without omission. Moreover, it understands why Heaven…”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The answers to each point are detailed and comprehensive, as is found in no other script. The discussion of generous recompense is sincere and exhaustive. Surely its author also gratefully reveres the sage’s teaching and does not forget its source?”

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批〔孔氏家乘此作殆盡之矣〕
讀以似以續之詩則知天之衍聖嗣也爲
無窮讀報德報功之論則知天之厚聖人
也爲不偶聖人之生異矣天亦以異而待
之既厚其生也且厚其子孫也又厚其血
食於千萬世也聖人亦何以得之盖道在
聖人則功在聖人功在萬世則報在萬世
是知天之所以厚待聖人者亦報施之公
道宜然耳夫豈私厚之哉中庸曰天之生
===
物必因其材而篤焉况聖人之所以自培
植者如此其至則其得上天之厚報亦無
足恠者執事膺聘而来瞻仰道德之光忻
慕慶澤之遠感慨之意既發於中世系之
問遂形於策請以所聞見者言之先孔子
而聖者堯舜也堯之後不肖者丹朱孰如
鯉也詩禮之傳舜之後不肖者商均孰如
伋也性命之闡賢哉子孫豈無所自盖孔
子之先實由微子封於宋始於微仲衍自
punctuated:
考試官教諭李，批〔孔氏家乘，此作殆盡之矣。〕

讀「以似以續」之詩，則知天之衍聖嗣也爲無窮；讀報德報功之論，則知天之厚聖人也爲不偶。聖人之生異矣，天亦以異而待之：既厚其生也，且厚其子孫也，又厚其血食於千萬世也。聖人亦何以得之？盖道在聖人，則功在聖人；功在萬世，則報在萬世。是知天之所以厚待聖人者，亦報施之公道宜然耳，夫豈私厚之哉？中庸曰：「天之生物，必因其材而篤焉。」况聖人之所以自培植者如此其至，則其得上天之厚報亦無足恠者。執事膺聘而来，瞻仰道德之光，忻慕慶澤之遠，感慨之意既發於中，世系之問遂形於策。請以所聞見者言之。先孔子而聖者，堯舜也。堯之後不肖者丹朱，孰如鯉也詩禮之傳？舜之後不肖者商均，孰如伋也性命之闡？賢哉子孫，豈無所自？盖孔子之先，實由微子封於宋，始於微仲衍，自
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔This essay covers almost the whole of the Kong family genealogy.〕

Reading the verse “to carry on and to continue,” one knows that Heaven perpetuates the sage’s descendants without end; reading the discussion of recompensing virtue and merit, one knows that Heaven’s generous treatment of the sage is no accident. The sage’s birth was extraordinary, and Heaven likewise treated him extraordinarily: it bestowed generous blessings upon his life, upon his descendants, and upon the sacrificial offerings made to him through countless generations. How did the sage obtain all this? Since the Way resides in the sage, the merit belongs to the sage; since that merit extends through all generations, its recompense likewise extends through all generations. Thus we know that Heaven’s generous treatment of the sage is simply what the impartial principle of recompense requires. How could it be a matter of partial favor? The Doctrine of the Mean says: “When Heaven produces things, it necessarily enriches them according to their capacities.” Moreover, since the sage’s cultivation of himself was so consummate, there is nothing surprising in his receiving Heaven’s abundant recompense.

You, honored examiners, have come in response to your appointments. Gazing reverently upon the radiance of his Way and virtue, and admiring the enduring reach of his blessings, you were moved inwardly and accordingly framed a policy question about his lineage. Allow me to speak of what I have heard and seen. The sages who preceded Kongzi were Yao and Shun. Yao’s unworthy descendant was Danzhu: how could he compare with Kong Li, who received the teachings of the Odes and the rites? Shun’s unworthy descendant was Shang Jun: how could he compare with Kong Ji, who elucidated human nature and Heaven’s mandate? Worthy indeed were these descendants! Could their worthiness have been without a source? The ancestry of Kongzi in fact derives from Weizi’s enfeoffment in Song, with the line beginning with Weizhong Yan; from …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
衍而歷稽也中也共也弗父何也宋父周
也自周而歷世父勝也正考父也孔父嘉
也木金父也睾夷父也睾夷生防叔防叔
生伯夏伯夏者叔梁紇所從出也叔梁紇
者即孔子所由生也其生也有自來其聖
也有所為雖曰間氣而生是亦本原厚積
之發也而孔子又從而培植之本益固矣
而末之茂也豈期然而然哉故自伋之後
名白者則相於齊名順者則相於魏名鮒
===
者則博士於秦戰國時之顯者也博極羣
書而還大將軍者曰延年授太子經而拜
太師者曰孔霸好學有大才而襲封關內
侯者曰孔均漢時之著者也孔鮮始為奉
聖亭侯宋文帝改封崇聖侯崇有尊尚之
義進於奉也審矣非進侯者之秩也無非
褒加聖人也孔渠始為恭聖侯隋煬帝改
封嗣哲紹聖侯紹有纘緒之意加於恭也
明矣非加侯者之爵也亦無非追隆聖人
punctuated: 衍而歷稽也、中也、共也、弗父何也、宋父周也，自周而歷世父勝也、正考父也、孔父嘉也、木金父也、睾夷父也。睾夷生防叔，防叔生伯夏，伯夏者叔梁紇所從出也。叔梁紇者，即孔子所由生也。其生也有自來，其聖也有所為。雖曰間氣而生，是亦本原厚積之發也。而孔子又從而培植之，本益固矣，而末之茂也，豈期然而然哉？故自伋之後，名白者則相於齊，名順者則相於魏，名鮒者則博士於秦，戰國時之顯者也。博極羣書而還大將軍者曰延年，授太子經而拜太師者曰孔霸，好學有大才而襲封關內侯者曰孔均，漢時之著者也。孔鮮始為奉聖亭侯，宋文帝改封崇聖侯。崇有尊尚之義，進於奉也審矣，非進侯者之秩也，無非褒加聖人也。孔渠始為恭聖侯，隋煬帝改封嗣哲紹聖侯。紹有纘緒之意，加於恭也明矣，非加侯者之爵也，亦無非追隆聖人
translation_en:
…Yan, through Ji, Zhong, Gong, Fufu He, and Songfu Zhou; from Zhou, the succession continued through Shifu Sheng, Zhengkaofu, Kongfu Jia, Mu Jinfu [?], and Gaoyifu. Gaoyi begot Fangshu, Fangshu begot Boxia, and Boxia was the father of Shuliang He. Shuliang He, in turn, was the father of Confucius. His birth thus had its ancestral source, and his sagehood had its foundations. Although he is said to have been born from the rare, exceptional vital force of Heaven and Earth, this too was the flowering of virtue richly accumulated at its source. Confucius further nurtured it, making the roots still firmer. Could the flourishing of its branches have come about through deliberate expectation? Thus, among the descendants after Ji, the one named Bai served as chief minister in Qi, the one named Shun as chief minister in Wei, and the one named Fu as an Erudite in Qin. These were the eminent figures of the Warring States period. The one who mastered the full range of books and returned as Grand General [?] was Yannian; the one who taught the classics to the heir apparent and was appointed Grand Preceptor was Kong Ba; and the one who loved learning, possessed great ability, and inherited the title of Marquis Within the Passes was Kong Jun. These were the distinguished figures of the Han.

Kong Xian was initially Hamlet Marquis for Serving the Sage. Emperor Wen of the Song changed his title to Marquis for Exalting the Sage. ‘Exalting’ conveys reverence and esteem: it clearly goes beyond ‘serving.’ This was not an advancement in the marquis’s official rank; it was wholly intended to confer greater praise upon the Sage. Kong Qu was initially Marquis for Revering the Sage. Emperor Yang of the Sui changed his title to Marquis for Succeeding the Wise and Continuing the Sage. ‘Continuing’ conveys carrying on the inherited tradition: it plainly adds something to ‘revering.’ This was not an increase in the marquis’s noble rank; it likewise served solely to honor the Sage retrospectively…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也他如仕唐者則對策高第其孔昌寓乎
狀元及第其孔振乎明經及第其孔緩乎
一時文盛雖不敢追配先烈刪述之文是
亦奉先烈之遺矩者仕宋者則以剛毅直
諒名其道輔也以操行介潔稱其孔傳也
以介潔不阿許其孔端也一時高節雖不
敢竊擬先聖時中之行是亦守先聖之家
法者嗚呼鴻儒碩學大爵高官肩摩踵接
未易枚舉今之所陳者特如所聞耳且往
古來今享王祀於無窮爇衍聖於無替愈
遠益昌誠非筆舌之所易紀追視堯舜之
後何寥寥無一可聞者耶蓋又有說也堯
舜有聖人之德得聖人之位盛極當時若
孔子有堯舜之德不得堯舜之位天之負
於前者正所以償之於後也況崇德報功
固在人所當盡又在天所不爽此其所以
歷千百世而人物迭興無有紀極也耶愚
也忝生是邦聖人之學固不敢洋望其一
punctuated:
也。他如仕唐者，則對策高第，其孔昌寓乎？狀元及第，其孔振乎？明經及第，其孔緩乎？一時文盛，雖不敢追配先烈刪述之文，是亦奉先烈之遺矩者。仕宋者，則以剛毅直諒名，其道輔也；以操行介潔稱，其孔傳也；以介潔不阿許，其孔端也。一時高節，雖不敢竊擬先聖時中之行，是亦守先聖之家法者。嗚呼！鴻儒碩學，大爵高官，肩摩踵接，未易枚舉。今之所陳者，特如所聞耳。
且往古來今，享王祀於無窮，爇衍聖於無替，愈遠益昌，誠非筆舌之所易紀。追視堯舜之後，何寥寥無一可聞者耶？蓋又有說也。堯舜有聖人之德，得聖人之位，盛極當時。若孔子，有堯舜之德，不得堯舜之位，天之負於前者，正所以償之於後也。況崇德報功，固在人所當盡，又在天所不爽，此其所以歷千百世而人物迭興，無有紀極也耶？
愚也忝生是邦，聖人之學，固不敢洋望其一
translation_en:
…As for others who served under the Tang: was it not Kong Changyu who attained a high grade in answering policy questions? Was it not Kong Zhen who passed as the first-ranked candidate? Was it not Kong Huan who passed the examination in elucidating the classics? Though the literary achievements that flourished in their day cannot presume to match their illustrious ancestor’s work of editing and transmitting the classics, these men nevertheless upheld the standards he bequeathed. Among those who served under the Song, it was Kong Daofu who was renowned for firmness, resolution, forthrightness, and trustworthiness; Kong Chuan who was praised for upright and unsullied conduct; and Kong Duan who was esteemed for integrity and refusal to yield to others. Though their lofty principles cannot presume to equal the former Sage’s conduct, which accorded with the Mean as circumstances required, these men nevertheless preserved his family’s teachings. Ah! Great Confucian scholars and men of profound learning, holders of exalted noble ranks and high offices, followed so closely upon one another that they cannot readily be enumerated. What I have set forth here is merely what I have heard.
Moreover, from antiquity to the present, the Sage has received sacrifices befitting a king without end, and the title of Duke for Fulfilling the Sage has continued without interruption [?]. The more distant the beginnings, the greater the flourishing: truly, neither pen nor tongue can readily record it. Looking back at the descendants of Yao and Shun, why are they so obscure that not a single one is heard of? There is an explanation for this too. Yao and Shun possessed the virtue of sages and obtained the positions of sages, attaining the height of glory in their own time. Confucius, however, possessed the virtue of Yao and Shun but did not obtain their positions. What Heaven withheld from him earlier was precisely what it would compensate for later. Furthermore, honoring virtue and requiting achievement are duties that people must fully discharge, and matters in which Heaven does not err. Is this why, through hundreds and thousands of generations, outstanding men have arisen one after another, without limit?
Unworthy though I am, I have had the privilege of being born in this land. As for the Sage’s learning, I certainly dare not aspire to even a fraction of it [?]…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
二然聖人遺蹟之陳世家之盛蓋得濡於
耳染於目也古人云觀羹墻則思堯觀河
洛則思禹今目聖人之墓於泗上瞻聖人
之廟於闕里獨無所思乎然思之要在學
之何如耳孟子曰乃所願則學孔子也愚
竊游歌於鄒魯之間敢不以此自勵
王崇獻
第四問
同考試官訓導李　批〔能即其人而論其得失見識〕
===
〔制之學非徒取其記問之長而已也〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔場中卷此策者多得以失紋求其事核文整如此篇者蓋有數也〕
考試官教諭張　批〔論人物得失鑿鑿有見有學有識之士也〕
考試官教諭李　批〔策眷眷所問〕
明於知人斯可立論以方人明於知已斯
可舉人以况已夫方人非難而明於知人
為難况已非難而明於知已為難苟無知
punctuated:
二。然聖人遺蹟之陳、世家之盛，蓋得濡於耳、染於目也。古人云：「觀羹墻則思堯，觀河洛則思禹。」今目聖人之墓於泗上，瞻聖人之廟於闕里，獨無所思乎？然思之要，在學之何如耳。孟子曰：「乃所願，則學孔子也。」愚竊游歌於鄒魯之間，敢不以此自勵？

王崇獻

第四問

同考試官訓導李，批〔能即其人而論其得失，見識〕〔制之學，非徒取其記問之長而已也。〕

同考試官教諭王，批〔場中卷此策者，多得以失紋，求其事核文整如此篇者，蓋有數也。〕

考試官教諭張，批〔論人物得失，鑿鑿有見，有學有識之士也。〕

考試官教諭李，批〔策眷眷所問。〕

明於知人，斯可立論以方人；明於知已，斯可舉人以况已。夫方人非難，而明於知人為難；况已非難，而明於知已為難。苟無知
translation_en:
…even a little of it. Yet the surviving traces of the Sage, arrayed before us, and the flourishing of his hereditary house have surely reached my ears and met my eyes. An ancient saying runs: “Looking upon broth and walls, one thinks of Yao; looking upon the He and Luo rivers, one thinks of Yu.” Now, seeing the Sage’s tomb beside the Si River and gazing upon his temple at Queli, could one alone have no thoughts of him? Yet the essential point in thinking of him lies in how one learns from him. Mencius said: “As for what I wish, it is to learn from Confucius.” Living and singing among Zou and Lu, how could I dare not encourage myself with these words?

Wang Chongxian

Fourth Question

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He can discuss the merits and failings of the individuals themselves, showing discernment…〕〔…learning concerning institutions [?]; we do not merely prize his proficiency in memorization and recitation.〕

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Among the examination papers answering this policy question, many “gain through losing the pattern” [?]. Those whose treatment of the facts is sound and whose writing is orderly, like this essay, are surely few.〕

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔His discussion of the merits and failings of historical figures is precise and insightful. He is a man of learning and discernment.〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay attends closely to what was asked.〕

Only with clear understanding of others can one formulate judgments to compare people; only with clear understanding of oneself can one cite others to compare oneself with them. Comparing people is not difficult; what is difficult is understanding them clearly. Comparing oneself with others is not difficult; what is difficult is understanding oneself clearly. If one lacks understanding…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
己知人之明則是非混淆於鑑別之中邪
正倒置於權衡之下差之毫釐繆以千里
而欲方人況己也不亦難哉請因明問而
陳其一二諸葛孔明之在蜀也膺三聘之
勤受付托之重出師二表忠貫日星八陣
一圖光昭海宇爰考其人乃伊呂之儔耳
自比管樂蓋其謙詞賈似道之在宋也以
嫉妬之心秉鈞軸之任專權蠹政大失民
心積釁稔禍終亡宋祚爰考其人蓋杞檜
===
之雄也自託伊周乃其誇誕恢廓大度才
明勇畧克復舊物於羣雄草竊之餘先訪
儒雅於天下甫定之際光武真中興之主
也石勒以為韓彭之流豈知光武者哉出
守雲中牢制閫外不私軍市之租遠遁匈
奴之騎魏尚真名世之将也馮唐以為頗
牧之屬其知魏尚者歟澶淵摧敵北門禦
寇丞相準之忠端可方唐之魏公徵也碩
德重望之王旦豈與馮道伍哉雖然美珠
punctuated: 己知人之明，則是非混淆於鑑別之中，邪正倒置於權衡之下，差之毫釐，繆以千里，而欲方人況己也，不亦難哉？請因明問而陳其一二。諸葛孔明之在蜀也，膺三聘之勤，受付托之重，出師二表，忠貫日星；八陣一圖，光昭海宇。爰考其人，乃伊呂之儔耳。自比管樂，蓋其謙詞。賈似道之在宋也，以嫉妬之心，秉鈞軸之任，專權蠹政，大失民心，積釁稔禍，終亡宋祚。爰考其人，蓋杞檜之雄也。自託伊周，乃其誇誕。恢廓大度，才明勇畧，克復舊物於羣雄草竊之餘，先訪儒雅於天下甫定之際，光武真中興之主也。石勒以為韓彭之流，豈知光武者哉？出守雲中，牢制閫外，不私軍市之租，遠遁匈奴之騎，魏尚真名世之将也。馮唐以為頗牧之屬，其知魏尚者歟？澶淵摧敵，北門禦寇，丞相準之忠，端可方唐之魏公徵也。碩德重望之王旦，豈與馮道伍哉？雖然，美珠
translation_en:
…without clarity in knowing oneself and others, right and wrong become confused in one's discrimination, and the wicked and upright trade places in one's judgment. An error of a hair's breadth leads to a discrepancy of a thousand li. Would it not then be difficult to compare others or liken oneself to them? Allow me to address one or two examples in response to your discerning question.

When Zhuge Kongming served in Shu, he received the earnest solicitation of three visits and accepted the weighty responsibility entrusted to him. In his two memorials on dispatching the army, his loyalty reached the sun and stars; through his diagram of the Eight Formations, his brilliance shone throughout the realm. On examining the man, we find him a peer of Yi Yin and Lü Shang. His comparison of himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi was surely an expression of modesty. When Jia Sidao served the Song, he held the reins of government with a jealous heart. Monopolizing power and corrupting government, he utterly alienated the people. His accumulated offenses brought calamity to fruition and ultimately ended the Song's dynastic rule. On examining the man, we find him an outstanding member of the company of Lu Qi and Qin Hui. His claim to rank with Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou was boastful exaggeration.

Magnanimous and generous, gifted, discerning, courageous, and resourceful, Guangwu recovered his dynasty's former possessions after the depredations of contending warlords, and made seeking out learned scholars a priority as soon as the realm was settled. He was truly a ruler who restored his dynasty. Shi Le considered him of the same order as Han Xin and Peng Yue: did he understand Guangwu? Appointed to govern Yunzhong, Wei Shang maintained firm control over his frontier command, did not appropriate the army market's tax revenues for himself, and drove the Xiongnu cavalry far away. He was truly a general renowned in his age. Feng Tang considered him of the same company as Lian Po and Li Mu: surely he understood Wei Shang?

Crushing the enemy at Chanyuan and defending the northern gateway against invaders, Grand Councilor Kou Zhun displayed a loyalty that could indeed be compared with that of Wei Zheng, Duke of Wei under the Tang. Could Wang Dan, a man of great virtue and high prestige, be ranked alongside Feng Dao? Nevertheless, the fine pearls…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
受遺亦畧相似東攻張步北收上谷將軍
弇之勇端可擬漢之韓信也捫虱高談之
王猛夫豈孔明匹哉雖然魚水得君亦畧
相若好賢納諫尚文抑武金世宗賢則賢
矣贊爲堯舜或不免於過情神謨睿筭濟
世安民唐太宗賢則賢矣自況文宣或不
免於慚德宇量弘澗明達好謀武帝乃晉
之英君劉毅方於桓靈亦箴規之詞耳勵
精求治去奢從儉文宗乃唐之誼辟自以
===
赧獻爲愧亦鬱抑之懷耳深潛純粹具體
聖人顔子孔門大賢也黄憲何人荀淑亦
以顔子目之然汪汪德量澄不清而淆不
濁憲亦一時高士也運籌帷幄决勝千里
子房漢廷人傑也荀彧何人曹操亦以子
房稱之然表表才華擢賢能而詰軍旅彧
亦一代偉人也夫荷氊披毳者不足以語
綿絲之美咀藜含糗者不足以語牢醴之
佳低昂人物評品古今上智之事也是非
punctuated: 受遺亦畧相似。東攻張步，北收上谷，將軍弇之勇，端可擬漢之韓信也。捫虱高談之王猛，夫豈孔明匹哉？雖然，魚水得君，亦畧相若。好賢納諫，尚文抑武，金世宗賢則賢矣，贊爲堯舜，或不免於過情。神謨睿筭，濟世安民，唐太宗賢則賢矣，自況文宣，或不免於慚德。宇量弘澗，明達好謀，武帝乃晉之英君，劉毅方於桓靈，亦箴規之詞耳。勵精求治，去奢從儉，文宗乃唐之誼辟，自以赧獻爲愧，亦鬱抑之懷耳。深潛純粹，具體聖人，顔子孔門大賢也。黄憲何人，荀淑亦以顔子目之？然汪汪德量，澄不清而淆不濁，憲亦一時高士也。運籌帷幄，决勝千里，子房漢廷人傑也。荀彧何人，曹操亦以子房稱之？然表表才華，擢賢能而詰軍旅，彧亦一代偉人也。夫荷氊披毳者，不足以語綿絲之美；咀藜含糗者，不足以語牢醴之佳。低昂人物，評品古今，上智之事也。是非
translation_en:
…in accepting gifts, too, there was some resemblance. Attacking Zhang Bu in the east and securing Shanggu in the north, General Geng Yan displayed courage that could indeed be compared with that of Han Xin of the Han. But could Wang Meng, who discoursed loftily while picking lice, possibly equal Kongming? Even so, in finding a ruler with whom he enjoyed the affinity of fish and water, he was somewhat similar.

Honoring worthy men and accepting remonstrance, esteeming civil pursuits and restraining military ones, Emperor Shizong of the Jin was certainly worthy; yet praising him as a Yao or Shun perhaps exceeded the truth. With inspired plans and sagacious calculations, aiding the world and bringing peace to the people, Emperor Taizong of the Tang was certainly worthy; yet in comparing himself with Emperors Wen and Xuan of the Han, he perhaps had moral shortcomings of which to be ashamed. Broad in bearing and capacity [?], perceptive and fond of deliberation, Emperor Wu was an outstanding ruler of the Jin. Liu Yi’s comparison of him with Emperors Huan and Ling was merely an admonition. Applying himself earnestly to good government, abandoning extravagance and embracing frugality, Emperor Wenzong was a righteous sovereign of the Tang. His sense of shame at comparing himself with King Nan of Zhou and Emperor Xian of Han merely expressed his pent-up frustration.

Profound, reserved, and pure, embodying the essential qualities of a sage, Master Yan was a great worthy of Confucius’s school. Who was Huang Xian, that Xun Shu should likewise regard him as a Master Yan? Yet his virtue and capacity were like a vast expanse of water, which grew no clearer when allowed to settle and no murkier when stirred: Xian, too, was an eminent scholar of his time. Devising strategies within the command tent and determining victory a thousand li away, Zifang was an outstanding man of the Han court. Who was Xun Yu, that Cao Cao should likewise call him a Zifang? Yet, conspicuous in talent, promoting the worthy and capable and putting military affairs in order, Yu, too, was a great man of his age.

Those who wear felt and coarse wool cannot adequately discuss the beauty of silk floss and silk; those who chew goosefoot greens and eat parched grain cannot adequately discuss the excellence of sacrificial meats and sweet wine. Ranking people and assessing figures past and present are tasks for the highest wisdom. Right and wrong…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也典籍之記載取之耳目之見聞亦取之
朝堂之議取之芻蕘之言亦取之合衆論
之公斷一己之獨則天下無遺策矣胼胝
之勞不憂盤错之交不亂萬變之應不窮
千夫之撼不動左右逢原整暇有序則天
下無遺才矣何大事之不可謀大功之不
可成耶請因明問以對古者九州之域不
出中原江南嶺表皆爲裔服江淛之地唐
虞何有焉封建之制王畿千里貢賦之来
===
不過五百里侯國百里貢賦之来不過五
十里漕運之法禹貢何録焉下至春秋吴
於邗溝築城始穿城壕之水東北通射陽
湖西北至末口入淮以通粮道此漕運之
權輿也於民何病至秦始皇代匈奴飛芻
輓粟起於琅邪負海之郡轉輸河北率三
十鍾而致一石此漕運之桎梏也於民奚
堪漢之初年京師之需仰給近郡諸侯之
粟不歸天子當時關東之漕僅數十萬石
punctuated:
也。典籍之記載取之，耳目之見聞亦取之；朝堂之議取之，芻蕘之言亦取之。合衆論之公，斷一己之獨，則天下無遺策矣。胼胝之勞不憂，盤错之交不亂，萬變之應不窮，千夫之撼不動，左右逢原，整暇有序，則天下無遺才矣。何大事之不可謀，大功之不可成耶？請因明問以對。

古者九州之域不出中原，江南、嶺表皆爲裔服，江淛之地，唐虞何有焉？封建之制，王畿千里，貢賦之来不過五百里；侯國百里，貢賦之来不過五十里。漕運之法，《禹貢》何録焉？下至春秋，吴於邗溝築城，始穿城壕之水，東北通射陽湖，西北至末口入淮，以通粮道，此漕運之權輿也，於民何病？至秦始皇代匈奴，飛芻輓粟，起於琅邪負海之郡，轉輸河北，率三十鍾而致一石，此漕運之桎梏也，於民奚堪？漢之初年，京師之需仰給近郡，諸侯之粟不歸天子，當時關東之漕僅數十萬石
translation_en:
… Draw upon what is recorded in the classical writings, and also upon what the eyes and ears have witnessed and heard; draw upon deliberations at court, and also upon the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers. Bring together the impartial judgments of the many and put an end to the arbitrary judgment of oneself alone: then no useful policy in the realm will be overlooked. Be undaunted by toil that raises calluses, unconfused by tangled difficulties, inexhaustible in responding to myriad changes, and unmoved by the efforts of a thousand men to shake you. Find resources on every side, remaining composed, unhurried, and orderly: then no talent in the realm will go unused. What great undertaking could not be planned, what great achievement could not be accomplished? Permit me to reply in accordance with your illuminating question.

In antiquity, the territory of the Nine Provinces did not extend beyond the Central Plain. Jiangnan and Lingbiao were both outlying domains. What possession did Tang and Yu have of the lands of Jiang-Zhe? Under the system of enfeoffment, the royal domain measured a thousand li across, and tribute and taxes came from no farther than five hundred li away; a lord’s state measured a hundred li across, and tribute and taxes came from no farther than fifty li away. What system of grain transport by water does the Tribute of Yu record? Coming down to the Spring and Autumn period, Wu built a city at Hangou and first opened a waterway from its moat, connecting northeastward with Sheyang Lake and northwestward with Mokou, where it entered the Huai River, to open a route for transporting grain. This was the beginning of grain transport by water. What hardship did it impose on the people? When the First Emperor of Qin attacked [?] the Xiongnu, fodder was rushed forward and grain hauled from Langya and other coastal commanderies, relayed to the region north of the Yellow River. As a rule, thirty zhong were expended to deliver one shi. These were the shackles of grain transport: how could the people bear them? In the early years of the Han, the capital’s needs were supplied by nearby commanderies, while the grain of the feudal lords did not go to the Son of Heaven. At that time, grain transported by water from Guandong amounted to only several hundred thousand shi…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而巳武帝時從河東守番系之請山東益
漕至百餘萬石繼而奴婢之沒禽獸之養
糜費無經遂益爲四百萬石又繼而北伐
匈奴西通月氐神仙土木纍纍相繼又增
爲六百萬石嗚呼漢武之末去秦寧幾何
耶雖然漢之財賦仰於山東唐之財賦則
仰於江淮德宗之時韓滉轉運江淮之米
未至六軍脫巾於道及其旣至則喜謂太
子曰吾父子得生矣遂置酒相慶憂喜死
===
生如在目前唐人倚辦之急可知矣代宗
之時劉晏領漕江南之運積揚州汴河之
運積河陰河船積渭口渭船入太倉泝河
入渭隨處停貯唐人講畫之詳可見矣宋
有閘口之制十月則舟楫不行所以節民
力也王安石欲通冬運則以船艘數十設
碓擣氷役夫苦寒死者甚衆漕法其一變
也宋有轉般之法江不入汴汴不入江所
以習水勢也曾孝緒爲緐代發運令六路
punctuated:
而巳。武帝時，從河東守番系之請，山東益漕至百餘萬石。繼而奴婢之沒、禽獸之養，糜費無經，遂益爲四百萬石。又繼而北伐匈奴，西通月氐，神仙土木，纍纍相繼，又增爲六百萬石。嗚呼！漢武之末，去秦寧幾何耶？

雖然，漢之財賦仰於山東，唐之財賦則仰於江淮。德宗之時，韓滉轉運江淮之米未至，六軍脫巾於道；及其旣至，則喜謂太子曰：「吾父子得生矣！」遂置酒相慶。憂喜死生，如在目前，唐人倚辦之急可知矣。代宗之時，劉晏領漕，江南之運積揚州，汴河之運積河陰，河船積渭口，渭船入太倉。泝河入渭，隨處停貯，唐人講畫之詳可見矣。

宋有閘口之制，十月則舟楫不行，所以節民力也。王安石欲通冬運，則以船艘數十設碓擣氷，役夫苦寒，死者甚衆，漕法其一變也。宋有轉般之法，江不入汴，汴不入江，所以習水勢也。曾孝緒爲緐代發運，令六路
translation_en:
…and no more. Under Emperor Wu, following the request of Fan Xi, Governor of Hedong, grain shipments from Shandong were increased to more than one million shi. Subsequently, the confiscation of male and female slaves and the keeping of birds and beasts entailed unrestrained expenditure, and shipments were increased to four million shi. Then came northern campaigns against the Xiongnu, the opening of communications westward with the Yuezhi, and undertakings involving immortals and building works, following one upon another; shipments were again increased, to six million shi. Alas! By the end of Emperor Wu’s reign, how far was the Han from the Qin?

Nevertheless, the Han depended on Shandong for its fiscal revenues, whereas the Tang depended on the Jiang and Huai regions. Under Emperor Dezong, when the rice Han Huang was transporting from those regions had not yet arrived, soldiers of the Six Armies took off their headcloths in the roads. Once it arrived, the emperor joyfully told the heir apparent: “We, father and son, can now survive!” He then had wine served in celebration. Anxiety and joy, death and life, seemed immediately before their eyes: this shows how urgently the Tang depended on the delivery of these supplies. Under Emperor Daizong, Liu Yan directed grain transport. Shipments from Jiangnan were stockpiled at Yangzhou; shipments along the Bian River were stockpiled at Heyin; Yellow River vessels deposited their cargoes at the mouth of the Wei River; and Wei River vessels entered the Court of the Imperial Granaries. On the upstream journey along the Yellow River and into the Wei, cargoes were halted and stored at successive points. This shows the thoroughness of Tang planning.

The Song had a system governing sluice gates: in the tenth month, boats ceased operating, in order to conserve the people’s labor. Wang Anshi wished to keep transport running through the winter, so he fitted several dozen vessels with pestles to pound the ice. The laborers suffered bitter cold, and very many died. This was one change in the grain-transport system. The Song also had a system of relay transshipment: Yangzi vessels did not enter the Bian, and Bian vessels did not enter the Yangzi, so that crews could work in waters whose conditions they knew. Zeng Xiaoxu, serving as Transport Commissioner [the wording 爲緐代發運 is unclear], ordered the six circuits …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
郡縣各總歲額雖湖南至遠之地亦直抵
京師漕法又一變也元都燕京注意河防
者有二初以伯顏之議造平底海船運糧
京師而韓仲暉等復言自安山開河北至
臨清凡二百五十餘里引汶絕濟直屬衛
漳度地高低建閘蓄洩名曰會通河以代
海運民甚便之我
太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵天下財賦悉趨南都北
運不興而會通河遂淤繼以郭守敬之議
===
鑿通州至大都為河引昌平白浮村一畝
玉泉之水注之設閘啓閉名曰通惠河運
舟自直沽而来者得以徑到大都民亦便
之尋以地高水淺隨脩隨罷
國朝因之興廢如故夫通州切近京師通惠
之河不講可也會通之河廼
國家糧運之咽喉講之容可緩乎我
太宗文皇帝都北之初遂脩是河復元之舊至
十三年海運始罷然是河之水發源於泰
punctuated: 郡縣各總歲額，雖湖南至遠之地，亦直抵京師，漕法又一變也。元都燕京，注意河防者有二：初以伯顏之議，造平底海船運糧京師，而韓仲暉等復言，自安山開河北至臨清，凡二百五十餘里，引汶絕濟，直屬衛漳，度地高低，建閘蓄洩，名曰會通河，以代海運，民甚便之。我太祖高皇帝定鼎金陵，天下財賦悉趨南都，北運不興，而會通河遂淤。繼以郭守敬之議，鑿通州至大都為河，引昌平白浮村一畝玉泉之水注之，設閘啓閉，名曰通惠河。運舟自直沽而来者，得以徑到大都，民亦便之。尋以地高水淺，隨脩隨罷。國朝因之，興廢如故。夫通州切近京師，通惠之河不講可也；會通之河，廼國家糧運之咽喉，講之容可緩乎？我太宗文皇帝都北之初，遂脩是河，復元之舊。至十三年，海運始罷。然是河之水，發源於泰
translation_en:
…each prefecture and county to take responsibility for its full annual quota; even shipments from places as distant as Hunan went directly to the capital. This was another change in the grain-transport system.

The Yuan established their capital at Yanjing. There were two major undertakings concerning river management. First, following Bayan’s proposal, flat-bottomed seagoing vessels were built to carry grain to the capital. Han Zhonghui and others then proposed cutting a canal northward from Anshan to Linqing, a distance of more than 250 li, drawing in the Wen River, crossing the Ji River, and connecting directly with the Wei and Zhang rivers. Taking account of differences in elevation, they built sluices to retain and release water. This was named the Huitong Canal and was intended to replace sea transport. The people found it very advantageous.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao established his capital at Jinling. The empire’s revenues all flowed toward the southern capital, transport northward was not undertaken, and the Huitong Canal consequently silted up. Subsequently, following Guo Shoujing’s proposal [the chronology here is doubtful], a canal was excavated from Tongzhou to Dadu. Water from Baifu village in Changping and from Yimu and Yuquan [?] was diverted into it, and sluices were installed to regulate its flow. It was named the Tonghui Canal. Transport vessels arriving from Zhigu could proceed directly to Dadu, which the people likewise found advantageous. Before long, however, because the ground was high and the water shallow, repairs were repeatedly followed by abandonment. Our dynasty inherited this situation, and the same cycle of restoration and disuse continued.

Now Tongzhou is very close to the capital, so it might be permissible to leave the Tonghui Canal out of consideration. But the Huitong Canal is the vital passage for the state’s grain transport: can deliberation over it possibly be delayed? When our Emperor Taizong Wen first established his capital in the north, he repaired this canal, restoring its former Yuan condition. Only in the thirteenth year was sea transport discontinued. Yet the water of this canal has its source at Mount Tai…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山徂徠諸澗合流於汶泗洸濟諸河自濟
以南則合淮泗自濟以北則屬衛漳初與
黃河不相統也爲其不通黃河故水源淺
薄淫雨則溪澗漫溢旱乾則水脉微細運
舟通塞仰望天時近者黃陵岡一決於河
南而安平鎮口遂傾於東海幸而黃河源
深勢猛傾海之外餘波尚在故運舟經口
雖未免於費力而離口上下則自在乎中
流是害我漕運此黃河也利我漕運亦此
===
黃河也彼黃陵岡不塞則安平鎮口不得
收功固確論也舍安平鎮口而倡爲海運
之說固疎謀也以故二三年之間重㢤
聖慮疊遣重臣今黃陵岡已免奔決而安平鎮
口亦無傾注其功豈不偉歟但恐旱暵之
餘閘河乾淺視昔尤甚運舟之行比昔尤
難明問及此可謂遠慮生之謬論則曰以
兩口未塞之先論之當於安山以北去處
通海隄岸多作減水壩以殺黃陵岡之奔
punctuated:
山、徂徠諸澗，合流於汶、泗、洸、濟諸河。自濟以南，則合淮、泗；自濟以北，則屬衛、漳，初與黃河不相統也。爲其不通黃河，故水源淺薄，淫雨則溪澗漫溢，旱乾則水脉微細，運舟通塞，仰望天時。近者黃陵岡一決於河南，而安平鎮口遂傾於東海。幸而黃河源深勢猛，傾海之外，餘波尚在，故運舟經口，雖未免於費力，而離口上下，則自在乎中流。是害我漕運，此黃河也；利我漕運，亦此黃河也。彼黃陵岡不塞，則安平鎮口不得收功，固確論也。舍安平鎮口而倡爲海運之說，固疎謀也。以故二三年之間，重㢤聖慮，疊遣重臣。今黃陵岡已免奔決，而安平鎮口亦無傾注，其功豈不偉歟？但恐旱暵之餘，閘河乾淺，視昔尤甚；運舟之行，比昔尤難。明問及此，可謂遠慮。
生之謬論則曰：以兩口未塞之先論之，當於安山以北去處，通海隄岸，多作減水壩，以殺黃陵岡之奔
translation_en:
…the ravines of Mount Tai and Mount Culai, whose waters converge in the Wen, Si, Guang, and Ji rivers. South of Ji, the waters join the Huai and Si; north of Ji, they connect with the Wei and Zhang. Originally, they did not form a connected system with the Yellow River. Because there was no connection with the Yellow River, the water supply was meager: prolonged rains made the streams and ravines overflow, while drought reduced their flow to a trickle. Whether transport boats could pass depended upon the weather.
Recently, once the embankment at Huanglinggang in Henan was breached, the waters poured through the opening at Anpingzhen toward the eastern sea. Fortunately, the Yellow River has deep sources and a powerful current; even as it discharged into the sea, some of its flow remained. Thus, although transport boats still had to struggle to pass the opening, once they had moved upstream or downstream beyond it, they could proceed freely in the channel. It is this Yellow River that harms our grain transport, and it is also this Yellow River that benefits it. The assertion that work at the Anpingzhen opening cannot succeed unless Huanglinggang is closed is certainly sound. To abandon the Anpingzhen opening and advocate transport by sea is certainly an ill-considered plan. For this reason, over the past two or three years the matter has weighed heavily upon the emperor’s thoughts [?], and high ministers have repeatedly been dispatched. Now Huanglinggang is no longer subject to rushing breaches, and water no longer pours through the Anpingzhen opening. Is this not a great achievement? Yet I fear that after a drought the canal regulated by sluice gates will be even drier and shallower than before, and passage for transport boats even more difficult. That your discerning question addresses this may indeed be called foresight.
This student’s humble opinion is as follows: considering the situation before the two openings were closed, numerous overflow weirs should have been built along the embankments leading toward the sea in the area north of Anshan, to diminish the rushing…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
流平窪之地多作陂湖以收黃陵岡之餘
波如此則水勢既分其力自薄安平鎮口
之塞當不竢崇朝矣安平鎮既塞其口則
運船無虞黃陵岡既分其勢則漕河不竭
是黃河之水昔為我擾者今為我助此一
策也以兩口既塞之後論之天旱河乾理
勢或然又當於濟寧上下近河之所如南
旺湖積水澤鉅野澤悉皆去河咫尺且無
湖寬廣不啻百里若濬深其湖底高厚其
===
隄岸當河之面設閘開閉俾四時雨澤皆
瀦積其中湖水視河勢高八九餘尺隨旱
分數起板濟河又於各方泉眼悉加挑濬
數泉所會亦要鑿為一湖高厚啓閉悉如
前法舊湖被人侵種者改正之新湖該納
稅糧者除豁之勿顧一時小利而忘百世
大功此又塞口之後緊要一良策也若或
不此之務而徒區區於挑淺築壩封閘起
夫是為無策也愚敢以是為終篇對將以
punctuated:
流，平窪之地多作陂湖，以收黃陵岡之餘波。如此，則水勢既分，其力自薄，安平鎮口之塞當不竢崇朝矣。安平鎮既塞其口，則運船無虞；黃陵岡既分其勢，則漕河不竭。是黃河之水昔為我擾者，今為我助，此一策也。
以兩口既塞之後論之，天旱河乾，理勢或然。又當於濟寧上下近河之所，如南旺湖、積水澤、鉅野澤，悉皆去河咫尺，且無湖寬廣不啻百里。若濬深其湖底，高厚其隄岸，當河之面設閘開閉，俾四時雨澤皆瀦積其中，湖水視河勢高八九餘尺，隨旱分數起板濟河。又於各方泉眼悉加挑濬，數泉所會亦要鑿為一湖，高厚啓閉悉如前法。舊湖被人侵種者改正之，新湖該納稅糧者除豁之。勿顧一時小利而忘百世大功，此又塞口之後緊要一良策也。若或不此之務，而徒區區於挑淺、築壩、封閘、起夫，是為無策也。愚敢以是為終篇對，將以
translation_en:
…flow, and construct numerous reservoirs in low-lying areas to receive the surplus waters from Huanglinggang. In this way, once the force of the water is dispersed, its strength will naturally diminish, and closing the breach at Anpingzhen should not take even a morning. Once the breach at Anpingzhen is closed, transport vessels will be free from danger; once the force of the water at Huanglinggang is dispersed, the Grand Canal will not run dry. Thus the waters of the Yellow River, which formerly troubled us, will now assist us. This is one strategy.
As for the situation after both breaches have been closed, drought and a dry canal may well occur in the natural course of things. There are also places near the canal above and below Jining, such as Nanwang Lake, Jishui Marsh, and Juye Marsh, all within a very short distance of the canal; moreover, the lakes [?] extend over no fewer than a hundred li. If their beds were dredged deeper and their embankments raised and thickened, with sluice gates installed on the side facing the canal, rainfall throughout the four seasons could be stored within them. With the lake water standing eight or nine chi or more above the canal, the sluice boards could be raised according to the severity of drought to replenish the canal. Furthermore, springs in every locality should all be cleared and dredged. Wherever several springs converge, a lake should also be excavated; the height and thickness of its embankments and the opening and closing of its sluices should all follow the method described above. Encroachments by cultivators upon existing lakes should be rectified, and grain-tax liabilities on land used for new lakes should be remitted. Do not attend to the small gains of a moment and forget a great achievement that will benefit a hundred generations. This is another sound and urgently needed strategy for the period after the breaches have been closed. If, instead of attending to these matters, one merely busies oneself with dredging shoals, building dams, sealing sluices, and levying laborers, this amounts to having no strategy at all. I venture, in my humble judgment, to conclude my answer with these proposals, intending thereby to…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
為吾
聖天子
獻焉
punctuated: 為吾聖天子獻焉。
translation_en: …to present it to our sage Son of Heaven.

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
弘治乙卯秋山東循例舉士
士論定而小錄成澤竊序其
後曰昔人有言科目取士無
情如造化至公如權衡蓋以
防禁之嚴緘縢之密一付之
無心也以無心取士則取士
===
未有不得者而或又謂其徒
以言爾言果不足以取人乎
哉孟子以知言自負謂知其
言則知其心而因有以知其
政事且期以聖人復起不能
易所論其自信之審如此非
無見也近世有讀范仲淹金
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

弘治乙卯秋，山東循例舉士。士論定而小錄成，澤竊序其後曰：昔人有言：「科目取士，無情如造化，至公如權衡。」蓋以防禁之嚴、緘縢之密，一付之無心也。以無心取士，則取士未有不得者。而或又謂其徒以言爾。言果不足以取人乎哉？孟子以知言自負，謂知其言則知其心，而因有以知其政事，且期以聖人復起不能易所論。其自信之審如此，非無見也。近世有讀范仲淹金
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the yimao year of Hongzhi [1495], Shandong selected scholars according to established practice. Once the assessment of the candidates was settled and the brief record completed, I, Ze, ventured to append this postface:

Someone of old said: “Selecting scholars through the examinations is as dispassionate as the workings of creation and as utterly impartial as a balance.” This is because strict safeguards and prohibitions, together with securely sealed papers, entrust the entire process to impartial judgment. When scholars are selected impartially, the selection never fails to obtain suitable men. Yet some say that it relies on words alone. Can words really be insufficient for selecting men?

Mencius took pride in his ability to understand words. He held that understanding a man’s words meant understanding his mind, and thereby afforded a means of knowing his conduct in government. He even maintained that, were a sage to arise again, he could not alter these conclusions. Such was the firmness of his confidence; it was not without insight. In recent times, there have been those who, on reading Fan Zhongyan’s “Gold …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
在鎔賦則知其為文武全材
讀王孝先賦有物混成則知
其為宰相器讀蘇子瞻刑賞
忠厚之至論則知其為異人
因目之以國士讀文天祥廷
對策則知其忠肝如鐵石若
此者皆以言取也徵之他日
===
諸公名位之隆德業之盛文
章節義之高照耀人世果相
符而不相背孰謂言不足以
取人歟自有科目之法來豪
傑之士皆由此出歷千百年
而英君誼辟不能改其法非
不能改也誠令外此而求士
punctuated: 在鎔賦》，則知其為文武全材；讀王孝先賦《有物混成》，則知其為宰相器；讀蘇子瞻《刑賞忠厚之至論》，則知其為異人，因目之以國士；讀文天祥廷對策，則知其忠肝如鐵石。若此者，皆以言取也。徵之他日，諸公名位之隆、德業之盛、文章節義之高，照耀人世，果相符而不相背。孰謂言不足以取人歟？自有科目之法來，豪傑之士皆由此出。歷千百年，而英君誼辟不能改其法，非不能改也，誠令外此而求士
translation_en: …“Rhapsody on Gold in the Crucible,” one recognizes his complete talents in both civil and military affairs. Reading Wang Xiaoxian’s rhapsody “There Is Something Undifferentiated and Complete,” one recognizes his capacity to serve as chief councilor. Reading Su Zizhan’s “Discourse on the Utmost Loyalty and Generosity in Punishments and Rewards,” one recognizes an extraordinary man and accordingly regards him as an outstanding talent of the realm. Reading Wen Tianxiang’s policy response at court, one recognizes a loyalty as firm as iron and stone. All these judgments selected men on the basis of their words. Tested against their later lives, the eminence of these gentlemen’s reputations and positions, the abundance of their virtues and achievements, and the loftiness of their writings, integrity, and righteousness shone upon the world: they indeed confirmed those judgments rather than contradicted them. Who says that words are insufficient for selecting men? Ever since the examination system was established, men of outstanding ability have all emerged through it. Over hundreds and thousands of years, enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns have been unable to change this system. It is not that they lacked the power to change it; rather, if they were indeed to seek worthy men outside it…

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
則必至於紛紜不激於遠嫌
必昵於比周果能如造化如
權衡乎夫科目本不為取士
之病徒以操其柄者自病之
耳誣經說聖曲學阿世或至
於中選而平易說理立論正
大者或至於見黜此執是而
===
議者得以張其喙焉苟操其
柄者虛心果能如造化如權
衡則不得人不為憂矣我
國家養士於學校而以言取士
於科目歷百有二十餘年而
不變士之遭逢其盛其所以
感奮磨礪期以應
punctuated:
則必至於紛紜，不激於遠嫌，必昵於比周，果能如造化、如權衡乎？夫科目本不為取士之病，徒以操其柄者自病之耳。誣經說聖、曲學阿世，或至於中選；而平易說理、立論正大者，或至於見黜。此執是而議者得以張其喙焉。苟操其柄者虛心，果能如造化、如權衡，則不得人不為憂矣。
我國家養士於學校，而以言取士於科目，歷百有二十餘年而不變。士之遭逢其盛，其所以感奮磨礪，期以應
translation_en:
…then confusion would inevitably result: unless driven to extremes in avoiding suspicion of favoritism, one would inevitably become entangled in partisan collusion. Could such a method truly resemble the workings of nature or the impartial weighing of a balance? The examination system itself is no impediment to selecting worthy men; those who wield its authority merely make it so. Those who misrepresent the Classics and the teachings of the sages, twisting learning to curry favor with the world, may be selected, while those who explain principles plainly and advance upright and sound arguments may be rejected. This gives those who seize upon such cases to criticize the system an opportunity to open their mouths. If those who wield its authority set aside their preconceptions and can truly act like nature and the balance, there will be no need to worry about failing to obtain worthy men.
Our dynasty nurtures scholars in its schools and selects them through their written words in the examinations. This has remained unchanged for more than a hundred and twenty years. Scholars fortunate enough to encounter this flourishing age are thereby inspired to exert themselves and hone their abilities, hoping to answer …

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
上之求者固非徒能言而行不逮
者也況諸士生長鄒魯之邦
游歌大聖大賢之故鄉其風
聲氣習之所熏炙必將以聖
賢自期待言之所試實心之
所養焉浮艶不成令器如王
師旦之所論者若遠去矣澤
===
濫竊校文之柄自分不能窮
理不敢以知言僭擬至於所
取諸士得列名於是錄者則
敢以為范為王為蘇為文望
之也嗚呼諸士其肯負所望
以負
國家養士求士之盛心哉
punctuated:
上之求者，固非徒能言而行不逮者也。況諸士生長鄒魯之邦，游歌大聖大賢之故鄉，其風聲氣習之所熏炙，必將以聖賢自期待。言之所試，實心之所養焉。浮艶不成令器，如王師旦之所論者，若遠去矣。
澤濫竊校文之柄，自分不能窮理，不敢以知言僭擬。至於所取諸士得列名於是錄者，則敢以為范、為王、為蘇、為文望之也。嗚呼！諸士其肯負所望，以負國家養士求士之盛心哉？
translation_en:
…those who aspire to meet the throne’s expectations are certainly not merely men capable of fine words whose conduct falls short. Moreover, you scholars were born and raised in the lands of Zou and Lu, studying and singing in the native country of the great sages and worthies. Imbued with its traditions and habits, you will surely aspire to become sages and worthies yourselves. What is tested through your words is, in truth, what you have cultivated in your hearts. Those whose superficial brilliance makes them unfit to become men of worth, such as Wang Shidan discussed, seem far removed from you.
I, Ze, have undeservedly assumed authority over the assessment of examination writings. Knowing my own inability to fathom principle fully, I dare not presumptuously claim the capacity to discern men through their words. As for the scholars selected whose names appear in this record, however, I do venture to hope that they will become men like Fan, Wang, Su, and Wen. Ah! Would you scholars willingly disappoint these hopes, and thereby betray the state’s earnest intention in nurturing and seeking worthy scholars?

title: 弘治八年山東鄉試錄
text:
直隸滁州来安縣儒學教諭
張澤謹序
punctuated: 直隸滁州来安縣儒學教諭張澤謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully written by Zhang Ze, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lai’an County, Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region.
